translations.literal: Biographies, number thirty-three

sentences.zh: 裴叔業夏侯道遷李元護席法友王世弼江悅之淳于誕沈文秀張讜李苗劉藻傅永傅豎眼張烈李叔彪路恃慶房亮曹世表潘永基硃元旭

translations.literal: Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chunyu Dan, Shen Wenxiu, Zhang Dang, Li Miao, Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, Zhang Lie, Li Shubiao, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, Zhu Yuanxu
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye, Xiahou Daoqian, Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, Wang Shibi, Jiang Yuezhi, Chunyu Dan, Shen Wenxiu, Zhang Dang, Li Miao, Liu Zao, Fu Yong, Fu Shuyan, Zhang Lie, Li Shubiao, Lu Shiqing, Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, and Zhu Yuanxu

sentences.zh: 魏冀州刺史徽之後也。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Hui, Inspector of Ji Province under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from Hui, who had served Wei as Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 五世祖苞，晉秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Bao was Inspector of Qin Province under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Bao served Jin as Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 祖邕，自河東居於襄陽。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong moved from Hedong and settled at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong left Hedong and made his home at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 父順宗，兄叔寶，仕宋、齊，並有名位。

translations.literal: His father Shunzong and elder brother Shubao served Song and Qi, and both had notable rank and position.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shunzong and elder brother Shubao served under Song and Qi, both achieving recognized rank and standing.

sentences.zh: 叔業少有氣幹，頗以將略自許。

translations.literal: Shuye as a youth had spirit and capacity, and rather prided himself on military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuye had energy and ability, and he took considerable pride in his talents as a commander.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽末，曆官為羽林監、齊高帝驃騎行參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhui era of Song, he successively held office as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and Acting Staff Officer to Emperor Gao of Qi when he was General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Song's Yuanhui era he served successively as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest and as acting staff officer under the future Emperor Gao of Qi, then General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 齊受命，累遷為甯蠻長史、廣平太守。

translations.literal: After Qi received the mandate, he was repeatedly promoted, becoming Chief Clerk of Ningman and Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi took the throne, he rose through several posts to become Chief Clerk of Ningman and Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 叔業早與齊明帝同事。

translations.literal: Shuye had earlier served together with Emperor Ming of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye had previously served alongside Emperor Ming of Qi.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，以為心腹，使領軍奄襲諸蕃鎮，盡心用命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming assisted in government, he made Shuye a confidant and had him lead troops in sudden attacks on the various provincial garrisons; Shuye gave himself wholly to carrying out the commands.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Ming's regency, he treated Shuye as a trusted confidant and sent him to command surprise attacks on the provincial garrisons; Shuye carried out his orders with complete devotion.

sentences.zh: 及即位，以為給事黃門侍郎，封武昌縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he made him Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed him as Count of Wuchang County.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming came to the throne, he appointed Shuye Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and enfeoffed him as Count of Wuchang County.

sentences.zh: 孝文南次鐘離，拜叔業為徐州刺史，以水軍入淮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen halted south at Zhongli, he appointed Shuye Inspector of Xu Province and sent him into the Huai with naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen camped south at Zhongli, he made Shuye Inspector of Xu Province and ordered him to enter the Huai with a naval force.

sentences.zh: 帝令郎中裴聿往與之語，叔業盛飾左右服玩以誇之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Gentleman Pei Yu to go and speak with him; Shuye richly adorned his attendants, clothing, and ornaments in order to impress him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Gentleman Pei Yu to speak with him, and Shuye arrayed his attendants, garments, and finery in splendor to impress him.

sentences.zh: 聿曰：「伯父儀服誠為美麗，但恨不晝遊耳。」

translations.literal: Yu said, "Uncle, your ceremonial dress is indeed beautiful; I only regret that you are not parading by daylight."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Uncle, your robes and regalia are truly splendid; the only pity is that you are not showing them off in broad daylight."

sentences.zh: 齊帝崩，廢帝即位。

translations.literal: The Qi emperor died; the deposed emperor ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi emperor died, the deposed emperor came to the throne.

sentences.zh: 誅大臣，都下屢有變發。

translations.literal: He executed great ministers, and in the capital disturbances broke out repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: He put senior ministers to death, and uprisings kept breaking out in the capital.

sentences.zh: 叔業登壽春城，北望肥水，謂部下曰：「卿等欲富貴乎？

translations.literal: Shuye climbed the walls of Shouchun, looked north across the Fei River, and said to his subordinates, "Do you wish for wealth and rank?
translations.idiomatic: Shuye mounted the walls of Shouchun and gazed north across the Fei River. He said to his officers, "Do you want wealth and rank?

sentences.zh: 我言富貴亦可辦耳。」

translations.literal: If I speak of it, wealth and rank can also be arranged."
translations.idiomatic: If you follow my lead, wealth and rank are within reach."

sentences.zh: 未幾，見徙南袞州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be Governor of Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as Governor of Southern Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 會陳顯達圍建鄴，叔業遣司馬李元護應之，及顯達敗而還。

translations.literal: When Chen Xianda besieged Jianye, Shuye sent his Chief of Staff Li Yuanhu to answer the call; after Xianda was defeated he returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Xianda besieged Jianye, Shuye sent his chief of staff Li Yuanhu to his aid; Yuanhu returned once Xianda had been defeated.

sentences.zh: 叔業慮內難未已，不願為南兗州。

translations.literal: Shuye feared that internal troubles would not cease and did not wish to take Southern Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye feared the court turmoil would not end and was reluctant to accept the post in Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 齊廢主嬖臣茹法珍、王咺之等疑其有異，去來者並雲叔業北入。

translations.literal: The deposed Qi's favorite ministers Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuazhi, and others suspected he had ulterior designs; all who came and went reported that Shuye would go north.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed emperor's favorites Ru Fazhen and Wang Xuazhi suspected him of disloyalty, and everyone passing through said Shuye meant to defect to the north.

sentences.zh: 叔業兄子植、ＩＲ、瑜、粲等棄母奔壽陽。

translations.literal: Shuye's elder brother's sons Zhi, Yang, Yu, Can, and others abandoned their mother and fled to Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's nephews Zhi, Yang, Yu, Can, and others left their mother behind and fled to Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 法珍等以其既在疆場，且欲羈縻之，白齊主，遣中書舍人裴穆慰誘之，許不須回換。

translations.literal: Fazhen and the others, because he was already on the frontier and they also wished to keep him bound, reported to the Qi ruler and sent Palace Attendant Pei Mu to comfort and entice him, promising that he need not be rotated out.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuye already held the frontier and they wanted to keep him tied to them, Fazhen and his faction persuaded the Qi ruler to send Palace Attendant Pei Mu to reassure him and promise he would not be transferred away.

sentences.zh: 叔業雖得停，而憂懼不已。

translations.literal: Although Shuye was allowed to remain, his worry and fear did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye was allowed to stay in place, but his anxiety never lifted.

sentences.zh: 時梁武帝為雍州刺史，叔業遣親人馬文范以自安之計訪之梁武帝，曰：「雍州若能堅據襄陽，輒當戮力自保。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wu of Liang was Governor of Yong Province; Shuye sent his kinsman Ma Wenfan to consult him on a plan for his own security, saying, "If Yong Province can firmly hold Xiangyang, I shall join forces to protect ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang was then Governor of Yong Province. Shuye sent his kinsman Ma Wenfan to ask his advice, saying, "If you can hold Xiangyang firmly, I will join you in defending ourselves.

sentences.zh: 若不爾，回面向北，不失河南公。」

translations.literal: If not, by turning to face the north one would not lose the title Duke of Henan."
translations.idiomatic: If not, by turning north I can still become Duke of Henan."

sentences.zh: 梁武報曰：「唯應送家還都以安慰之，自然無患。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang replied, "You should only send your family back to the capital to reassure them, and naturally there will be no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu replied, "Send your family back to the capital to reassure the court, and you will have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 若意外相逼，當勒馬二萬人，直出橫江，以斷其後，則天下事一舉可定。

translations.literal: If they unexpectedly press you, I shall muster twenty thousand horsemen, go straight out through Hengjiang, and cut off their rear; then the affairs of the realm can be settled in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: If they force your hand, I will raise twenty thousand horsemen, strike out through Hengjiang, and cut their retreat; the empire can then be settled at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 若欲北向，彼必遣人相代，以河北一地相處，河南公寧復可得？

translations.literal: If you wish to turn north, they will surely send someone to replace you and give you some place north of the river; how could you still obtain the title Duke of Henan?
translations.idiomatic: If you turn north, they will send someone to replace you and park you on some patch north of the river. Do you really think you would still be made Duke of Henan?

sentences.zh: 如此，則南歸望絕矣。」

translations.literal: In that case, hope of returning south would be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: That way you would lose any chance of ever returning south."

sentences.zh: 叔業沉疑未決，遣信詣豫州刺史薛真度，訪入北之宜。

translations.literal: Shuye hesitated and could not decide; he sent a messenger to Governor of Yu Province Xue Zhendu to inquire whether going north was advisable.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye remained undecided. He sent a messenger to Xue Zhendu, Governor of Yu Province, to ask whether defecting north was wise.

sentences.zh: 真度答書，盛陳朝廷風化。

translations.literal: Zhendu replied in a letter, lavishly setting forth the court's civilizing influence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu wrote back at length praising the northern court's civilized rule.

sentences.zh: 叔業乃遣子芬之及兄女夫韋伯昕奉表內附。

translations.literal: Shuye thereupon sent his son Fenzhi and his elder brother's son-in-law Wei Boxin to present a memorial submitting to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye then sent his son Fenzhi and his brother's son-in-law Wei Boxin with a memorial offering submission to the north.

sentences.zh: 景明元年正月，宣武詔授叔業持節、散騎常侍、都督、豫州刺史、征南將軍，封蘭陵郡公。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Jingming, Emperor Xuanwu issued an edict appointing Shuye Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Yu Province, and General Who Conquers the South, enfeoffing him as Duke of Lanling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jingming year 1, Emperor Xuanwu appointed Shuye Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, regional commander, Governor of Yu Province, and General Who Conquers the South, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 又賜叔業璽書，遣彭城王勰、尚書令王肅赴接。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Shuye an imperial letter under seal and sent Prince of Pengcheng Xie and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Su to go and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Shuye an imperial letter under seal and dispatched Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Su to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 軍未度淮，叔業病卒，李元護、席法友等推叔業兄子植監州事。

translations.literal: Before the army had crossed the Huai, Shuye died of illness; Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, and others installed Shuye's elder brother's son Zhi to oversee provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army crossed the Huai, Shuye died of illness. Li Yuanhu, Xi Fayou, and others put his nephew Zhi in charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 詔贈叔業驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，諡忠武公，給東園溫明秘器。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Shuye the title Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with posthumous name Loyal Martial Duke, and granted the secret funerary objects of the Eastern Garden and the Warm Bright coffin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand General of Agile Cavalry with Grand Master privileges, gave him the posthumous name Loyal Martial Duke, and granted the imperial funerary regalia.

sentences.zh: 子蒨之，字文德，仕齊，隨郡王左常侍，先卒。

translations.literal: His son Qianzhi, style Wende, served Qi as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Suixian and died first.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianzhi, courtesy name Wende, served Qi as Left Regular Attendant to the Prince of Suixian and died before his father.

sentences.zh: 子譚紹封。

translations.literal: His son Tan inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 譚粗險好殺，所乘牛馬為小驚逸，手自殺之。

translations.literal: Tan was coarse, dangerous, and fond of killing; if the ox or horse he rode was slightly startled and bolted, he killed it with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was brutal and bloodthirsty; if a mount he rode was even slightly startled and bolted, he killed it himself.

sentences.zh: 然孝事諸叔，盡于子道，國祿歲入，每以分贍，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he was filial toward his uncles and fulfilled the way of a son; each year he divided his state stipend to support them, and the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he treated his uncles with filial devotion and shared his stipend with them each year, for which contemporaries praised him.

sentences.zh: 位輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of General Who Assists the State and Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Assists the State and Palace Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南豫州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Southern Yu Province, with posthumous name Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Southern Yu Province, with the posthumous name Respectful.

sentences.zh: 子測，字伯源，襲。

translations.literal: His son Ce, style Boyuan, inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ce, courtesy name Boyuan, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 曆通直散騎侍郎，天平中，走於關中。

translations.literal: He served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry in Direct Service; in the Tianping era he fled to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry in Direct Service and fled to Guanzhong during the Tianping era.

sentences.zh: 蒨之弟芬之，字文馥，長者好施，篤愛諸弟。

translations.literal: Qianzhi's younger brother Fenzhi, style Wenfu, was a man of mature character who loved to give and was deeply affectionate toward his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi's younger brother Fenzhi, courtesy name Wenfu, was generous and deeply devoted to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位羽林監。

translations.literal: He served Qi and reached the post of Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.
translations.idiomatic: He served Qi as Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers.

sentences.zh: 入魏，以父勳封上蔡伯。

translations.literal: Entering Wei, because of his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shangcai.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Wei he was enfeoffed as Earl of Shangcai in recognition of his father's service.

sentences.zh: 為東秦州刺史，在州有清靜稱。

translations.literal: He was Governor of Eastern Qin Province and in his province won repute for purity and tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Eastern Qin Province he earned a reputation for clean and orderly rule.

sentences.zh: 後徙封山茌縣，遷岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later his fief was moved to Shanzhi County and he was transferred to be Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later his fief was moved to Shanzhi County and he was appointed Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 為隴賊所圍，城陷，賊以送上邽，為莫折念生所害，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was besieged by Longyou bandits; the city fell and the bandits sent him up to Shanggui, where he was killed by Mo Zhe Niansheng; he was posthumously made Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Longyou rebels besieged him; when the city fell they sent him to Shanggui, where Mo Zhe Niansheng had him killed. He was posthumously made Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 芬之弟藹之，字幼重，性輕率，好琴書。

translations.literal: Fenzhi's younger brother Aizhi, style Youzhong, was by nature light and rash and loved the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: Fenzhi's younger brother Aizhi, courtesy name Youzhong, was impulsive by nature and loved music and books.

sentences.zh: 其內弟柳諧善鼓琴，藹之師而微不及也。

translations.literal: His wife's younger brother Liu Xie was skilled at playing the zither; Aizhi took him as teacher but fell slightly short.
translations.idiomatic: His brother-in-law Liu Xie was an excellent zither player; Aizhi studied under him but never quite matched him.

sentences.zh: 位汝陽太守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Administrator of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became Administrator of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 叔業長兄子彥先，少有志尚。

translations.literal: Shuye's elder brother's son Yanxian from youth had lofty aims.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's nephew Yanxian had shown ambition from youth.

sentences.zh: 叔業以壽春入魏，彥先封雍丘縣子，位勃海相。

translations.literal: When Shuye brought Shouchun into Wei, Yanxian was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongqiu County and reached the post of Chancellor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye surrendered Shouchun to Wei, Yanxian was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongqiu and appointed Chancellor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰惠恭。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous name was Kind and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he received the posthumous name Kind and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 彥先子約，字元儉，性頗剛鯁，後襲爵。

translations.literal: Yanxian's son Yue, style Yuanjian, was by nature rather stubborn and upright; later he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxian's son Yue, courtesy name Yuanjian, was stubborn and upright by nature and later inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 冀州大乘賊起，敕為別將，行勃海郡事，城陷見害。

translations.literal: When the Dasheng bandits rose in Ji Province, he was ordered to serve as Separate Commander and act in the affairs of Bohai Commandery; the city fell and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dasheng rebels rose in Ji Province, he was appointed Separate Commander and put in charge of Bohai; the city fell and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 長子英起，武定末洛州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yingqi, at the end of Wuding, was Governor of Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yingqi became Governor of Luo Province late in the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 英起弟威起，卒于齊王府中兵參軍，贈鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: Yingqi's younger brother Weiqi died as Army Controller in the Prince of Qi's household and was posthumously made Junior Director of the Court for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: Yingqi's younger brother Weiqi died as Army Controller in the Prince of Qi's household and was posthumously made Junior Director of the Court for Dependencies.

sentences.zh: 彥先弟絢，揚州中從事。

translations.literal: Yanxian's younger brother Xuan was Middle Attendant of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxian's younger brother Xuan served as Middle Attendant of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時揚州霖雨，水入城，刺史李崇居城上，系船憑焉。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Province had continuous rain; water entered the city, and Governor Li Chong lived atop the city wall, mooring his boat and relying on it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province was then deluged by rain; floodwater entered the city, and Governor Li Chong took refuge on the wall with his boat moored beside him.

sentences.zh: 絢率城南人數千家汎舟南走高原。

translations.literal: Xuan led several thousand households south of the city to take boats and flee south to the highlands.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan led several thousand households from the south of the city in boats southward to the high ground.

sentences.zh: 謂崇還北，遂與別駕鄭祖起等送子十四人于梁。

translations.literal: He said Chong would return north, and thereupon with Vice Administrator Zheng Zuqi and others sent fourteen sons to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Chong would retreat north, he and Vice Administrator Zheng Zuqi and others sent fourteen sons as hostages to Liang.

sentences.zh: 崇勒水軍討之，眾潰見獲，投水而死。

translations.literal: Chong mustered the water army to attack him; the crowd was routed and he was captured, then threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Chong led the river fleet against him; Xuan's force was routed and he was taken, then drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 植字文遠，叔業兄叔寶子也。

translations.literal: Zhi, style Wenyuan, was the son of Shuye's elder brother Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, courtesy name Wenyuan, was the son of Shuye's elder brother Shubao.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，覽綜經史，尤長釋典，善談理義。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, surveyed the classics and histories comprehensively, was especially accomplished in Buddhist scriptures, and was skilled at discussing principles.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning, read widely in the classics and histories, excelled in Buddhist texts, and was skilled in doctrinal debate.

sentences.zh: 隨叔業在壽春。

translations.literal: He followed Shuye at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shuye at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 叔業卒，席法友、柳玄達等共舉植監州。

translations.literal: When Shuye died, Xi Fayou, Liu Xuanda, and others jointly raised Zhi to oversee the province.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuye died, Xi Fayou, Liu Xuanda, and others jointly put Zhi in charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 秘叔業喪問，教命處分，皆出於植。

translations.literal: He concealed news of Shuye's death; all orders and dispositions issued from Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Shuye's death secret, and all orders and arrangements came from Zhi himself.

sentences.zh: 於是開門納魏軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the gates and admitted the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened the gates and admitted the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 詔以植為袞州刺史、崇義縣侯，入為大鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: An edict made Zhi Governor of Yan Province and Marquis of Chongyi County; he entered court as Grand Master for Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Governor of Yan Province and Marquis of Chongyi, then brought him to court as Grand Master for Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 後以長子昕南叛，有司處之大辟，詔特恕其罪，以表勳誠。

translations.literal: Later, because his eldest son Xin defected south, the authorities sentenced him to death; an edict specially pardoned his crime to show regard for his merit and loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when his eldest son Xin defected to the south, the authorities sentenced him to death, but an edict specially pardoned him in recognition of the family's service.

sentences.zh: 尋除授揚州大中正，出為瀛州刺史，再遷度支尚書，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, went out as Governor of Ying Province, was transferred again to Minister of Revenue, and was given the additional title Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, then Governor of Ying Province, then Minister of Revenue with the additional rank of Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 植性非柱石，所為無恆。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was not that of a pillar; what he did had no constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was no pillar of stability and acted without constancy.

sentences.zh: 袞州之還也，表請解官，隱于嵩山，宣武不許，深以為怪。

translations.literal: On returning from Yan Province he memorialized requesting to resign office and retire on Mount Song; Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it and was deeply puzzled.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Yan Province he asked to resign and retire to Mount Song; Emperor Xuanwu refused and was deeply puzzled.

sentences.zh: 然公私集論，自言人門不後王肅，怪朝廷處之不高。

translations.literal: Yet in public and private gatherings he said that his family standing was not behind Wang Su's and found it strange that the court did not place him higher.
translations.idiomatic: In public and private he claimed his family was no lesser than Wang Su's and complained that the court had not promoted him high enough.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書，志意頗滿，欲以政事為己任，謂人曰：「非我須尚書，尚書亦須我。」

translations.literal: When he became Minister, his ambition was quite satisfied; he wished to take government affairs as his own charge and said to people, "It is not that the Ministry needs me; the Ministry also needs me."
translations.idiomatic: Once he became Minister of Revenue he was quite pleased with himself and wanted to run affairs in his own way. He told people, "It is not that the ministry needs me—the ministry needs me."

sentences.zh: 辭氣激揚，見於言色。

translations.literal: His words and tone were impassioned and showed in his speech and expression.
translations.idiomatic: His tone was heated, and it showed in his face and voice.

sentences.zh: 及入參議論，時對眾官，面有譏毀。

translations.literal: When he entered to join in deliberation, he would at times answer the assembled officials to their faces with ridicule and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: In council he would openly mock and insult other officials to their faces.

sentences.zh: 又表毀征南將軍田益宗，言華夷異類，不應在百世衣冠之上。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to defame General Who Conquers the South Tian Yizong, saying that Chinese and barbarian were different kinds and should not stand above families of long pedigree.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted a memorial attacking General Who Conquers the South Tian Yizong, claiming that as a man of mixed Chinese and barbarian origin he should not rank above old aristocratic families.

sentences.zh: 率多侵侮，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Most of his conduct was invasive and insulting, all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his conduct was arrogant and insulting in this vein.

sentences.zh: 侍中于忠、黃門元昭覽之切齒，寢而不奏。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Zhong and Yellow Gate Yuan Zhao, on reading it, ground their teeth and laid it aside without presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Ordinary Yu Zhong and Yellow Gate Yuan Zhao read it with clenched teeth and suppressed it without forwarding it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 韋伯昕告植欲謀廢黜。

translations.literal: Wei Boxin reported that Zhi wished to plot deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boxin accused Zhi of plotting to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 尚書又奏，羊祉告植姑子皇甫仲達，雲受植旨，遂詐稱被詔，率合部曲，欲圖領軍於忠。

translations.literal: The Ministry again memorialized: Yang Zhi reported that Zhi's wife's sister's son Huangfu Zhongda, saying he received Zhi's order, then falsely claimed to have received an edict, mustered his followers, and wished to plot against Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry also reported that Yang Zhi had accused Zhi's nephew by marriage Huangfu Zhongda of acting on Zhi's orders, falsely claiming an imperial edict, gathering his followers, and plotting against Commander-in-Chief Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 時忠專權，既構成其禍，又矯詔殺之，朝野稱冤。

translations.literal: At that time Zhong monopolized power; having framed this disaster for him, he also forged an edict and killed him; court and countryside called it injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then held sole power; having framed Zhi, he forged an edict and had him executed, and the court and the people called it a gross injustice.

sentences.zh: 臨終，神志自若，遺令子弟，命盡之後，剪落鬚髮，被以法服，以沙門禮葬于嵩高之陰。

translations.literal: At the end his spirit was calm as ever; he left instructions to his sons and younger brothers that after his death they should cut off his beard and hair, clothe him in monastic robes, and bury him by monastic rites on the northern slope of lofty Song.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he remained composed. He instructed his sons that after his death they should shave his head and beard, dress him in monastic robes, and bury him on the northern slope of Mount Song according to Buddhist rites.

sentences.zh: 初，植與僕射郭祚、都水使者韋俊等同時見害。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhi, with Vice Director Guo Zuo, Commissioner of Waterways Wei Jun, and others, was killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had been killed at the same time as Vice Director Guo Zuo and Commissioner of Waterways Wei Jun.

sentences.zh: 後祚、俊事雪加贈，而植追復封爵而已。

translations.literal: Later Zuo's and Jun's cases were cleared and they received posthumous honors, whereas for Zhi only his fief was restored posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Zuo and Wei Jun were cleared and given posthumous honors, while Zhi received only restoration of his title.

sentences.zh: 植故吏勃海刁沖上疏訟之，於是贈尚書僕射、揚州刺史，乃改葬。

translations.literal: Zhi's former subordinate Diao Chong of Bohai submitted a memorial to plead his case; thereupon he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Governor of Yang Province, and only then was he reburied.
translations.idiomatic: His former subordinate Diao Chong of Bohai submitted a memorial on his behalf; Zhi was then posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Governor of Yang Province, and was reburied.

sentences.zh: 植母，夏侯道遷姊也。

translations.literal: Zhi's mother was the elder sister of Xiahou Daoqian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's mother was the elder sister of Xiahou Daoqian.

sentences.zh: 性甚剛峻，于諸子皆如嚴君。

translations.literal: Her nature was very stern and severe; toward all her sons she was like a strict father.
translations.idiomatic: She was stern by nature and treated all her sons like a strict father would.

sentences.zh: 長成後，非衣幍不見，小有罪過，必束帶伏門，經五三日乃引見之，督以嚴訓。

translations.literal: After they grew up she would not see them unless they wore caps and robes; for small faults she made them bind their sashes and kneel at the door, and only after five or three days would she summon them in, supervising them with strict instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were grown she would see them only when properly dressed; for minor faults she made them kneel bound at the door for three to five days before receiving them again and lecturing them sternly.

sentences.zh: 唯少子衍得以常服見之，旦夕溫凊。

translations.literal: Only the youngest son Yan was allowed to see her in ordinary dress, morning and evening asking after her warmth and cool.
translations.idiomatic: Only her youngest son Yan was allowed to visit her in everyday clothes and attend her morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 植在瀛州也，其母年逾七十，以身為婢，自施三寶，布衣麻菲，手執箕帚於沙門寺掃灑。

translations.literal: While Zhi was in Ying Province, his mother passed seventy; she made herself a maidservant, offered herself to the Three Jewels, wore plain cloth and hemp sandals, and with broom and dustpan in hand swept at a Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhi was in Ying Province, his mother, past seventy, made herself a temple servant, devoted herself to the Three Jewels, dressed in plain hemp, and swept the floors of a Buddhist monastery with broom in hand.

sentences.zh: 植弟瑜、粲、衍並亦奴僕之服，泣涕而從，有感道俗。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brothers Yu, Can, and Yan also wore servants' dress, followed weeping, and moved clergy and laity alike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's brothers Yu, Can, and Yan also dressed as servants and followed her weeping, moving monks and laypeople alike.

sentences.zh: 諸子各以布帛數百贖免其母，於是出家為比丘。

translations.literal: The sons each used several hundred bolts of cloth to ransom and free their mother; thereupon she left home and became a bhikṣu.
translations.idiomatic: The sons each paid several hundred bolts of cloth to ransom her from service, after which she took monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 入嵩高積歲，乃還家。

translations.literal: She entered lofty Song for accumulated years, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: She spent years on Mount Song before returning home.

sentences.zh: 植既長嫡，母又年老，其在州數歲，以妻子自隨。

translations.literal: Since Zhi was the eldest legitimate son and his mother was also old, during his several years in the province he took wife and children with him.
translations.idiomatic: As the eldest son and with an aged mother, he took his wife and children with him during his years in the province.

sentences.zh: 雖自州送祿奉母及贍諸弟，而各別資財，同居異爨，一門數灶，蓋亦染江南之俗也。

translations.literal: Although from the province he sent his stipend to support his mother and provide for his younger brothers, each kept separate property; they lived together but cooked separately, with several stoves in one household—probably also infected by Jiangnan custom.
translations.idiomatic: Although he sent his stipend from the province to support his mother and brothers, each kept separate property; they lived under one roof but cooked separately, with several kitchens in the household—a Jiangnan custom, critics said.

sentences.zh: 論者譏焉。

translations.literal: Critics ridiculed this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators ridiculed them for it.

sentences.zh: 植弟颺，壯果有謀略。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Yang was strong, resolute, and possessed stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Yang was bold, resolute, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 在齊，以軍功位驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: In Qi, through military merit he reached the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he rose through military merit to General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 入魏，為南司州刺史，封義陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Entering Wei, he became Governor of Southern Si Province and was enfeoffed as Earl of Yiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Wei he became Governor of Southern Si Province and was enfeoffed as Earl of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 詔命未至，為賊所殺，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: Before the edict of appointment arrived, he was killed by bandits; his rank was advanced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Before his appointment edict arrived he was killed by bandits; his rank was posthumously raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 宣武以颺勳效未立而卒，其子烱不得襲封。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu, because Yang's merit and achievement had not been established before he died, did not allow his son Jiong to inherit the fief.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang had died before his merit was fully established, Emperor Xuanwu would not let his son Jiong inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，烱行貨于執事，乃封城平縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, Jiong offered bribes to those in power and was then enfeoffed as Earl of Chengping County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ming's reign Jiong bribed those in power and was enfeoffed as Earl of Chengping.

sentences.zh: 烱字休光，小字黃頭，頗有文學，善事權門。

translations.literal: Jiong, style Xiuguang, childhood name Yellow Head, had considerable literary accomplishment and was skilled at serving powerful families.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong, courtesy name Xiuguang, childhood name Yellow Head, was literarily accomplished and adept at courting the powerful.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉納其金帛，除鎮遠將軍、散騎常侍、揚州大中正，進爵為侯，改封高城。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha accepted his gold and silks, appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, advanced his rank to marquis, and changed his fief to Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha accepted his gifts of gold and silk and appointed him General Who Pacifies the Distance, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and Chief Rectifier of Yang Province, raised him to marquis, and moved his fief to Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書右丞，出為東郡太守，為城人所害。

translations.literal: Soon he also held the post of Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he went out as Governor of Dong Commandery and was killed by men of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also appointed Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then sent out as Governor of Dong Commandery, where he was killed by insurgents within the city.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、青州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Qing Province; his posthumous name was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Qing Province, with the posthumous epithet Jian (Concise).

sentences.zh: 颺弟瑜，字文琬，封下密縣子，試守滎陽郡，坐虐暴殺人免官。

translations.literal: Yang's younger brother Yu, style Wenwan, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiami County, acted as Administrator of Xingyang Commandery on probation, and was dismissed from office for cruel and violent killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Wenwan, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiami County and served as acting Administrator of Xingyang Commandery until he was removed from office for brutal murders.

sentences.zh: 後徙封灌津子，卒于勃海太守，贈豫州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: Later his fief was moved to Viscount of Guanjin; he died as Governor of Bohai, was granted posthumously Governor of Yu Province, and his posthumous name was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Later his title was changed to Viscount of Guanjin. He died while serving as Governor of Bohai and was posthumously named Governor of Yu Province, with the posthumous epithet Ding (Settled).

sentences.zh: 瑜弟粲，字文亮，封舒縣子。

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Can, style Wenliang, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shu County.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Can, courtesy name Wenliang, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shu County.

sentences.zh: 沉重善風儀，頗以驕豪為失。

translations.literal: He was grave and dignified and skilled in bearing and deportment, yet took pride and arrogance as faults.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave and dignified, with excellent bearing and manners, though his pride and arrogance were widely regarded as failings.

sentences.zh: 曆正平、恆農二郡太守。

translations.literal: He successively served as Administrator of the two commanderies Zhengping and Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Administrator of Zhengping and Hengnong commanderies.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍曾以事屬粲，粲不從，雍甚為恨。

translations.literal: Prince Yong of Gaoyang once entrusted a matter to Can, but Can would not comply, and Yong harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong of Gaoyang once asked Can to handle a matter on his behalf, but Can refused, and Yong took a deep dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 後因九日馬射，敕畿內太守皆赴京師，雍時為州牧，粲修謁，雍含怒待之。

translations.literal: Later, on the Double Ninth archery on horseback, an edict ordered all administrators within the capital region to come to the capital; Yong was then Regional Inspector, Can paid a formal visit, and Yong received him with contained anger.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the Double Ninth Festival horse-archery event, an edict summoned all administrators of the capital region to the capital. Yong was then Regional Inspector; when Can came to pay his respects, Yong received him with barely concealed anger.

sentences.zh: 粲神情閑邁，舉止抑揚，雍目而不覺解顏。

translations.literal: Can's expression was easy and lofty, his movements measured and expressive; Yong watched him and unawares relaxed his face into a smile.
translations.idiomatic: Can's bearing was serene and lofty, his gestures poised and expressive. Yong watched him and, without realizing it, broke into a smile.

sentences.zh: 及坐定，謂粲曰：「可更為一行。」

translations.literal: When they had taken their seats, he said to Can: "You may offer another round."
translations.idiomatic: Once they were seated, he said to Can, "Give us another round."

sentences.zh: 粲便下席為行，從容而出。

translations.literal: Can then left his seat to perform the round and withdrew at his ease.
translations.idiomatic: Can left his seat to perform the toast and withdrew with unhurried grace.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: Because of the affair he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office over the incident.

sentences.zh: 後宣武聞粲善自標置，欲觀其風度，令傳詔就家急召之，須臾間，使者相屬，闔家恇懼，不測所以，粲更恬然，神色不變。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xuanwu heard that Can was skilled at self-presentation and wished to observe his bearing; he ordered an urgent summons to his home by imperial message. Within moments messengers followed one another; the whole household was terrified, not knowing the reason, yet Can grew only more calm, his expression unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xuanwu heard that Can had a gift for self-presentation and wished to see his bearing for himself, so he ordered an urgent summons to Can's home. Within moments messengers arrived one after another. The entire household was terrified, unable to guess the reason, but Can grew only calmer, his expression unchanged.

sentences.zh: 帝歎異之。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in wonder at him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 時僕射高肇以外戚之貴，勢傾一時，朝士見者，咸望塵拜謁。

translations.literal: At that time the Deputy Director Gao Zhao, by the eminence of his maternal kin connection, tilted power for a season; court officials who saw him all bowed in obeisance at the dust of his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Deputy Director Gao Zhao, elevated by his ties to the imperial consort clan, dominated the court. Officials who encountered him would bow from afar before the dust of his carriage even settled.

sentences.zh: 粲候肇，唯長揖而已。

translations.literal: When Can waited upon Zhao, he gave only a long bow with folded hands.
translations.idiomatic: When Can called on Zhao, he offered only a formal bow with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 及還，家人尤責之，粲曰：「何可自同凡俗也。」

translations.literal: On returning, his family reproached him all the more; Can said: "How could one make oneself the same as the common crowd?"
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home, his family reproached him sharply. Can said, "How could I make myself common like everyone else?"

sentences.zh: 又曾詣清河王懌，下車始進，便屬暴雨，粲容步舒雅，不以霑、濡改節。

translations.literal: He had also once called on Prince Yi of Qinghe; he had just alighted and begun to enter when a violent rainstorm struck. Can's bearing and pace remained easy and elegant; he did not alter his composure because of being wet or soaked.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he called on Prince Yi of Qinghe. He had just stepped down from his carriage and begun to enter when a violent rainstorm broke. Can kept his pace serene and elegant, unaltered by being drenched and soaked through.

sentences.zh: 懌乃令人持蓋覆之，歎謂左右曰：「何代無奇人！」

translations.literal: Yi then had someone hold an umbrella over him and sighed to those beside him: "What age has lacked extraordinary men!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi then had someone hold an umbrella over him and sighed to his attendants, "In what age are there not extraordinary men!"

sentences.zh: 性好釋學，親升講座，雖持義未精，而風韻可重。

translations.literal: His nature favored Buddhist learning; he personally ascended the lecture seat. Though his grasp of doctrine was not refined, his bearing and tone were worthy of respect.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to Buddhist learning and would himself mount the lecture seat. Though his command of doctrine was not deep, his presence and manner commanded respect.

sentences.zh: 但不涉經史，終為知音所輕。

translations.literal: Yet because he did not engage with the classics and histories, in the end connoisseurs looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: But because he did not engage with the classics and histories, men of discernment ultimately held him in less esteem.

sentences.zh: 後為揚州大中正、中書令。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Rectifier of Yang Province and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Chief Rectifier of Yang Province and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明帝釋奠，以為侍講，轉金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming performed the libation sacrifice, Can was made Lecturer-in-Attendance and was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming performed the ceremonial libation at the imperial academy, Can was appointed Lecturer-in-Attendance and later promoted to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，以粲為西袞州刺史，尋為濮陽太守崔巨倫所逐，棄州入嵩高山。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Can was made Governor of Western Yan Province; soon he was driven out by Cui Julun, Administrator of Puyang, abandoned the province, and entered Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Can was appointed Governor of Western Yan Province, but soon Cui Julun, Administrator of Puyang, drove him out. He abandoned the province and withdrew into Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，復為中書令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin's reign he again became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Jiemin's reign he was again appointed Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後正月晦，帝出臨洛濱，粲起御前，再拜上壽酒。

translations.literal: Later, on the last day of the first month, the emperor went out to the banks of the Luo; Can rose before the imperial seat, bowed twice, and presented wine for longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the last day of the first month, the emperor went out to the banks of the Luo River. Can rose before the imperial seat, bowed twice, and presented a cup of longevity wine.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「昔北海入朝，暫竊神器，爾日卿戒之以酒；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the past when Beihai entered the court he briefly usurped the imperial regalia; on that day you admonished him with wine;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Beihai came to court in the past, he briefly seized the imperial regalia. On that day you admonished him with wine.

sentences.zh: 今欲我飲，何異於往情？」

translations.literal: now you wish me to drink—how is this different from the former sentiment?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you want me to drink. How is that different from before?"

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「北海志在沈湎，故諫其所失，陛下齊聖溫克，臣敢獻微誠。」

translations.literal: Can said: "Beihai's intent lay in drowning himself in drink, so I admonished him for his fault. Your Majesty is equal to the sage, gentle and restrained—I dare offer a small sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Can replied, "Beihai was intent on drowning himself in wine, so I admonished him for his excess. Your Majesty is sage-like, gentle and self-restrained—I dare offer this small token of loyalty."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「甚愧來譽。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am deeply ashamed at such praise coming to me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am deeply embarrassed by such praise."

sentences.zh: 仍為命酌。

translations.literal: He then ordered wine to be poured.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered wine to be served.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，出為驃騎大將軍、膠州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he went out as General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was sent out as General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 屬時亢旱，土人勸令禱於海神。

translations.literal: As the time suffered severe drought, the local people urged that he pray to the Sea God.
translations.idiomatic: A severe drought struck the region, and the local people urged him to pray to the Sea God.

sentences.zh: 粲憚違眾人，乃為祈請，直據胡床，舉杯曰：「僕白君。」

translations.literal: Can feared to defy the multitude, so he performed the prayer, sat straight on a folding camp chair, raised his cup, and said: "Your servant speaks to you, lord."
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to defy public opinion, he performed the prayer, sat upright on a folding camp chair, raised his cup, and said, "Your servant speaks to you, lord."

sentences.zh: 左右云：「前後例皆拜謁。」

translations.literal: Those beside him said: "In precedent before and after, all have bowed in obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: His attendants said, "By precedent everyone has always bowed in obeisance."

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「五嶽視三公，四瀆視諸侯，安有方伯致禮海神。」

translations.literal: Can said: "The Five Marchmounts are regarded as equal to the Three Dukes, the Four Watercourses as equal to the feudal lords—how could a regional governor perform obeisance to the Sea God?"
translations.idiomatic: Can said, "The Five Marchmounts are treated as the equals of the Three Dukes, and the Four Watercourses as the equals of feudal lords. How could a regional governor bow to the Sea God?"

sentences.zh: 卒不肯拜。

translations.literal: In the end he would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 時青州叛賊耿翔寇亂三齊，粲唯高譚虛論，不事防禦之術。

translations.literal: At that time the Qing Province rebel Geng Xiang raided and threw the Three Qi into disorder; Can only engaged in lofty talk and empty discourse and did not attend to methods of defense.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qing Province rebel Geng Xiang was ravaging the Three Qi region, while Can indulged only in lofty talk and empty theorizing, neglecting all measures of defense.

sentences.zh: 翔乘其無備，掩襲州城。

translations.literal: Xiang seized his lack of preparation and made a surprise assault on the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang took advantage of his unpreparedness and launched a surprise attack on the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 左右白言賊至，粲云：「豈有此理！」

translations.literal: Those beside him reported that bandits had arrived; Can said: "How could there be such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants reported that rebels had arrived. Can said, "That cannot be!"

sentences.zh: 左右又言「已入州門！」

translations.literal: Those beside him again said: "They have already entered the provincial gate!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants again cried, "They have already entered the provincial gate!"

sentences.zh: 粲乃徐云：「耿王可引上聽事，自餘部眾，且付城人。」

translations.literal: Can then said slowly: "Prince Geng may be led up to the reception hall; as for the rest of the troops, for now hand them over to the men of the city."
translations.idiomatic: Can then said calmly, "Prince Geng may be shown to the reception hall. As for the rest of his troops, leave them to the city garrison for now."

sentences.zh: 不達時變如此。

translations.literal: His failure to grasp the changes of the times was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his failure to grasp the realities of the moment.

sentences.zh: 尋為翔害，送首于梁。

translations.literal: Soon he was killed by Xiang; his head was sent to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was killed by Xiang, and his head was sent to the Liang court.

sentences.zh: 子含，字文若，員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Han, style Wenruo, was an External Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han, courtesy name Wenruo, served as External Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 粲弟衍，字文舒，學識優於諸兄，才亦過之。

translations.literal: Can's younger brother Yan, style Wenshu, in learning and knowledge surpassed his elder brothers, and in talent also exceeded them.
translations.idiomatic: Can's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Wenshu, surpassed his elder brothers in learning and knowledge, and in talent as well.

sentences.zh: 事親以孝聞，兼有將略。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his parents and also possessed military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for filial devotion to his parents and also possessed military talent.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位陰平太守。

translations.literal: He served Qi and held the post of Administrator of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Qi as Administrator of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 歸魏，授通直郎，衍堅辭朝命，上表請隱嵩高。

translations.literal: On returning to Wei he was granted the post of Palace Attendant of Direct Communication; Yan firmly declined the court's appointment and submitted a memorial requesting to live in seclusion on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: After defecting to Wei he was appointed Palace Attendant of Direct Communication, but Yan firmly declined the court appointment and submitted a memorial asking to live in seclusion on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 宣武末稍以出山，幹祿執事。

translations.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he gradually came out of the mountains and sought salary and office in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he gradually emerged from seclusion and took up official service for salary and rank.

sentences.zh: 從曆建興、河內二郡太守。

translations.literal: He followed and successively served as Administrator of the two commanderies Jianxing and Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Administrator of Jianxing and Henei commanderies.

sentences.zh: 曆二郡，廉貞寡欲，善撫百姓，人吏追思之。

translations.literal: Through the two commanderies he was incorrupt and sparing in desire, skilled at comforting the common people; officials and people afterward remembered him fondly.
translations.idiomatic: In both commanderies he was incorruptible and frugal, skilled at caring for the people. Officials and commoners alike cherished his memory long afterward.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，梁將曹敬宗寇荊州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiaochang era, the Liang general Cao Jingzong invaded Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiaochang era, the Liang general Cao Jingzong invaded Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 詔衍為別將，與恆農太守王羆救荊州。

translations.literal: An edict made Yan a separate commander; together with Wang Pi, Administrator of Hengnong, he rescued Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yan a separate commander, and together with Wang Pi, Administrator of Hengnong, he marched to relieve Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 衍大破之，荊州圍解。

translations.literal: Yan inflicted a great defeat on him, and the siege of Jing Province was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yan inflicted a crushing defeat on the invaders and lifted the siege of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 除北道都督，鎮鄴西之武城，封安陽縣子。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander of the Northern Route, garrisoned Wucheng west of Ye, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander of the Northern Route, stationed at Wucheng west of Ye, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Anyang County.

sentences.zh: 時相州刺史安樂王鑒潛圖叛逆，衍覺其有異，密表陳之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Jian of Anle, Regional Inspector of Xiang Province, secretly plotted rebellion; Yan perceived something amiss and submitted a secret memorial reporting it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Jian of Anle, Regional Inspector of Xiang Province, was secretly plotting rebellion. Yan sensed something amiss and submitted a confidential memorial reporting it.

sentences.zh: 尋而鑒所部別將嵇宗馳驛告變，乃詔衍與都督源子邕、李神軌等討鑒，平之。

translations.literal: Before long Jian's subordinate Separate Commander Ji Zong raced post-horses to report the uprising; then an edict ordered Yan together with the commanders Yuan Ziyong, Li Shengui, and others to campaign against Jian and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jian's subordinate Separate Commander Ji Zong raced by post relay to report the revolt. An edict then ordered Yan, together with the commanders Yuan Ziyong, Li Shengui, and others, to campaign against Jian and suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 除相州刺史、北道大都督，進封臨汝縣公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Route, and advanced in fief to Duke of Linru County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regional Inspector of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Route, and his title was advanced to Duke of Linru County.

sentences.zh: 詔衍與子邕北討葛榮，軍敗見害。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yan and Ziyong to campaign north against Ge Rong; the army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yan and Ziyong to campaign north against Ge Rong. Their army was defeated and Yan was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、司空、相州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Chariots and Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Regional Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 子嵩襲。

translations.literal: His son Song inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Song inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 叔業之歸魏，又有尹挺、柳玄達、韋伯昕、皇甫光、梁祐、崔高容、閻慶胤、柳僧習並預其功。

translations.literal: When Shuye returned to Wei, there were also Yin Ting, Liu Xuanda, Wei Boxin, Huangfu Guang, Liang You, Cui Gaorong, Yan Qingyin, and Liu Sengxi—all shared in his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye defected to Wei, Yin Ting, Liu Xuanda, Wei Boxin, Huangfu Guang, Liang You, Cui Gaorong, Yan Qingyin, and Liu Sengxi also shared in his achievement.

sentences.zh: 尹挺，天水冀人，仕齊，位陳郡太守。

translations.literal: Yin Ting, a native of Ji in Tianshui, served Qi and held the post of Administrator of Chen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ting, a native of Ji in Tianshui, served in Qi as Administrator of Chen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 與叔業參謀歸誠，曆南司州刺史。

translations.literal: He joined Shuye in planning the turn of allegiance and successively served as Regional Inspector of Southern Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Shuye in planning the defection and later served as Regional Inspector of Southern Si Province.

sentences.zh: 柳玄達，河東解人，頗涉經史，仕齊，諸王參軍。

translations.literal: Liu Xuanda, a native of Jie in Hedong, had considerable exposure to the classics and histories; he served Qi as a staff officer to the princes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanda, a native of Jie in Hedong, was well versed in the classics and histories and served in Qi as a staff officer to the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 與叔業姻婭周旋。

translations.literal: He moved in marriage-kin circles with Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: He moved in the same marriage circles as Shuye and was closely acquainted with him.

sentences.zh: 叔業獻款，玄達贊成其計。

translations.literal: When Shuye offered his allegiance, Xuanda supported and brought his plan to completion.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye offered his allegiance to Wei, Xuanda helped bring the plan to fruition.

sentences.zh: 入魏，除司徒諮議參軍，封南頓縣子。

translations.literal: On entering Wei he was appointed Consulting Staff Officer to the Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Viscount of Nandun County.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Wei he was appointed Consulting Staff Officer to the Minister of Education and enfeoffed as Viscount of Nandun County.

sentences.zh: 卒，改封夏陽縣，子絳襲。

translations.literal: He died; his fief was changed to Xiayang County, and his son Jiang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his fief was changed to Xiayang County. His son Jiang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 絳弟遠，字季雲，性粗放無拘檢，時人或謂之柳癲。

translations.literal: Jiang's younger brother Yuan, style Jiyun, by nature was rough and unrestrained without discipline; people of the time sometimes called him Madman Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang's younger brother Yuan, courtesy name Jiyun, was by nature rough and unrestrained. People of the time sometimes called him Mad Liu.

sentences.zh: 好彈琴耽酒，時有文詠。

translations.literal: He loved playing the zither and indulging in wine, and from time to time composed literary verses.
translations.idiomatic: He loved playing the zither and drinking wine, and from time to time composed literary verses.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，除儀同、開府參軍事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed Peer of the First Rank and Staff Officer of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was appointed Peer of the First Rank and Staff Officer of the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 情琴酒之間，每出行返，家人或問消息，答云：「無所聞，縱聞亦不解。」

translations.literal: Devoted to zither and wine, whenever he went out and returned his family would sometimes ask for news; he would answer: "I heard nothing; even if I heard something I would not understand it."
translations.idiomatic: Absorbed in his zither and wine, whenever he went out and returned his family would sometimes ask what news he had heard. He would answer, "I heard nothing—and even if I did, I wouldn't understand it."

sentences.zh: 後客遊卒。

translations.literal: Later he died while traveling as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while traveling abroad.

sentences.zh: 玄達弟玄瑜，位陰平太守，卒。

translations.literal: Xuanda's younger brother Xuanyu held the post of Administrator of Yinping and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanda's younger brother Xuanyu served as Administrator of Yinping and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子諧，頗有文學，善鼓琴，以新聲手勢，京師士子翕然從學。

translations.literal: His son Xie had considerable literary accomplishment, was skilled at striking the zither, and by novel tones and hand gestures the gentlemen of the capital flocked to study with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie was accomplished in letters and skilled at the zither. With his novel melodies and playing gestures, the young gentlemen of the capital flocked to study under him.

sentences.zh: 除著作佐郎，于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and met harm at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 韋伯昕，京兆杜陵人，學尚有壯氣。

translations.literal: Wei Boxin, a native of Duling in Jingzhao, in learning and conduct possessed bold spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Boxin, a native of Duling in Jingzhao, was learned and possessed a bold spirit.

sentences.zh: 自以才智優於裴植，常輕之，植嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: He considered his talent and wisdom superior to Pei Zhi and constantly looked down on him; Zhi hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He considered himself cleverer than Pei Zhi and constantly looked down on him. Zhi hated him with the bitterness of a blood enemy.

sentences.zh: 即彥先之妹夫也。

translations.literal: He was the husband of Yanxian's younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: He was the husband of Yanxian's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 叔業以其有大志，故遣子芬之為質。

translations.literal: Shuye, because he had great ambition, therefore sent his son Fenzhi as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shuye saw that he had great ambition, he sent his son Fenzhi as a hostage to him.

sentences.zh: 入魏，封零陵縣男，曆南陽太守，坐事免。

translations.literal: On entering Wei he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lingling County, successively served as Administrator of Nanyang, and was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Wei he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lingling County and served as Administrator of Nanyang before being dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後拜員外散騎常侍，加中壘將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed External Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and given the additional title General of the Central Rampart.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed External Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry with the additional title General of the Central Rampart.

sentences.zh: 告裴植謀為廢黜，植坐死。

translations.literal: He reported that Pei Zhi plotted deposition; Zhi was condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Pei Zhi for plotting deposition, and Zhi was executed.

sentences.zh: 後百餘日，伯昕亦病卒。

translations.literal: More than a hundred days later Boxin also died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a hundred days later Boxin also died of illness.

sentences.zh: 臨亡，見植為祟，口云：「裴尚書死，不獨見由，何以見怒？」

translations.literal: Near death he saw Zhi as a haunting spirit and said aloud: "Director Pei died—not solely because of me; why show anger toward me?"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he saw Zhi's ghost and cried out, "Director Pei died—not solely because of me. Why do you show me such anger?"

sentences.zh: 皇甫光，安定人，美須髯，善言笑。

translations.literal: Huangfu Guang, a native of Anding, had handsome beard and whiskers and was skilled in speech and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Guang, a native of Anding, had a handsome beard and was gifted at conversation and wit.

sentences.zh: 入魏，卒于勃海太守。

translations.literal: On entering Wei he died as Governor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: After entering Wei he died while serving as Governor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 兄椿齡，從薛安都于彭城內附，除岐州刺史。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chunling followed Xue Andu in submitting from within Pengcheng and was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chunling followed Xue Andu in surrendering at Pengcheng and was appointed Regional Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 椿齡子璋，鄉郡相。

translations.literal: Chunling's son Zhang was a district magistrate of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chunling's son Zhang served as a district magistrate in his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 璋弟枿，位吏部郎，性貪婪，多所受納，鬻賣吏官，皆有定價。

translations.literal: Zhang's younger brother Nie held the post of Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; by nature he was greedy, accepted many bribes, and sold official posts—all with fixed prices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's younger brother Nie served as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel. Greedy by nature, he accepted countless bribes and sold official posts, each at a fixed price.

sentences.zh: 後以丞相、高陽王雍之婿，為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, as son-in-law to the Chancellor and Prince Yong of Gaoyang, he became Regional Inspector of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as son-in-law to Chancellor Prince Yong of Gaoyang, he was appointed Regional Inspector of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 為政殘暴，百姓患之。

translations.literal: His governance was cruel and violent; the common people suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was cruel and violent, and the people suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 卒于安南將軍、光祿大夫、贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died holding the posts of General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously granted Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding the posts of General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and was posthumously honored as Left Deputy Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子長卿，太尉司馬。

translations.literal: His son Changqing was a Major under the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Changqing served as Major under the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 梁祐，北地人，叔業從姑子也。

translations.literal: Liang You, a native of Beidi, was Shuye's nephew by his paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Liang You, a native of Beidi, was Shuye's nephew on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 好學，便弓馬，隨叔業征伐，身被五十餘創。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at bow and horse; he followed Shuye on campaigns and received more than fifty wounds on his body.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and was skilled in archery and horsemanship. He followed Shuye on campaign and sustained more than fifty wounds.

sentences.zh: 景明初，賜爵山桑子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shansang.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jingming period, he was granted the title Viscount of Shansang.

sentences.zh: 出為北地太守，清身率下，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Beidi, led his subordinates with a pure conduct, and enjoyed a very fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Administrator of Beidi, where he led by personal integrity and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 曆大中大夫。

translations.literal: He successively served as Grand Master for All Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Grand Master for All Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從容風雅，好為談詠，常與朝廷名賢，泛舟洛水，以詩酒自娛。

translations.literal: Unhurried and refined, fond of discourse and verse, he often joined famous worthies of the court boating on the Luo River, amusing himself with poetry and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Easy in manner and elegant in taste, he loved conversation and poetry; he often took famous men of the court boating on the Luo River, finding his pleasure in verse and wine.

sentences.zh: 遷光祿大夫，端然養志，不曆權門，卒於京兆內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Palace Library, uprightly cultivating his aspirations, not passing through the gates of power-holders, and died as Inner Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Library, composedly nurturing his ideals and never courting powerful families; he died in office as Inner Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 崔高容，清河人，博學善文辭，美風彩。

translations.literal: Cui Gaorong, a man of Qinghe, was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition, with fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gaorong of Qinghe was deeply learned, gifted in letters, and striking in presence.

sentences.zh: 景明初，位散騎侍郎，出為揚州開府掾，帶陳留太守，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, he was Attendant Cavalier at Large; he went out as staff officer of Yangzhou headquarters, concurrently Administrator of Chenliu, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jingming period he was Regular Attendant Cavalier at Large, then served as staff officer for the Yangzhou headquarters with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Chenliu; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 閻慶胤，天水人，博識洽聞，善於談論，聽其言說，不覺忘疲。

translations.literal: Yan Qingyin, a man of Tianshui, was widely informed and well versed in talk; those who listened to him speak did not notice fatigue setting in.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Qingyin of Tianshui was erudite and eloquent; listeners to his discourse forgot their weariness.

sentences.zh: 卒于敷城太守。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Administrator of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Administrator of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 柳僧習見其子虯傳。

translations.literal: Liu Sengxi—see the biography of his son Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: For Liu Sengxi, see the biography of his son Qiu.

sentences.zh: 夏侯道遷，譙國人也。

translations.literal: Xiahou Daoqian was a man of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Daoqian was a native of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 少有志操。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and moral fiber.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he possessed firm purpose and integrity.

sentences.zh: 年十七，父母為結婚韋氏，道遷云：「欲懷四方之志，不願取婦。」

translations.literal: At seventeen, his parents arranged his marriage to the Wei clan. Daoqian said: "I wish to harbor ambitions for the four quarters and do not wish to take a wife."
translations.idiomatic: When he was seventeen, his parents arranged his marriage to the Wei family. Daoqian said, "I mean to embrace ambitions for the whole realm and do not wish to marry."

sentences.zh: 家人咸謂戲言。

translations.literal: His family all regarded it as jesting talk.
translations.idiomatic: The whole household took this for a joke.

sentences.zh: 及婚，求覓不知所在。

translations.literal: When the wedding day came, they sought him but could not find where he was.
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding day they searched for him but could not discover his whereabouts.

sentences.zh: 訪問，乃雲逃入益州。

translations.literal: On inquiry, it turned out he had fled into Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After inquiry they learned he had fled into Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 後隨裴叔業于壽春，為南譙太守。

translations.literal: Later he followed Pei Shuye at Shouchun as Administrator of Nanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Pei Shuye to Shouchun and served as Administrator of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 二家雖為姻好，親情不協，遂單騎歸魏，拜驍騎將軍，隨王肅至壽春。

translations.literal: Though the two families were joined by marriage, their kinship accord was poor; he therefore rode alone back to Wei, was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, and followed Wang Su to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Although the two houses were linked by marriage, affection between the kin did not harmonize; he therefore rode alone back to Wei, was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry, and followed Wang Su to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 肅薨，道遷棄戍南叛。

translations.literal: When Su died, Daoqian abandoned his garrison and defected south.
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Daoqian abandoned his post and rebelled southward.

sentences.zh: 會梁以莊丘黑為征虜將軍、梁秦二州刺史，鎮南鄭。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang appointed Zhuangqiu Hei as General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces, stationing troops at Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liang appointed Zhuangqiu Hei General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Governor of Liang and Qin provinces, with his headquarters at Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 黑請道遷為長史，帶漢中郡。

translations.literal: Hei requested Daoqian as chief clerk, concurrently in charge of Hanzhong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hei asked that Daoqian serve as chief clerk with concurrent authority over Hanzhong commandery.

sentences.zh: 會黑死，而道遷陰圖歸順。

translations.literal: When Hei died, Daoqian secretly plotted to return and submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Hei died, Daoqian secretly planned to return and submit to the north.

sentences.zh: 先是，仇池鎮將楊靈珍反叛南奔，梁以靈珍為征虜將軍，假武都王，助戍漢中。

translations.literal: Before this, Yang Lingzhen, frontier commander of Chouchi, had rebelled and fled south; Liang appointed Lingzhen General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Acting Prince of Wudu, to help garrison Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Lingzhen, garrison commander of Chouchi, had rebelled and fled south; Liang made him General Who Pacifies Barbarians and Acting Prince of Wudu to assist in garrisoning Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 道遷乃擊靈珍，斬其父子，送首于京師。

translations.literal: Daoqian then attacked Lingzhen, beheaded him and his sons, and sent their heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian then attacked Lingzhen, beheaded him and his sons, and sent their heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 江悅之等推道遷為梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuezhi and others pushed Daoqian to be Governor of Liang and Qin provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuezhi and others urged Daoqian to assume the governorship of Liang and Qin provinces.

sentences.zh: 道遷遣表歸闕，詔璽書慰勉，授持節、散騎常侍、平南將軍、豫州刺史，封豐縣侯，遣尚書邢巒指授節度。

translations.literal: Daoqian sent a memorial surrendering to court; an edict with imperial seal comforted and encouraged him, appointing Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant at the Side, General Who Pacifies the South, Governor of Yu Province, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Feng County, and dispatching Minister Xing Luan to direct his command.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian sent a memorial of submission to the throne; the emperor responded with a sealed edict of encouragement, appointing him Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Governor of Yu Province, enfeoffing him as Marquis of Feng County, and sending the Minister Xing Luan to confer operational authority.

sentences.zh: 道遷表受平南、常侍，而辭豫州、豐縣侯，引裴叔業公爵為例。

translations.literal: Daoqian memorialized accepting Pacify South and Regular Attendant but declining Yu Province and Marquis of Feng, citing Duke Pei Shuye as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian memorialized that he would accept General Who Pacifies the South and Regular Attendant but decline Yu Province and the marquisate of Feng, citing the precedent of Duke Pei Shuye.

sentences.zh: 宣武不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu would not agree.

sentences.zh: 道遷自南鄭來朝京師，引見於太極東堂，免冠徒跣謝曰：「比在壽春，遭韋纘之酷，申控無所，致此倡狂。

translations.literal: Daoqian came from Nanzheng to court, was received in the eastern hall of Taiji, and bareheaded and barefoot apologized: "Previously at Shouchun I suffered Wei Zuan cruelty; I had nowhere to appeal and thus brought on this reckless misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian came from Nanzheng to the capital and was received in the eastern hall of Taiji; bareheaded and barefoot he apologized: "When I was at Shouchun I suffered the cruelty of Wei Zuan; with no one to whom I could appeal, I fell into this wild defiance.

sentences.zh: 是段之來，希酬昔遇。」

translations.literal: The reason I have come this time is that I hoped to repay past kindness."
translations.idiomatic: I have come now in the hope of repaying former favor."

sentences.zh: 宣武曰：「卿建為山之功，一簣之玷，何足謝也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu said: "You have built a mountain-high achievement; what is a basket of earth stain that you need apologize?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu said, "You have heaped up a mountain of merit; what is one basketful of earth beside it that you should apologize?"

sentences.zh: 道遷以賞報為微，逡巡不拜，尋改封濮陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Daoqian, finding the rewards slight, hesitated and did not bow in acceptance; soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian, thinking the reward too small, hesitated and would not bow in acceptance; soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，頻表解州，宣武許之。

translations.literal: After more than a year he repeatedly memorialized to resign the province; Emperor Xuanwu permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he repeatedly asked to be relieved of the governorship, and Emperor Xuanwu granted his request.

sentences.zh: 除南袞州大中正，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Superior Clan Evaluator for Southern Yanzhou but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Superior Clan Evaluator for Southern Yanzhou but declined the post.

sentences.zh: 道遷雖學不深洽，而曆覽書史，閑習尺牘。

translations.literal: Though Daoqian's learning was not deep and comprehensive, he had perused histories, and was practiced in documents and correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Although Daoqian learning was not profound, he had read widely in histories and was skilled in letters and documents.

sentences.zh: 好言宴，務口實，京師珍羞，罔不畢有。

translations.literal: He loved banquets and valued delicacies; no delicacy of the capital was absent from his table.
translations.idiomatic: He loved feasting and prized fine food; every delicacy of the capital found its way to his table.

sentences.zh: 于京城西水次市地，大起園池，殖列蔬果，延致秀彥，時往遊適。

translations.literal: At the waterfront market west of the capital he bought land and raised a large garden and pool, planting vegetables and fruits in rows, inviting outstanding talents, and often going there for excursions.
translations.idiomatic: West of the capital, at the riverside market, he bought land and built a large garden and pond, planting rows of vegetables and fruit, inviting men of talent, and often going there for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 妓妾十餘，常自娛樂，國秩歲入三千餘匹，專供酒饌，不營家產。

translations.literal: More than ten concubines—he constantly amused himself; his state stipend brought in over three thousand bolts yearly, devoted solely to food and drink, with no thought for household property.
translations.idiomatic: He kept more than ten concubines and constantly entertained himself; his state income of over three thousand bolts a year went entirely to food and wine, and he did not trouble himself with family estates.

sentences.zh: 每誦孔融語曰：「坐上客恆滿，樽中酒不空，餘非吾事也。」
