translations.literal: He often quoted Kong Rong saying: "Guests ever fill my seats, wine never empties in my cups—the rest is no concern of mine."
translations.idiomatic: He often quoted Kong Rong: "My guests are always full, my cups never empty—everything else is none of my business."

sentences.zh: 識者多之。

translations.literal: Men of discernment largely approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment largely approved of him.

sentences.zh: 曆華、瀛二州刺史，為政清嚴，善禁盜賊。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of Hua and Ying provinces; his governance was pure and strict, and he was good at suppressing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Governor of Hua and Ying provinces; his rule was clean and severe, and he was adept at suppressing bandits.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈雍州刺史，諡明侯。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously made Governor of Yong Province, posthumous name Marquis Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed Governor of Yong Province with the posthumous title Marquis Ming.

sentences.zh: 初，道遷以拔漢中歸誠本由王潁興之計，求分邑戶五百封之，宣武不許。

translations.literal: At first, Daoqian's plan to seize Hanzhong and submit in loyalty had chiefly been Wang Yingxing's scheme; he requested five hundred households of his fief be granted to Yingxing, but Emperor Xuanwu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: At first Daoqian recovery of Hanzhong and loyal submission had chiefly been Wang Yingxing plan; he asked that five hundred households of his fief be granted to Yingxing, but Emperor Xuanwu refused.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，道遷重求分封，太后大奇之，議欲更以三百戶封潁興，會卒，遂寢。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling assumed the regency, Daoqian again sought a share of enfeoffment; the Empress Dowager was greatly struck by it and considered enfeoffing Yingxing with three hundred households instead, but when he died the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling took the regency, Daoqian again sought a division of the fief; the Empress Dowager was greatly impressed and considered granting Yingxing three hundred households, but Yingxing died and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 道遷不聘正室，唯有庶子數人。

translations.literal: Daoqian did not marry a principal wife, having only several sons born of concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian never took a principal wife and had only several sons by concubines.

sentences.zh: 長子夬、，字元廷，曆鎮遠將軍、南袞州大中正。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kui, styled Yuanting, successively served as General of Garrison Advancement and Superior Clan Evaluator for Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kui, courtesy name Yuanting, successively served as General of Garrison Advancement and Superior Clan Evaluator for Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夬性好酒，居喪不戚，醇醪肥鮮，不離於口，沽買飲啖，多所費用。

translations.literal: Kui was fond of wine; in mourning he was not sorrowful—strong wine and rich food never left his mouth; buying drink and food cost much.
translations.idiomatic: Kui loved wine; during mourning he showed no grief, and rich brew and fine meat never left his lips; he spent heavily buying drink and food.

sentences.zh: 父時田園，貨賣略盡，人間債猶數千餘匹，谷食至常不足，弟妹不免饑寒。

translations.literal: During his father's lifetime the family estates were sold off almost entirely; private debts still ran to several thousand bolts, grain was often insufficient, and siblings and sisters could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: In his father lifetime the family fields were sold off nearly completely; private debts still amounted to several thousand bolts, grain was often short, and his younger brothers and sisters could not escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 初，道遷知夬好酒，不欲傳授國封。

translations.literal: At first Daoqian, knowing Kui loved wine, did not wish to pass on the hereditary enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, knowing Kui's love of wine, Daoqian had not wished to pass on the hereditary fief.

sentences.zh: 夬未亡前，忽夢見征虜將軍房世寶至其家聽事，與其父坐，屏人密言。

translations.literal: Before Kui died he suddenly dreamed the General Who Pacifies Barbarians Fang Shibao came to his house reception hall and sat with his father; attendants were dismissed for secret talk.
translations.idiomatic: Before Kui's death he suddenly dreamed that Fang Shibao, General Who Pacifies Barbarians, came to his home reception hall and sat with his father while attendants were sent away for a private talk.

sentences.zh: 夬心驚懼，謂人曰：「世寶為官，少間必擊我也。」

translations.literal: Kui was startled and said to others: "Shibao holds office—before long he will surely strike me."
translations.idiomatic: Kui was alarmed and said to others, "Shibao has taken office; before long he will surely beat me."

sentences.zh: 尋有人至，云：「官呼郎」，隨召即去，遣左右杖之二百，不勝楚痛，大叫。

translations.literal: Soon someone came saying "Sir summons the young master"; summoned he at once went; they sent attendants to cane him two hundred strokes; unable to bear the lash he cried out greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone arrived saying, "The master calls the young gentleman"; he went at once, and attendants were sent to cane him two hundred times; unable to endure the pain he cried out loudly.

sentences.zh: 良久乃悟，流汗徹於寢具。

translations.literal: After a long while he awoke, sweat soaking through bedding.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he woke, sweat soaking through his bedding.

sentences.zh: 至明，前京城太守趙卓詣之，見其衣濕，謂夬曰：「卿昨夜當大飲，溺衣如此。」

translations.literal: By daybreak the former Administrator of the Capital Zhao Zhuo visited him, saw his clothes wet, and said to Kui: "You must have drunk heavily last night—soaked your clothes like this."
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Zhao Zhuo, former Administrator of the Capital, came to see him, noticed his clothes were wet, and said to Kui, "You must have drunk heavily last night and wet your clothes like this."

sentences.zh: 夬乃具陳所夢。

translations.literal: Kui then related the dream in full.
translations.idiomatic: Kui then told the dream in full.

sentences.zh: 先是旬余，秘書監鄭道昭暴病卒，夬聞，謂卓曰：「人生何常，唯當縱飲。」

translations.literal: About ten days before, Secretariat Supervisor Zheng Daozhao had died suddenly of illness; hearing of it Kui said to Zhuo: "Human life how constant—only drown oneself in drink."
translations.idiomatic: Some ten days earlier Secretariat Supervisor Zheng Daozhao had died suddenly; when Kui heard of it he said to Zhuo, "How constant is human life? One should only drink to excess."

sentences.zh: 於是昏酣遂甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sank into deeper stupor.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sank into still deeper drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 夢後，二日不能言，針之，乃得語，而猶虛劣。

translations.literal: After the dream, two days he could not speak; after acupuncture he could speak, but remained weak.
translations.idiomatic: After the dream he could not speak for two days; after acupuncture he could speak again, but remained feeble.

sentences.zh: 俄而心悶而死。

translations.literal: Soon oppressed in the chest he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, oppressed in the chest, he died.

sentences.zh: 洗浴者視其屍體，大有杖處，青赤隱起，二百下許。

translations.literal: Those who bathed the corpse saw on his body prominent lash marks, blue and red rising, about two hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who washed the corpse found on his body heavy cane marks, blue and red welts, roughly two hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 贈钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 初，夬與南人辛諶、庾遵、江文遙等終日遊聚。

translations.literal: At first Kui with southerners Xin Chen, Yu Zun, Jiang Wenyuan and others gathered in daily revelry.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kui had spent whole days in revelry with southerners such as Xin Chen, Yu Zun, and Jiang Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 酣飲之際，恆相謂曰：「人生局促，何殊朝露，坐上相看，先後間耳。

translations.literal: In the midst of drinking they would say to one another: "Life is cramped, no different from morning dew—we sit facing one another, only a span apart in order.
translations.idiomatic: While drinking they would say to one another, "Life is cramped, no different from morning dew—we sit looking at one another, only a breath apart in turn.

sentences.zh: 脫有先亡者，於良辰美景，靈前飲宴，儻或有知，庶共歆饗。」

translations.literal: If any should die first, on a fine day and scene we shall feast before his spirit-tent; perhaps if they have knowledge they may share the offerings."
translations.idiomatic: If any of us dies first, on some fine day and scene let us feast before his spirit seat; if the dead still have awareness, perhaps they may share the offerings."

sentences.zh: 及夬亡後，三月上巳，諸人相率至夬靈前，仍共酌飲。

translations.literal: After Kui died, on the third-month Shangsi the company went together before Kui spirit seat and still drank together.
translations.idiomatic: After Kui died, on the third-month Shangsi festival the group went together to Kui spirit seat and drank as before.

sentences.zh: 時日晚天陰，室中微暗，咸見夬在坐，衣服形容，不異平昔，時執杯酒，似若獻酬，但無語耳。

translations.literal: The sky that evening was overcast and the room dim; all saw Kui seated, dress and features no different from ordinary days, at times holding a wine cup as if offering or returning a toast, but without words.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the sky was overcast and the room dim; all saw Kui seated, his dress and appearance unchanged from ordinary days, at times holding a wine cup as if offering or returning a toast, yet without speaking.

sentences.zh: 夬家客雍僧明心有畏恐，披簾欲出，便即僵僕，狀若被毆。

translations.literal: Kui's house guest Yong Sengming was inwardly afraid; he pulled back the curtain to leave and at once collapsed stiff as if beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Kui house guest Yong Sengming was inwardly afraid; he drew back the curtain to go out and at once fell stiff as if he had been beaten.

sentences.zh: 夬從兄欣宗云：「今是節日，諸人憶弟疇昔之言，故來共飲。

translations.literal: Kui's elder cousin by the paternal line Xin Zong said: "Today is the festival—everyone remembers my younger brother's words of old and came to drink together.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's paternal cousin Xin Zong said, "Today is the festival; everyone remembered my younger brother's words of old and came to drink together.

sentences.zh: 僧明何罪，而被嗔責？」

translations.literal: What crime has Sengming that he was rebuked and punished?"
translations.idiomatic: What crime did Sengming commit that he was scolded and punished?"

sentences.zh: 僧明便悟。

translations.literal: Sengming then understood.
translations.idiomatic: Sengming then understood.

sentences.zh: 而欣宗鬼語如夬平生，並怒家人，皆得其罪，又發陰私竊盜，咸有次緒。

translations.literal: And Xin Zong ghost-speech was like Kui in life; together they scolded the household, each offense known; they also exposed secret thefts, all in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xin Zong spoke in a ghostly voice like Kui in life; together they rebuked the household, naming each offense, and also exposed hidden thefts, all in proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 夬妻，裴植之女也，與道遷諸妾不睦，訟鬩徹於公庭。

translations.literal: Kui's wife was a daughter of Pei Zhi; she was not at peace with Daoqian's various concubines, lawsuits reaching the public court.
translations.idiomatic: Kui wife was a daughter of Pei Zhi; she was at odds with Daoqian concubines, and their quarrels reached the public courts.

sentences.zh: 子籍，年十餘歲，襲祖封已數年，而夬弟翽等言其眇目ＩＴ疾，不任承繼，自以與夬同庶，己應紹襲。

translations.literal: His son Ji, over ten years old, had inherited the grandfather's enfeoffment for several years, but Kui's younger brothers Shen and others said he was dim-sighted and epileptic, unfit to succeed; they themselves being of the same concubine-born status as Kui, ought to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, a boy of more than ten, had inherited the grandfather fief for several years, but Kui younger brothers Shen and others said he was dim-sighted and epileptic and unfit to succeed; claiming the same concubine-born status as Kui, they held that they ought to inherit.

sentences.zh: 尚書奏籍承封。

translations.literal: The Ministry submitted that Ji should receive the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry memorialized that Ji should receive the fief.

sentences.zh: 道遷兄子ＩＳ，位咸陽太守。

translations.literal: Zao, a son of Daoqian's elder brother, held the post of Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zao, a son of Daoqian elder brother, served as Administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 道遷之謀，又襄陽羅道珍、北海王安世、潁川辛諶、漢中薑永等皆參其勳末。

translations.literal: In Daoqian's plotting there were also Luo Daozhen of Xiangyang, Wang Anshi of Beihai, Xin Chen of Yingchuan, Jiang Yong of Hanzhong, and others—all shared in the tail end of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Those who shared in the later stages of Daoqian achievement included Luo Daozhen of Xiangyang, Wang Anshi of Beihai, Xin Chen of Yingchuan, Jiang Yong of Hanzhong, and others.

sentences.zh: 道珍為齊州東平原相，有能名。

translations.literal: Daozhen was Chancellor of Eastern Pingyuan in Qi Province and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhen served as Chancellor of Eastern Pingyuan in Qi Province and had a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 安世，苻堅丞相王猛玄孫也。

translations.literal: Anshi was the great-great-grandson of Former Qin Chancellor Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was the great-great-grandson of Wang Meng, chancellor of Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 曆涉書傳，位北華州刺史。

translations.literal: He read widely in books and histories and served as Governor of Northern Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged through books and histories and held the post of Governor of Northern Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 諶，魏衛尉辛毗後也，有文學，位濮陽、上党二郡太守。

translations.literal: Chen was a descendant of Wei Minister of the Guard Xin Pi; he had literary talent and served as Administrator of Puyang and Shangdang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a descendant of Xin Pi, Minister of the Guard of Wei; he was literary and served as Administrator of Puyang and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 永善彈琴，有文學，位漢中太守。

translations.literal: Yong was skilled at the zither and had literary talent; he served as Administrator of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was skilled at the zither and gifted in letters; he served as Administrator of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 永弟漾，亦善士，性至孝。

translations.literal: Yong's younger brother Yang was also a good man, and by nature supremely filial.
translations.idiomatic: Yong younger brother Yang was likewise a worthy man and by nature deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 時潁川庾道者，亦與道遷俱入國，雖不參勳謀，亦為奇士。

translations.literal: At that time Yu Daozhe of Yingchuan also entered the state together with Daoqian; though he did not take part in the merit plotting, he too was an extraordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Daozhe of Yingchuan also came north with Daoqian; though he did not join the plotting for merit, he too was a remarkable man.

sentences.zh: 曆覽史傳，善草隸書，輕財重義。

translations.literal: He read widely in historical records, was skilled in cursive and clerical script, and prized righteousness over wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in historical works, excelled in cursive and clerical calligraphy, and valued righteousness above wealth.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，右中郎將。

translations.literal: In Liang he served as Right Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liang he served as Right Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 及至洛陽，環堵弊廬，多與俊秀交舊，積二十餘歲，殊無宦情。

translations.literal: When he reached Luoyang he lived in a cramped, dilapidated hut; he associated much with outstanding men of old acquaintance, and for more than twenty years showed virtually no desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived in Luoyang he dwelt in a cramped, broken-down hut; for more than twenty years he kept company with talented friends and showed almost no wish for office.

sentences.zh: 後為饒安縣令，罷，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Magistrate of Raoan County; after leaving office he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Magistrate of Raoan County; after leaving that post he died.

sentences.zh: 李元護，遼東襄平人，晉司徒胤之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Li Yuanhu was a man of Xiangping in Liaodong, eighth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanhu was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, eighth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Li Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤子順、璠及孫沉、志皆有名宦。

translations.literal: Yin sons Shun and Fan and grandsons Shen and Zhi all had famous careers in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sons Shun and Fan and grandsons Shen and Zhi all attained distinguished offices.

sentences.zh: 沉孫根，仕慕容寶，為中書監。

translations.literal: Shen grandson Gen served Murong Bao as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shen grandson Gen served Murong Bao as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 根子後智等隨慕容德南渡河，居青州，數世無名，三齊豪門多輕之。

translations.literal: Gen sons Houzhi and others followed Murong De south across the river and settled in Qing Province; for generations they had no fame, and the great houses of the Three Qi regions largely looked down on them.
translations.idiomatic: Gen sons Houzhi and others followed Murong De south across the river and settled in Qing Province; for generations they held no standing, and the great clans of the Three Qi looked down on them.

sentences.zh: 元護以魏平齊後，隨父懷慶南奔。

translations.literal: After the state pacified Qi, Yuanhu followed his father Huaiqing in fleeing south.
translations.idiomatic: When the state pacified Qi, Yuanhu followed his father Huaiqing in fleeing south.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，美須髯，少有武力。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a fine beard and whiskers, and in youth possessed martial strength.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, with a handsome beard and whiskers, and in youth had martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，位馬頭太守，雖以將用自達，然亦頗覽文史，習于簡牘。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as Administrator of Matou; though he rose through military talent, he also read widely in literature and history and was practiced in documents.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Administrator of Matou; though he advanced by military talent, he also read widely in literature and history and was skilled with documents.

sentences.zh: 後為裴叔業司馬，帶汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Pei Shuye staff officer with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was staff officer to Pei Shuye with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 叔業歸順，元護贊同其謀。

translations.literal: When Shuye submitted to the north, Yuanhu endorsed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye submitted to the north, Yuanhu supported his design.

sentences.zh: 叔業疾病，元護督率上下以俟援軍。

translations.literal: When Shuye fell ill, Yuanhu directed those above and below while awaiting the relief army.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuye fell ill, Yuanhu led the garrison in awaiting the relief army.

sentences.zh: 壽春克定，元護頗有力焉。

translations.literal: When Shouchun was secured, Yuanhu contributed considerable effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun was taken, Yuanhu contributed considerable effort.

sentences.zh: 景明初，以元護為齊州刺史、廣饒縣伯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Yuanhu was made Governor of Qi Province and Baron of Guangrao County.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jingming period Yuanhu was appointed Governor of Qi Province and Baron of Guangrao County.

sentences.zh: 尋以州人柳世明圖為不軌，元護誅戮所加，微為濫酷。

translations.literal: Soon, because the provincial gentleman Liu Shiming plotted rebellion, Yuanhu executions in the case were slightly excessive and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when a provincial gentleman named Liu Shiming plotted sedition, the executions Yuanhu carried out were somewhat excessive and harsh.

sentences.zh: 州內饑儉，表請賑貸，蠲其賦役。

translations.literal: Within the province there was famine; he memorialized requesting relief grain on loan and remission of taxes and corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the province, he submitted a memorial requesting relief grain and the remission of taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 但多有部曲，時為侵擾，城邑苦之，故不得為良刺史也。

translations.literal: Yet he had many retainers who at times committed harassment; towns and cities suffered under them, so he could not be reckoned a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: But he kept a large retinue that often preyed on the people; towns and cities suffered, and he did not count among the good governors.

sentences.zh: 三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his tenure he died.

sentences.zh: 病前月餘，京師無故傳其凶問。

translations.literal: More than a month before his illness, the capital for no reason circulated word of his death.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month before he fell ill, the capital was rife with groundless rumors of his death.

sentences.zh: 又城外送客亭柱有人書曰「李齊州死」，綱佐餞別者見而拭之，後復如此。

translations.literal: Moreover, on a pillar of the guest pavilion outside the city wall someone wrote, "Li of Qi Province is dead"; aides seeing off guests wiped it away, yet it appeared again the same way.
translations.idiomatic: Someone also wrote on a pillar of the roadside guest pavilion outside the walls, "Li of Qi Province is dead." Aides who were seeing guests off erased it, but the writing reappeared just the same.

sentences.zh: 元護妾妓十餘，聲色自縱。

translations.literal: Yuanhu had more than ten concubines and performers and indulged himself in music and women.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhu kept more than ten concubines and courtesans and gave himself over to music and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 情欲既甚，支骨稍消，須長二尺，一時落盡。

translations.literal: His lust was extreme; his flesh and bones gradually wasted away; his beard, two feet long, fell out all at once.
translations.idiomatic: His passions ran so deep that his flesh wasted away; his two-foot beard fell out in a single day.

sentences.zh: 贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 元護為齊州，經拜舊墓，巡省故宅，饗賜村老，莫不欣暢。

translations.literal: When Yuanhu held Qi Province, he would visit his ancestral graves, tour his former residence, feast and bestow gifts on village elders, and none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuanhu was governor of Qi, he would pay respects at the family graves, tour his old home, and feast and reward the village elders—everyone was delighted.

sentences.zh: 及將亡，謂左右曰：「吾嘗以方伯簿伍至青州，士女屬目。

translations.literal: When he was about to die, he told those beside him: "I once came to Qing Province as a regional inspector in full retinue, and men and women fixed their eyes upon me.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he told his attendants, "I once entered Qing Province as a regional lord at the head of a full train, and men and women turned to watch.

sentences.zh: 若喪過東陽，不可不好設儀衛，哭泣盡哀，令觀者改容也。」

translations.literal: If my funeral passes through Dongyang, you must not fail to array guards of honor and weep with full grief, so that onlookers change countenance."
translations.idiomatic: If my funeral cortège passes through Dongyang, you must array a fine guard of honor and weep with full grief, so that every onlooker is moved to change expression."

sentences.zh: 家人遵其誡。

translations.literal: His family followed his injunction.
translations.idiomatic: His family carried out his instructions.

sentences.zh: 子會襲，正始中降爵為子。

translations.literal: His son Hui inherited; in the Zhengshi era the enfeoffment was reduced to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui inherited the title; in the Zhengshi period the rank was reduced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 會頑騃好酒，其妻南陽太守清河房伯玉女也，甚有姿色，會不答之。

translations.literal: Hui was dull-witted and fond of wine. His wife was Fang Biyu, daughter of Administrator of Nanyang Fang Boyu of Qinghe—a woman of striking beauty whom Hui would not receive.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was dull and addicted to wine. His wife was Fang Biyu, daughter of Fang Boyu, Administrator of Nanyang in Qinghe—a woman of great beauty whom Hui would not touch.

sentences.zh: 房乃通其弟機，因會醉，殺之。

translations.literal: Fang then took his younger brother Ji as lover; when Hui was drunk she had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fang took up with his younger brother Ji and, when Hui was drunk, had him killed.

sentences.zh: 子景宣襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingxuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingxuan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 機與房遂如夫婦，積十餘年，房氏色衰，乃更婚娶。

translations.literal: Ji and Fang then lived as husband and wife for more than ten years; when Fang beauty faded, he took another wife.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Fang lived as husband and wife for more than ten years; when Fang lost her looks, he married again.

sentences.zh: 元護弟靜，性貪忍，兄亡未斂，便剝妓服玩及餘物。

translations.literal: Yuanhu younger brother Jing was by nature greedy and cruel; before his elder brother was laid in the coffin he stripped the performers of garments, trinkets, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhu younger brother Jing was greedy and cruel; before his brother body was even encoffined he stripped the courtesans of their clothes, ornaments, and whatever else he could take.

sentences.zh: 曆齊郡內史。

translations.literal: He served as Inner Governor of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Inner Governor of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 席法友，安定人也，祖、父南奔。

translations.literal: Xi Fayou was a man of Anding; his grandfather and father fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Fayou was a native of Anding; his grandfather and father had fled south.

sentences.zh: 法友仕齊，以膂力自效，任安豐新蔡二郡太守、建安戍主。

translations.literal: Fayou served Qi and proved himself by bodily strength, holding the posts of Administrator of Anfeng and Xincai commanderies and garrison commander of Jianan.
translations.idiomatic: Fayou served under Qi, distinguishing himself by sheer strength; he was Administrator of Anfeng and Xincai and commander of the Jianan garrison.

sentences.zh: 後與裴叔業同謀歸魏，拜豫州刺史、苞信縣伯。

translations.literal: Later he joined Pei Shuye in plotting to surrender to Wei and was appointed Governor of Yu Province and Baron of Baoxin County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he plotted with Pei Shuye to defect to Wei and was appointed Governor of Yu Province and Baron of Baoxin.

sentences.zh: 叔業卒後，法友與裴植追成業志，淮南克定，法友有力焉。

translations.literal: After Shuye died, Fayou with Pei Zhi pursued completion of the enterprise; when Huainan was pacified, Fayou had a share of the force.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuye died, Fayou and Pei Zhi carried on his design; when Huainan was secured, Fayou had done his part.

sentences.zh: 曆華、並二州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Governor of Hua and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Governor of Hua and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 後為別將出淮南，欲解朐山之圍。

translations.literal: Later, as a separate commander he marched out into Huainan intending to lift the siege of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a detached commander, he marched into Huainan to relieve the siege of Qushan.

sentences.zh: 法友始渡淮而朐山敗沒，遂停十年。

translations.literal: Fayou had only just crossed the Huai when Qushan fell; he then remained idle for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Fayou had barely crossed the Huai when Qushan was lost, and he then sat idle for ten years.

sentences.zh: 恬靜自安，不競世利。

translations.literal: Tranquil and self-content, he did not contend for worldly profit.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in quiet contentment and did not strive for worldly gain.

sentences.zh: 宣武末，除濟州刺史，廉和著稱。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xuanwu reign he was made Governor of Ji Province, famed for integrity and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Xuanwu reign he was appointed Governor of Ji Province, where his integrity and gentleness won renown.

sentences.zh: 又徙封乘氏。

translations.literal: His fief was transferred to Chengsi.
translations.idiomatic: His fief was transferred to Chengsi.

sentences.zh: 後卒于光祿大夫，贈秦州刺史，諡襄侯。

translations.literal: Later he died as Director of the Palace Library; posthumously made Governor of Qin Province with the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Director of the Palace Library; he was posthumously appointed Governor of Qin Province and given the posthumous title Marquis Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子景通襲，善事元叉，兼賂叉父繼。

translations.literal: His son Jingtong inherited; he cultivated Yuan Cha and also bribed Cha father Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingtong inherited the title; he curried favor with Yuan Cha and also bribed Cha father Ji.

sentences.zh: 繼為司空，引景通為掾。

translations.literal: When Ji became Minister of Works he brought Jingtong in as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji became Minister of Works he took Jingtong on as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 子郾襲，走關西。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited and fled to the Guanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title and fled west of the passes.

sentences.zh: 王世弼，京兆霸城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shibi was a man of Baling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shibi was a native of Baling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 姚泓之滅，其祖、父南遷。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, his grandfather and father moved south.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong fell, his grandfather and father migrated south.

sentences.zh: 世弼身長七尺八寸，魁岸有壯氣，善草隸書，好愛墳典。

translations.literal: Shibi stood seven feet eight inches tall, imposing and full of martial spirit; he was skilled in cursive and clerical script and loved the classics of the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi stood seven feet eight inches, broad-shouldered and martial in bearing; he excelled in cursive and clerical calligraphy and loved the classical canon.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為軍主，助戍壽春，遂與裴叔業同謀歸誠。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as a garrison commander, helped defend Shouchun, and then joined Pei Shuye in plotting to pledge loyalty to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as a garrison commander at Shouchun and then joined Pei Shuye in plotting to defect to Wei.

sentences.zh: 除南徐州刺史，封慎縣伯。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Southern Xu Province and enfeoffed as Baron of Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Southern Xu Province and enfeoffed as Baron of Shen.

sentences.zh: 後除東秦州刺史，政任于刑，為人所怨，有受納之響，為御史中尉李平所彈，會赦免。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Eastern Qin Province; his government relied on punishments, men resented him, and there was talk of bribe-taking; Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him, but he was pardoned by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Governor of Eastern Qin, where he ruled through harsh punishments and earned resentment; rumors of graft reached Censor-in-Chief Li Ping, who impeached him, but an amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 後為河北太守，有清稱。

translations.literal: Later, as Administrator of Hebei, he had a reputation for purity.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Administrator of Hebei, he won a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 再遷中山內史，加平北將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to Inner Governor of Zhongshan and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Inner Governor of Zhongshan with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 直閣元羅，領軍元叉弟也，曾過中山，謂曰：「二州刺史，翻復為郡，當恨恨耳。」

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Luo, younger brother of Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha, once passed through Zhongshan and said to him: "Twice a provincial governor, now back to a commandery—you must be full of resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Luo, younger brother of Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha, once visited Zhongshan and said, "Twice a provincial governor, now demoted to a commandery—you must be bitter about it."

sentences.zh: 世弼曰：「儀同之號，起自鄧騭，平北為郡，始在下官。」

translations.literal: Shibi replied: "The title of Honored Companion began with Deng Zhi; the post of General Who Pacifies the North as a commandery post began with this humble official."
translations.idiomatic: Shibi replied, "The title Honored Companion began with Deng Zhi; making General Who Pacifies the North a commandery-level post began with me."

sentences.zh: 卒，贈豫州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of Yu Province with the posthumous epithet Kang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously appointed Governor of Yu Province and given the posthumous epithet Kang.

sentences.zh: 長子會，汝陽太守。

translations.literal: His eldest son Hui was Administrator of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Hui served as Administrator of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 次子由，字茂道，好學有文才，尤善草隸書，性方厚，有名士風，又工摹書，為時人所服。

translations.literal: His second son You, style Maodao, loved learning and had literary talent; he was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script, upright and generous in nature with the air of a famous gentleman, and also adept at tracing copies—men of the time admired him.
translations.idiomatic: His second son You, style Maodao, was studious and gifted in letters, especially in cursive and clerical calligraphy; upright and generous, he had the bearing of a cultivated gentleman and was also skilled at facsimile copying—contemporaries held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 位東萊太守，罷郡寓居潁川。

translations.literal: He held the post of Administrator of Donglai; after leaving the commandery he lodged in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Administrator of Donglai; after leaving office he settled in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 天平初，元洪威構逆，大軍攻討，為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianping era Yuan Hongwei plotted rebellion; the great army attacked and suppressed him, and You was killed by disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianping era Yuan Hongwei rose in rebellion; when the imperial army moved against him, You was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 名流悼惜之。

translations.literal: Notables mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of reputation mourned his loss.

sentences.zh: 江悅之，字彥和，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Yuezhi, style Yanhe, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yuezhi, style Yanhe, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 七世祖統，晉散騎常侍，避劉、石之亂，南渡。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor Tong was Jin Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; fleeing the turmoil of the Liu and Shi regimes, he crossed south.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor Tong was Jin Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; fleeing the chaos of the Liu and Shi regimes, he crossed the Yangtze south.

sentences.zh: 祖興之，父范之，並為宋武所誅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xingzhi and father Fanzhi were both executed by Emperor Wu of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xingzhi and father Fanzhi were both put to death by Emperor Wu of Song.

sentences.zh: 悅之少孤，仕宋，曆諸王參軍。

translations.literal: Yuezhi was orphaned young; he served Song and successively held staff posts under various princes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi lost his father early; he served under Song as staff officer to several princes in turn.

sentences.zh: 好兵書，有將略，善待士，有部曲數百人。

translations.literal: He loved military writings, had a commander talent, treated gentlemen well, and had several hundred retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He studied military texts, showed real command insight, treated men of talent generously, and kept several hundred retainers.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，為後軍將軍，部曲稱眾，千有餘人。

translations.literal: In Qi he served as Rear Army General; his retainers were said to be numerous, more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as Rear Army General with a retinue said to number more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 梁初，以討滅劉季連功，進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang, for merit in campaigning to destroy Liu Jilian, he was advanced to the title General Who Crowns the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Liang he was promoted to General Who Crowns the Army for his part in suppressing Liu Jilian.

sentences.zh: 武興氐攻破白馬，進圖南鄭，悅之大破氐眾，還復白馬。

translations.literal: The Wuxing Di broke through Baima and advanced against Nanzheng; Yuezhi routed the Di forces in great defeat and recovered Baima.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Di broke through Baima and pressed toward Nanzheng; Yuezhi routed them and recovered Baima.

sentences.zh: 梁、秦二州刺史莊丘黑死，夏侯道遷與悅之及龐樹，軍主李忻榮、張元亮、士孫天與等謀以梁州內附。

translations.literal: When Liang and Qin Governor Zhuangqiu Hei died, Xiahou Daoqian with Yuezhi and Pang Shu, garrison commanders Li Xinrong, Zhang Yuanliang, Shisun Tianyu, and others plotted to bring Liang Province over to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When the joint Governor of Liang and Qin, Zhuangqiu Hei, died, Xiahou Daoqian joined Yuezhi, Pang Shu, and the garrison commanders Li Xinrong, Zhang Yuanliang, Shisun Tianyu, and others in a plot to surrender Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 梁華陽太守尹天寶率眾向州城，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: Liang Administrator of Huayang Yin Tianbao led troops toward the provincial seat and then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Tianbao, Liang Administrator of Huayang, marched on the provincial capital and laid siege to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 悅之晝夜督戰，會武興軍至，天寶敗。

translations.literal: Yuezhi directed fighting day and night; when the Wuxing army arrived, Tianbao was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi directed the fighting day and night; when the Wuxing army arrived, Tianbao was defeated.

sentences.zh: 道遷克全勳款，悅之實有力焉。

translations.literal: Daoqian accomplishment in fulfilling the merit and pledge owed much to Yuezhi real force.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqian success in completing the surrender owed a real debt to Yuezhi's efforts.

sentences.zh: 與道遷俱至洛陽。

translations.literal: Together with Daoqian he reached Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Luoyang together with Daoqian.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈梁州刺史，追封安平縣子，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Soon he died; posthumously made Governor of Liang Province, retroactively enfeoffed as Viscount of Anping, posthumous epithet Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was posthumously appointed Governor of Liang Province, ennobled as Viscount of Anping, and given the posthumous epithet Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 悅之二子，文遙、文遠。

translations.literal: Yuezhi had two sons: Wenyao and Wenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi had two sons, Wenyao and Wenyuan.

sentences.zh: 文遙少有大度，輕財好士，士多歸之。

translations.literal: Wenyao from youth had great breadth of mind, prized wealth lightly and loved gentlemen; many men attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyao was magnanimous from youth, generous with wealth and fond of talented men; many gathered to him.

sentences.zh: 道遷之圖楊靈珍，文遙奮劍請行，遂手斬靈珍。

translations.literal: In Daoqian plot against Yang Lingzhen, Wenyao seized his sword and asked to go; he then personally beheaded Lingzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Daoqian plotted against Yang Lingzhen, Wenyao drew his sword and volunteered; he cut Lingzhen down with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 襲父封，拜咸陽太守。

translations.literal: He inherited his father enfeoffment and was appointed Administrator of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father title and was appointed Administrator of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 勤於禮接，終日坐聽事。

translations.literal: Diligent in courteous reception, he sat in the audience hall all day.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in receiving visitors and sat in the audience hall from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 至者見之，假以恩顏，屏人密問，於是人所疾苦，大盜姓名，奸猾吏長，無不知悉。

translations.literal: Those who came to see him he met with a gracious face, then dismissed attendants and questioned in secret; thus the people grievances, great robbers names, and crafty officials and headmen—none escaped his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: He received every caller with a gracious face, then dismissed attendants and questioned them in private; soon he knew every local grievance, every major bandit by name, and every corrupt clerk and headman.

sentences.zh: 郡中震肅，奸劫息止，政為雍州諸郡之最。

translations.literal: Within the commandery all were awed into order; robbery and extortion ceased; his administration ranked first among the commanderies of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was awed into order, banditry ceased, and his administration ranked first in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 後為安州刺史，善於綏納，甚得物情。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of An Province, skilled at soothing and accepting the people, and greatly won their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Governor of An Province, he was skilled at winning people over and enjoyed deep popular support.

sentences.zh: 時杜洛周、葛榮等相繼叛逆，幽、燕已南悉沒，唯文遙介在群賊之外，孤城獨守，鳩集荒餘，且耕且戰，百姓皆樂為用。

translations.literal: At that time Du Luozhou, Ge Rong, and others rose in rebellion in succession; south of You and Yan all fell, yet Wenyao alone stood outside the mass of bandits, holding a lone city, gathering the scattered survivors, farming and fighting together—the common people all gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Luozhou, Ge Rong, and others rose in succession and everything south of You and Yan fell, Wenyao alone held out beyond the rebel hosts: a lone city, gathering refugees, farming and fighting by turns, with the people gladly following him.

sentences.zh: 卒官，長史許思祖等以文遙有遺愛，復推其子果行州事。

translations.literal: He died in office; Chief Clerk Xu Sizu and others, because Wenyao left enduring affection, again pushed his son Guo to conduct provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; Chief Clerk Xu Sizu and others, moved by the affection Wenyao had left behind, put his son Guo in charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 既攝州事，乃遣使奉表。

translations.literal: Once he took charge of provincial affairs he sent envoys with a memorial of submission.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guo took charge, he sent envoys with a memorial of loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 莊帝嘉之，除果通直散騎侍郎，行安州事。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang praised this and made Guo Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry in Direct Service, acting in An Province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang commended him and appointed Guo Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry in Direct Service, with acting authority over An Province.

sentences.zh: 既而賊勢轉盛，救援不接，果乃攜諸弟並率城人東奔高麗。

translations.literal: Soon the rebels strength grew; relief did not arrive; Guo then took his younger brothers and led the people of the city east to flee into Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel strength soon grew and no relief came; Guo took his brothers and led the townspeople east into Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 天平中，詔高麗送果等。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era an edict ordered Goguryeo to send Guo and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianping the court ordered Goguryeo to return Guo and his party.

sentences.zh: 元象中，乃得還朝。

translations.literal: In the Yuanxiang era he was able to return to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he finally returned to court.

sentences.zh: 文遠善騎射，勇於攻戰，以軍功位中散大夫、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Wenyuan was skilled in mounted archery, bold in attack and battle, and by military merit reached the posts of Palace Attendant and Dragon-Prancing General.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyuan was skilled in horsemanship and archery, bold in assault, and rose by military merit to Palace Attendant and Dragon-Prancing General.

sentences.zh: 淳於誕，字靈遠，其先太山博人也，後世居蜀漢，或家安固之桓陵縣。

translations.literal: Chun Yudan, style Lingyuan, was by ancestry a man of Bo in Mount Tai; later generations dwelt in Shu-Han, or the family was at Huanling County in Angu.
translations.idiomatic: Chun Yudan, style Lingyuan, traced his line to Bo in Mount Tai; later generations lived in Shu-Han, and the family was said to be from Huanling in Angu.

sentences.zh: 父興宗，齊南安太守。

translations.literal: His father Xingzong was Qi Administrator of Nanan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xingzong was Administrator of Nanan under Qi.

sentences.zh: 誕年十二，隨父向揚州。

translations.literal: At twelve Yudan followed his father toward Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he accompanied his father to Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 父于路為群盜所害，誕雖幼而哀感奮發，傾資結客，旬朔之內，遂得復仇。

translations.literal: His father was killed on the road by a band of robbers; though young, Yudan was moved by grief and roused to action, spent his wealth to gather clients, and within a fortnight achieved revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers killed his father on the road; though still a boy, Yudan grieved and roused himself, spent his fortune to gather followers, and within a fortnight had his revenge.

sentences.zh: 州裏之間，無不稱歎。

translations.literal: Throughout the district none failed to praise and marvel.
translations.idiomatic: All through the region praised his deed.

sentences.zh: 景明中，自漢中歸魏，陳伐蜀計，宣武嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the Jingming era he came from Hanzhong to Wei, presented a plan to campaign against Shu, and Emperor Xuanwu gladly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingming era he came north from Hanzhong, presented a plan to conquer Shu, and Emperor Xuanwu welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，王旅大舉，除驃騎將軍、都督、別部司馬，領鄉導統軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yan-chang the royal army marched in force; he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Area Commander, Separate-Department Major, and leader of native-guide command troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yan-chang, when the imperial army marched in force, he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, area commander, Separate-Department Major, and leader of the native-guide forces.

sentences.zh: 誕不願先受榮爵，乃固讓實官，止參戎號。

translations.literal: Yudan did not wish to receive honorary rank first; he firmly declined substantive office and took only a military title.
translations.idiomatic: Yudan refused to accept honorary rank before merit; he firmly declined substantive office and served only under a military title.

sentences.zh: 及奉辭之日，詔若克成都，即以益州許之。

translations.literal: On the day he took leave, an edict promised that if Chengdu were taken, Yi Province would be granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he set out, an edict promised that if Chengdu fell, Yi Province would be his.

sentences.zh: 師次晉壽，蜀人大震。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jinshou; the people of Shu were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jinshou, and Shu was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 屬宣武晏駕，不果而還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu passed away, the campaign came to nothing and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu died, the campaign was abandoned and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後以客例，起家羽林監。

translations.literal: Later, by the precedent for guests, he began his career as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a man who had come over from abroad, he entered service as Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 正光中，秦、隴反叛，詔誕為西南道軍司馬，與行台魏子建共參經略。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang Qin and Long rebelled; Yudan was ordered as Army Major on the Southwest Route and joined Mobile Headquarters Wei Zijian in planning.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang, when Qin and Long rose in revolt, Yudan was appointed Army Major on the Southwest Route to plan the campaign with Mobile Headquarters Wei Zijian.

sentences.zh: 時梁益州刺史蕭深猷遣將樊文熾蕭世澄等率眾數萬圍小劍戍。

translations.literal: At that time Liang Governor of Yi Province Xiao Shenyou sent generals Fan Wenchì, Xiao Shicheng, and others leading tens of thousands to besiege the garrison of Xiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Governor of Yi Province Xiao Shenyou then sent Fan Wenchì, Xiao Shicheng, and others at the head of tens of thousands to besiege the Xiaojian garrison.

sentences.zh: 子建遣誕勒兵馳赴，大敗之，禽世澄等十一人，文熾先走獲免。

translations.literal: Zijian sent Yudan to drive troops in haste to the rescue; he inflicted a great defeat, captured Shicheng and eleven others, while Wenchì fled first and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian sent Yudan at the head of a relief force; he routed the enemy, captured Shicheng and eleven others, while Wenchì fled early and escaped.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，子建以誕行華陽郡，帶白馬戍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang Zijian had Yudan act as Huayang commandery with concurrent charge of the Baima garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiaochang, Zijian put Yudan in charge of Huayang commandery and the Baima garrison.

sentences.zh: 後卒于東梁州刺史，贈益州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Later he died as Governor of Eastern Liang Province; posthumously made Governor of Yi Province with posthumous epithet Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Governor of Eastern Liang; he was posthumously appointed Governor of Yi Province with the epithet Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 沈文秀，字仲遠，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Wenxiu, style Zhongyuan, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenxiu, style Zhongyuan, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 伯父慶之，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Qingzhi has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Qingzhi is given a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 文秀仕宋，位青州刺史。

translations.literal: Wenxiu served Song and held the post of Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu served under Song as Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 和平六年，宋明帝殺其主子業，文秀與諸州推立子業弟子勳。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Heping, Emperor Ming of Song killed his lord Ziye; Wenxiu joined the provinces in enthroning Ziye's nephew Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Heping, Emperor Ming of Song murdered his lord Liu Ziye; Wenxiu and the provincial leaders enthroned Ziye's nephew Liu Zixun.

sentences.zh: 子勳敗，皇興初，文秀與崔道固俱以州降魏。

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated, at the beginning of Huangxing Wenxiu and Cui Daogu both surrendered their provinces to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun's defeat, at the start of Huangxing Wenxiu and Cui Daogu both surrendered their provinces to Wei.

sentences.zh: 宋遣其弟文景來諭之，文秀復歸宋，為刺史如故。

translations.literal: Song sent his younger brother Wenjing to persuade him; Wenxiu returned to Song and remained governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Song sent his younger brother Wenjing to win him back; Wenxiu rejoined Song and continued as governor.

sentences.zh: 後慕容白曜長驅至東陽，文秀始欲降，以軍人虜掠，遂有悔心，乃嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Later Murong Baiyao drove swiftly to Dongyang; Wenxiu at first wished to surrender, but when soldiers plundered captives he repented and walled the city for a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao swept on to Dongyang, Wenxiu at first meant to submit, but his troops began looting captives; he changed his mind and shut the gates for a last stand.

sentences.zh: 白曜既下曆城，乃並力攻討，自夏至春始克。

translations.literal: After Baiyao took Li city he gathered strength for the assault; from summer until spring of the next year it was finally taken.
translations.idiomatic: Once Baiyao had taken Li city, he concentrated his forces on the siege; from summer until the following spring the city finally fell.

sentences.zh: 文秀取所持節，衣冠儼然，坐於齋內。

translations.literal: Wenxiu took the tally he held, dressed in full regalia, and sat in his study.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu took up his credential staff, dressed in full court regalia, and sat upright in his private hall.

sentences.zh: 亂兵入曰：「文秀何在！」

translations.literal: Riotous soldiers entered and said, "Where is Wenxiu!"
translations.idiomatic: Riot troops burst in and shouted, "Where is Wenxiu!"

sentences.zh: 文秀曆聲曰：「身是！」

translations.literal: Wenxiu said in a ringing voice, "I am he!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu answered in a ringing voice, "I am he!"

sentences.zh: 執而裸送于白曜。

translations.literal: They seized him, stripped him bare, and sent him to Baiyao.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him, stripped him naked, and delivered him to Baiyao.

sentences.zh: 左右令拜，文秀曰：「各二國大臣，無相拜禮。」

translations.literal: Attendants ordered him to bow; Wenxiu said, "We are each ministers of our respective states—there is no mutual bowing between us."
translations.idiomatic: His escort ordered him to bow. Wenxiu said, "We are ministers of two states—there is no bowing between us."

sentences.zh: 白曜忿之，因至撾撻。

translations.literal: Baiyao was enraged and had him beaten with cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao flew into a rage and had him beaten with clubs.

sentences.zh: 後還其衣，為之設饌，與長史房天樂、司馬沈嵩等鎖送京師，面縛數罪，宥死，待為下客，給以粗衣蔬食。

translations.literal: Later his clothes were returned, a feast was set for him, and with Chief Clerk Fang Tianle, Major Shen Song, and others he was shackled and escorted to the capital; sins were read to his face, his life was spared, he was kept as a low guest, and given coarse clothes and plain food.
translations.idiomatic: Later his clothes were restored and a meal set before him. With Chief Clerk Fang Tianle, Major Shen Song, and others he was shackled and sent to the capital, his crimes enumerated to his face; his life was spared, he was kept as a humble guest, and given coarse clothes and plain fare.

sentences.zh: 獻文重其節義，稍亦嘉禮之，拜外都下大夫。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen esteemed his integrity and gradually treated him with honor, appointing him Junior Grand Master of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianwen respected his steadfastness and gradually honored him, appointing him Junior Grand Master of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，遷外都大官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was promoted to Grand Provisioner of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he was promoted to Grand Provisioner of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉其忠於其國，賜絹彩二百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen praised his loyalty to his state and bestowed two hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen praised his loyalty to his former state and granted him two hundred bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 後為南征都將，臨發，賜以戎服。

translations.literal: Later he became commander of the southern expedition; on the eve of departure he was given military dress.
translations.idiomatic: He later became commander of the southern expedition; on the eve of departure he was presented with military dress.

sentences.zh: 除懷州刺史，假吳郡公。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Huai Province with the acting title Marquis of Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Huai Province with the acting title Marquis of Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 守清貧而政寬，不能禁止盜賊。

translations.literal: He kept to poverty and was lenient in governance, and could not suppress bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in poverty and ruled leniently, and could not suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 大興水田，於公私頗有利益。

translations.literal: He greatly promoted paddy fields, to considerable benefit for public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded irrigated rice fields, to the considerable benefit of public and private coffers alike.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 子保沖，後為徐州冠軍長史，坐據連口退敗，有司處之死刑。

translations.literal: His son Baochong later served as Champion Major of Xu Province; for holding Lian mouth and retreating in defeat, the authorities sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baochong later served as Champion Major of Xu Province; for holding Lian Pass and retreating in defeat, the authorities sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 孝文詔：「保沖，文秀之子，可特原命，配洛陽作部終身。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict: "Baochong, son of Wenxiu, may specially be spared his life and assigned to the Luoyang artisans for life."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen decreed: "Baochong, Wenxiu's son, is specially spared and assigned to the Luoyang artisans for life."

sentences.zh: 宣武時，卒于下邳太守。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he died as Governor of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he died while serving as Governor of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 房天樂者，清河人，滑稽多智。

translations.literal: Fang Tianle was a man of Qinghe, witty and full of resource.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Tianle, a native of Qinghe, was quick-witted and endlessly resourceful.

sentences.zh: 文秀板為長史，督齊郡，州府事一以委之。

translations.literal: Wenxiu appointed him Chief Clerk and overseer of Qi commandery; all prefectural and provincial affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu appointed him Chief Clerk with oversight of Qi commandery and entrusted him with every matter of the province and prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒于京師。

translations.literal: He died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 弟子嘉慶，漁陽太守。

translations.literal: His nephew Jiaqing became Governor of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Jiaqing became Governor of Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 張讜，字處言，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dang, style Chuyan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang, style Chuyan, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 六世祖弘，晉長秋卿。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Hong was Jin Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Hong served Jin as Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 父華，慕容超左僕射。

translations.literal: His father Hua was Left Vice Director of the Secretariat under Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hua was Left Vice Director of the Secretariat under Murong Chao.

sentences.zh: 讜仕宋，位東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Dang served Song as Governor of Eastern Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Dang served under Song as Governor of Eastern Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 及平徐、兗，讜乃歸順于尉元，亦表授東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xu and Yan were pacified, Dang submitted to Yuwu Yuan and was also appointed Governor of Eastern Xu by imperial table.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu and Yan were pacified, Dang submitted to Yuwu Yuan and was confirmed by imperial appointment as Governor of Eastern Xu.

sentences.zh: 遣中書侍郎高閭與讜對為刺史。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Lu was sent to serve as governor opposite Dang.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat Gao Lu was sent to serve as co-governor alongside Dang.

sentences.zh: 後至京師，禮遇亞于薛、畢，賜爵平陸侯。

translations.literal: Later when he reached the capital, his reception ranked below Xue and Bi; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: When he later reached the capital, his reception ranked just below Xue and Bi; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 讜性開通，篤於接恤，青、齊之士，雖疏族末姻，咸相敬視。

translations.literal: Dang was open and generous, devoted to receiving and succoring others; gentry of Qing and Qi, though distant kin or peripheral affines, all treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: Dang was open-handed and devoted to hospitality; gentlemen of Qing and Qi, however distant the kinship, all treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 李敷、李䐶等寵要勢家，亦推懷陳款，無所顧避。

translations.literal: Li Fu, Li Can, and other favorites of powerful houses also offered him their open regard without holding back.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu, Li Can, and other favorites of the great houses likewise opened their hearts to him without reserve.

sentences.zh: 畢眾敬等皆敬重之，高允之徒亦相器待。

translations.literal: Bi Zhongjing and others all held him in esteem; Gao Yun and his circle likewise valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhongjing and others all esteemed him; Gao Yun and his circle valued him as well.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史，諡康侯。

translations.literal: At his death he was posthumously made Governor of Qing Province with the posthumous title Marquis Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously appointed Governor of Qing Province with the epithet Marquis Kang.

sentences.zh: 子敬伯，求致父喪，出葬冀州清河舊墓，久不被許，停柩在家積五六年。

translations.literal: His son Jingbo asked to transport his father's coffin to bury him in the old tomb in Qinghe, Jizhou; permission was long withheld and the coffin stayed at home for five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingbo petitioned to take his father's coffin home for burial in the old family tomb in Qinghe, Jizhou; permission was long denied, and the coffin lay at home for five or six years.

sentences.zh: 第四子敬叔，先在徐州，初聞父喪，不欲奔赴，而規南叛，為徐州所勒送。

translations.literal: The fourth son Jingshu was earlier in Xu Province; when he first heard of his father's death he did not wish to hurry to the funeral but plotted to rebel southward, and Xu Province compelled him to be escorted back.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth son Jingshu was then in Xu Province; when he first heard of his father's death he refused to hurry home and plotted to defect south, whereupon Xu Province seized him and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 至乃自理，後得襲父爵。

translations.literal: On arrival he explained himself and later succeeded to his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he cleared himself and later succeeded to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 敬伯自以隨父歸國功，賜爵昌安侯，出為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Jingbo, citing his merit in following his father in submitting to the state, was granted the title Marquis of Chang'an and sent out as Governor of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbo, citing his merit in following his father to submit to Wei, was granted the title Marquis of Chang'an and appointed Governor of Leling.

sentences.zh: 敬叔，武邑太守。

translations.literal: Jingshu became Governor of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshu became Governor of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 父喪得葬舊墓，還屬清河。

translations.literal: When the father's funeral was permitted burial in the old tomb, they returned to Qinghe jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Once the father was buried in the old tomb, the family returned to Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 初，讜兄弟十人。

translations.literal: Earlier Dang had ten brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Dang had ten brothers in all.

sentences.zh: 兄忠，字處順，在南為合鄉令。

translations.literal: Elder brother Zhong, style Chushun, on the southern side was magistrate of Hexiang.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhong, style Chushun, had served the south as magistrate of Hexiang.

sentences.zh: 歸降，賜爵新昌侯。

translations.literal: On submitting he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: After he submitted, he was granted the title Marquis of Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 卒于新興太守，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Xinxing and was posthumously made Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Governor of Xinxing and was posthumously appointed Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 讜妻皇甫氏被掠，賜中官為婢，皇甫遂詐癡，不能梳沐。

translations.literal: Dang's wife Lady Huangfu was seized and given to a palace eunuch as a maidservant; Huangfu then feigned madness and could not wash or comb her hair.
translations.idiomatic: Dang's wife, Lady Huangfu, was seized and given to a palace eunuch as a maidservant; she then feigned madness and would not wash or comb her hair.

sentences.zh: 後讜為宋冀州長史，因貨千餘匹，購求皇甫。

translations.literal: Later when Dang was Song Major of Ji Province, he used more than a thousand bolts of goods to purchase and seek Lady Huangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Dang was Song Chief of staff for Ji Province, he spent more than a thousand bolts of goods to buy her back.

sentences.zh: 文成怪其納財之多，引見之，時皇甫年垂六十矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng marveled at the great sum paid and summoned her; Lady Huangfu was then nearly sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng marveled at the vast sum and summoned her for an audience; Lady Huangfu was then nearly sixty.

sentences.zh: 文成曰：「南人奇好，能重室家之義。

translations.literal: Wencheng said, "Southerners have strange tastes and can honor the meaning of household and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Wencheng said, "Southerners have peculiar tastes—they can honor the bonds of home and wife.

sentences.zh: 此老母復何所任，乃能如此致費也。」

translations.literal: What use is this old woman that he could spend so lavishly!"
translations.idiomatic: What can this old woman still do for him that he would spend so lavishly!"

sentences.zh: 皇甫氏歸，讜令諸妾境上奉迎。

translations.literal: When Lady Huangfu returned, Dang ordered all his concubines to welcome her at the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Huangfu returned, Dang ordered all his concubines to meet her at the border.

sentences.zh: 數年卒。

translations.literal: Several years later she died.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later she died.

sentences.zh: 後十年而讜入魏。

translations.literal: Ten years later Dang entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later Dang himself entered Wei.

sentences.zh: 讜兄子安世，正始中，自梁漢同夏侯道遷歸款，為客積年，出為東河間太守。

translations.literal: Dang's brother's son Anshi, in Zhengshi, from Liang and Han with Xiahou Daoqian submitted his allegiance; he was a guest for many years and then went out as Governor of Eastern Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Dang's nephew Anshi, in Zhengshi, came over from Liang and Han with Xiahou Daoqian; he remained a guest for many years, then was appointed Governor of Eastern Hejian.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 李苗，字子宣，梓潼涪人也。

translations.literal: Li Miao, style Zixuan, was a man of Fu in Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao, style Zixuan, was a native of Fu in Zitong.

sentences.zh: 父膺，梁太僕卿。

translations.literal: His father Ying was Liang Grand Master of Palace Steeds.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ying was Liang Grand Master of Palace Steeds.

sentences.zh: 苗出後叔父畎。

translations.literal: Miao was adopted out to his uncle Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Miao was given in adoption to his uncle Qian.

sentences.zh: 畎為梁州刺史，大著威名。

translations.literal: Qian was Liang Governor of Liang Province and won great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Qian served Liang as Governor of Liang Province and won great renown.

sentences.zh: 王足之伐蜀，梁武命畎拒足于涪，許其益州。

translations.literal: When Wang Zu campaigned against Shu, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered Qian to resist Zu at Fu and promised him Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zu invaded Shu, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered Qian to hold Zu at Fu and promised him Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 及足退，梁武遂改授。

translations.literal: When Zu withdrew, Emperor Wu of Liang changed the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu withdrew, Emperor Wu of Liang revoked the promise and reassigned the post.

sentences.zh: 畎怒，將有異圖，事發被害。

translations.literal: Qian was furious and was about to carry out a rebellious plot; the affair came out and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was enraged and plotted rebellion; the plot was exposed and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 苗年十五，有報雪志。

translations.literal: Miao at fifteen had the resolve to avenge and settle the score.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Miao swore to avenge his uncle.

sentences.zh: 延昌中歸魏，仍陳圖蜀計。

translations.literal: In Yan-chang he submitted to Wei and forthwith presented a plan to take Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yan-chang he defected to Wei and at once presented a plan to conquer Shu.

sentences.zh: 大將軍高肇西伐，詔假苗龍驤將軍鄉導。

translations.literal: The great general Gao Zhao campaigned west; Miao was ordered acting General of Dragon Cavalry as native guide.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Gao Zhao marched west, Miao was appointed acting General of Dragon Cavalry to guide the army.

sentences.zh: 次晉壽，宣武宴駕，班師。

translations.literal: The army halted at Jinshou; Emperor Xuanwu died and the troops were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Jinshou; when Emperor Xuanwu died, the campaign was called off and the troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後以客例，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later by the precedent for guests he was made Extraordinary Cadet Within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a man who had come over from abroad, he was appointed Extraordinary Cadet Within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 苗有文武才幹，以大功不就，家恥未雪，常懷慷慨。

translations.literal: Miao had civil and military talent; because the great achievement was unfulfilled and family shame unsettled, he often brooded in generous indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Miao possessed both civil and military talent; the great enterprise had failed and family shame remained unavenged, and he burned with frustrated ambition.

sentences.zh: 乃上書陳平定江南之計，其文理甚切于時。

translations.literal: He then memorialized setting forth a plan to pacify the Jiangnan; the reasoning was very apt to the time.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized with a plan to pacify the south; the argument was urgent and apt to the moment.

sentences.zh: 明帝幼沖，無遠略之意，竟不能納。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was young and inexperienced and lacked far-reaching intent, and in the end could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was still a child and lacked long-range vision; in the end he could not adopt the plan.

sentences.zh: 正光末，三秦反叛，侵及三輔。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang the three Qins rebelled and the disturbance reached the three auxiliaries.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang the three Qin provinces rebelled and the turmoil spread to the capital region.

sentences.zh: 時承平既久，人不習戰。

translations.literal: Peace had long endured and men were unused to war.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted so long that men had forgotten how to fight.

sentences.zh: 苗以隴兵強悍，且群聚無資，乃上書以為：「食少兵精，利於速戰；

translations.literal: Miao held that Long troops were fierce and had gathered without supplies, and memorialized: "Little food and elite troops favor swift battle;
translations.idiomatic: Miao judged that the Long troops were fierce but had massed without provisions, and memorialized: "Scant food and elite troops favor swift battle;

sentences.zh: 糧多卒眾，事宜持久。

translations.literal: Much grain and many soldiers call for protracted campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: Abundant grain and a host of soldiers call for a war of attrition.

sentences.zh: 今隴賊倡狂，非有素蓄，雖據兩城，本無德義，其勢在於疾攻，日有降納，遲則人情離阻，坐受崩潰。

translations.literal: The Long rebels are wildly arrogant without longstanding stores; though they hold two cities they have no virtue or justice—their momentum lies in pressing attack, with surrenders daily; delay will estrange men's hearts and they will collapse of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The Long rebels are raging without deep reserves; though they hold two cities they have no moral hold. Press the attack and surrenders will come day by day; delay will estrange their followers and they will collapse on their own.

sentences.zh: 夫飆至風起，逆者求萬一之功；

translations.literal: When the whirlwind rises, rebels seek a fraction of success;
translations.idiomatic: When the storm rises, rebels gamble on a stroke of luck;

sentences.zh: 高壁深壘，王師有全制之策。

translations.literal: with high walls and deep ramparts, the royal army has the strategy of complete control.
translations.idiomatic: behind high walls and deep ramparts, the imperial army can dictate the terms of victory.

sentences.zh: 今且宜勒大將，深溝高壘，堅守勿戰。

translations.literal: For now the great generals should be ordered to dig deep moats and raise high ramparts and hold fast without giving battle.
translations.idiomatic: For now order the commanders to dig deep trenches, raise high ramparts, and hold fast without giving battle.

sentences.zh: 別命偏師，精卒數千，出麥積崖以襲其後，則氵幵、岐之下，群妖自散。」

translations.literal: Send a separate force of several thousand elite soldiers out from Maiji cliff to strike their rear, then below the Qian and Qi rivers the rebel hosts will scatter of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Send a detached column of several thousand picked troops from Maiji Cliff to strike their rear, and the rebel hosts below the Qian and Qi will scatter of themselves."

sentences.zh: 於是詔苗為統軍，與別將淳于誕出梁、益，隸行台魏子建。

translations.literal: Thereupon Miao was ordered as commander-in-chief; with Separate General Chun Yudan he marched from Liang and Yi, subordinate to Mobile Headquarters Wei Zijian.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Miao was appointed commander-in-chief; with Separate General Chun Yudan he marched from Liang and Yi under Mobile Headquarters Wei Zijian.

sentences.zh: 子建以苗為郎中，仍領統軍，深見知待。

translations.literal: Zijian made Miao Gentleman Within and he still led the command army, and was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian made him a palace gentleman while he still led the command army, and treated him with deep trust.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，兼尚書左丞，為西北道行台，與大都督宗正珍孫討汾、絳蜀賊，平之。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang he was concurrently Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat, Northwest Route Mobile Headquarters, and with Area Commander-in-Chief Zongzheng Zhensun suppressed the bandits of Fen and Jiang in Shu; they pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang he served concurrently as Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and Northwest Route Mobile Headquarters; with Area Commander Zongzheng Zhensun he suppressed the Shu rebels of Fen and Jiang and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 及殺爾朱榮，榮從弟世隆擁部曲還逼都邑。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong was killed, Rong's younger cousin Shilong led his troops back to press the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Erzhu Rong was killed, his younger cousin Shilong led his private army back to threaten the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝莊幸大夏門，集群臣博議，百僚計無所出。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang took refuge at the Great Summer Gate and assembled the ministers for wide counsel; the hundred officials had no plan to offer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang took refuge at the Great Summer Gate and summoned the ministers for counsel; the bureaucracy could offer no plan.

sentences.zh: 苗獨奮衣起曰：「今朝廷有不測之危，正是忠臣烈士效節之時，請以一旅之眾，為陛下徑斷河梁。」

translations.literal: Miao alone flung his robe and rose, saying, "The court now faces unforeseen peril—it is the hour for loyal ministers and martyrs to give their utmost; I ask for a single brigade to cut the river bridge for Your Majesty at a stroke."
translations.idiomatic: Miao alone flung off his robe and stood. "The court faces sudden peril—this is the hour for loyal ministers to prove themselves. Grant me a single brigade and I will cut the river bridge for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 莊帝壯而許焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang was inspired and assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang was stirred and assented.

sentences.zh: 苗乃募人于馬渚上流，以師夜下。

translations.literal: Miao then recruited men upstream at Maze ford and led the troops down by night.
translations.idiomatic: Miao recruited men upstream at Maze Ford and led his force downriver by night.

sentences.zh: 去橋數里，放火燒船，俄然橋絕，賊沒水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Several li from the bridge they set fire to the boats; presently the bridge broke and many rebels drowned.
translations.idiomatic: A few li from the bridge they set the boats ablaze; the bridge collapsed at once and a great host of rebels drowned.

sentences.zh: 官軍不至，賊乃涉水與苗死鬥，眾寡不敵，苗浮河而沒。

translations.literal: The government army did not arrive; the rebels waded the river and fought Miao to the death; outnumbered, Miao floated on the river and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops never came; the rebels waded the river and fought Miao to the death. Outnumbered, he was swept away and drowned.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，哀傷久之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grieved for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news, he grieved for a long while.

sentences.zh: 贈都督、梁州刺史、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、河陽縣侯，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Area Commander, Governor of Liang Province, General of Cavalry and Chariots, equal in the Three Dignities with a fief as Marquis of Heyang, posthumous epithet Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Area Commander, Governor of Liang Province, General of Cavalry and Chariots, equal in rank to the Three Excellencies, and Marquis of Heyang, with the epithet Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 苗少有節操，志尚功名。

translations.literal: Miao from youth had integrity, his ambition set on merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Miao had integrity and hungered for glory.

sentences.zh: 每讀《蜀書》，見魏延請出長安，諸葛不許，歎息謂亮無奇計。

translations.literal: Whenever he read the History of Shu and saw Wei Yan ask to march out toward Chang'an while Zhuge refused, he would sigh that Liang had no extraordinary stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read the History of Shu and saw Wei Yan ask to strike out toward Chang'an while Zhuge Liang refused, he would sigh that Liang had no daring stratagem.

sentences.zh: 及覽《周瑜傳》，未曾不嗟咨絕倒。

translations.literal: And when he read the biography of Zhou Yu, he never failed to sigh and gasp in amazement.
translations.idiomatic: When he read the biography of Zhou Yu, he never failed to sigh in wonder.

sentences.zh: 太保城陽王徽、司徒臨淮王彧並重之。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Chengyang Hui and Minister over the Masses Prince of Linhuai Yu both valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Prince Hui of Chengyang and Minister over the Masses Prince Yu of Linhuai both held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 二王頗或不穆，苗每諫責。

translations.literal: The two princes were often ill-disposed toward each other; Miao always admonished and reproved them.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes were often at odds; Miao always admonished them.

sentences.zh: 徽寵勢隆極，猜忌彌甚，苗謂人曰：「城陽蜂目豺聲，今轉彰矣！」

translations.literal: As Hui's favor and power reached their peak his suspicion grew ever stronger; Miao said to others, "The Prince of Chengyang has the eyes of a wasp and the voice of a jackal—now it shows all the more plainly!"
translations.idiomatic: As Hui's favor and power reached their height his suspicion deepened; Miao said to others, "The Prince of Chengyang has a wasp's eyes and a jackal's voice—and now it shows plain as day!"

sentences.zh: 解鼓琴，善屬文詠，工尺牘之敏，當世罕及。

translations.literal: He understood the drum-zither, excelled at literary verse, and handled letters with a quick hand—rare in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the zither, wrote verse with ease, and drafted correspondence with a speed seldom matched in his generation.

sentences.zh: 死之日，朝野悲壯之。

translations.literal: On the day he died, court and countryside mourned him as a man of tragic valor.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, court and country mourned a hero.

sentences.zh: 及帝幽崩，世隆入洛，主者追苗贈封，以白世隆。

translations.literal: When the emperor died in confinement, Shilong entered Luoyang; the responsible officials pursued Miao's posthumous enfeoffment and reported it to Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor died in captivity, Shilong entered Luoyang; the authorities sought to confirm Miao's posthumous honors and informed Shilong.

sentences.zh: 世隆曰：「吾爾時群議，更三日便欲大縱兵士，燒燔都邑，任其采掠。

translations.literal: Shilong said, "At that time our council agreed that in three more days we would unleash the troops, burn the capital, and let them plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: Shilong said, "In council we had agreed that in three more days I would unleash my troops, burn the capital, and let them loot as they pleased.

sentences.zh: 賴苗，京師獲全。

translations.literal: Thanks to Miao, the capital was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: It was thanks to Miao that the capital was spared.

sentences.zh: 天下之善一也，不宜追之。」
