translations.literal: The good of the realm is one—posthumous honors should not be pursued."
translations.idiomatic: The good of the realm is one and the same—there is no need to pursue posthumous honors for him."

sentences.zh: 子曇襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yan succeeded to the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 劉藻，字彥先，廣平易陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zao, style Yansian, was a man of Yiyang in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao, style Yansian, was a native of Yiyang in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 六世祖遐，從晉元帝南渡。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Xia followed Emperor Yuan of Jin south across the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Xia followed Emperor Yuan of Jin when he crossed south.

sentences.zh: 父宗之，宋廬江太守。

translations.literal: His father Zongzhi was Song Governor of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zongzhi served Song as Governor of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 藻涉獵群籍，美談笑，善與人交，飲酒至一石不亂。

translations.literal: Zao ranged widely through the classics, was skilled at witty talk, knew how to win friends, and could drink a hu of wine without losing his composure.
translations.idiomatic: Zao ranged widely through the classics, delighted in witty conversation, made friends easily, and could drink a hu of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 太安中，與姊夫李嶷俱來歸魏，賜爵易陽子。

translations.literal: In Tai'an he came over to Wei with his brother-in-law Li Yao and was granted the title Viscount of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an he defected to Wei with his brother-in-law Li Yao and was granted the title Viscount of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 擢拜南部主書，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Principal Clerk of the Southern Department and was said to perform his duties well.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Principal Clerk of the Southern Department and was praised as thoroughly competent.

sentences.zh: 時北地諸羌，恃險作亂，前後宰守不能制。

translations.literal: At that time the Qiang of Beidi, trusting in rugged terrain, rose in revolt; successive governors could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Qiang of Beidi, trusting in the rugged terrain, rose in revolt, and governor after governor failed to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷患之，以藻為北地太守。

translations.literal: The court was troubled and appointed Zao Governor of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: The court was alarmed and appointed Zao Governor of Beidi.

sentences.zh: 藻推誠布信，諸羌咸來歸款，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: Zao spread sincerity and faith; all the Qiang came to submit, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Zao won them with sincerity and good faith; the Qiang all came to submit, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 雍州人王叔保等三百人表乞藻為騃奴戍主，詔曰：「選曹已用人，藻有惠政，自宜他敘。」

translations.literal: Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao petitioned that Zao be made garrison commander of Sainu; the edict read, "The Selection Office has already filled the post; Zao has shown benevolent rule and should receive another appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred men of Yong Province led by Wang Shubao petitioned to make Zao garrison commander of Sainu; the edict read, "The Selection Office has already appointed someone else; Zao has governed with kindness and should be given another post."

sentences.zh: 在任八年，遷離城鎮將。

translations.literal: After eight years in office he was transferred to Garrison Commander of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in office he was transferred to Garrison Commander of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 太和中改鎮為岐州，以藻為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: In Taihe the garrison was converted to Qi Province and Zao was made its governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe the garrison was converted to Qi Province and Zao was appointed its governor.

sentences.zh: 轉秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 秦人恃險，率多粗暴，或拒課輸，或害吏長，自前守宰，皆遙領，不入郡縣。

translations.literal: The people of Qin, trusting in difficult terrain, were for the most part fierce and rough; some refused taxes, some killed officials; previous governors had all ruled from afar without entering the counties.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin, trusting in the difficult terrain, were mostly fierce and rough; some refused taxes, some killed officials, and previous governors had all ruled from afar without ever entering the counties.

sentences.zh: 藻開示恩信，誅戮豪橫，羌、氐憚之，守宰於是始得居其舊所。

translations.literal: Zao proclaimed kindness and faith and executed violent overlords; Qiang and Di feared him, and governors thereafter could reside in their proper seats.
translations.idiomatic: Zao proclaimed kindness and faith and executed the violent overlords; the Qiang and Di feared him, and governors at last could take up their proper seats.

sentences.zh: 遇車駕南伐，以藻為東道都督。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zao was made Eastern Route commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south on campaign, Zao was made commander-in-chief of the eastern route.

sentences.zh: 秦人紛擾，詔藻還州，人情乃定。

translations.literal: The people of Qin grew turbulent; he was ordered back to his province and popular feeling settled.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin grew restless; he was ordered back to his province and popular feeling settled.

sentences.zh: 仍與安南元英征漢中，破賊軍，長驅至南鄭，垂平梁州，奉詔還軍，乃不果克。

translations.literal: He then joined Pacifier of the South Yuan Ying in the campaign against Hanzhong, defeated the rebel armies, swept on to Nanzheng, and was on the verge of pacifying Liang Province when an order recalled the army, so the conquest was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Pacifier of the South Yuan Ying in the Hanzhong campaign, routed the rebel armies, and swept on to Nanzheng, nearly pacifying Liang Province, until an imperial order recalled the army and the conquest went uncompleted.

sentences.zh: 後車駕南伐，以藻為征虜將軍，督統軍高聰等四軍為東道別將，辭于洛水之南。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor marched south on campaign, Zao was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and supervised the four armies of Commander Gao Cong and others as separate commander of the eastern route, taking leave south of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the southern campaign, Zao was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and, supervising the four armies under Commander Gao Cong and others, served as separate commander of the eastern route and took leave south of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：「與卿石頭相見。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen said, "I shall see you at Stone Citadel."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "I shall see you at Stone Citadel."

sentences.zh: 藻對曰：「臣雖才非古人，庶亦不留賊虜而遺陛下。

translations.literal: Zao replied, "Though my talent falls short of the ancients, I hope at least not to leave the enemy uncaptured for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Zao replied, "Though my talent falls short of the ancients, I hope at least not to leave the enemy standing for Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 輒當釃曲阿之酒以待百官。」

translations.literal: I shall at once broach the wine of Qu'e to await the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: I shall at once broach the wine of Qu'e to toast the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「今未至曲阿，且以河東數石賜卿。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and said, "We have not yet reached Qu'e—for now take several shi of Hedong wine as my gift."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "We have not yet reached Qu'e—for now take several shi of Hedong wine as my gift."

sentences.zh: 後與高聰等戰敗，俱徙平州。

translations.literal: Later he was defeated along with Gao Cong and others, and all were relocated to Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was defeated along with Gao Cong and the others, and all were banished to Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 景明初，宣武追錄舊功，拜藻為太尉司馬。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingming, Emperor Xuanwu recalled his former merit and appointed Zao Grand Marshal of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingming, Emperor Xuanwu recalled his former service and appointed him Grand Marshal of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子紹珍，無他才用，善附會，好飲酒。

translations.literal: His son Shaozhen had no other talent—he knew how to curry favor and loved drink.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaozhen had no other talent; he knew how to curry favor and loved his wine.

sentences.zh: 結托劉騰，啟為其國郎中令，襲子爵。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Liu Teng, who had him made Director of the Household of Liu's fief, and he inherited the viscountcy.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself to Liu Teng, who had him made Director of the Household of Liu's fief, and he inherited the viscountcy.

sentences.zh: 永安中，曆河北、黎陽二郡太守，所在無政績。

translations.literal: In Yong'an he served successively as governor of Hebei and Liyang; in neither post did he achieve anything.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an he served successively as governor of Hebei and Liyang, achieving nothing in either post.

sentences.zh: 天平中，坐子洪業入於關中，率眾侵擾，伏法。

translations.literal: In Tianping, because his son Hongye entered Guanzhong and led troops in raids, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping, because his son Hongye entered Guanzhong and led troops in raids, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 傅永，字脩期，清河人也。

translations.literal: Fu Yong, style Xiuqi, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yong, style Xiuqi, was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 幼隨叔父洪仲與張幸自青州入魏，尋復南奔。

translations.literal: As a youth he followed his uncle Hongzhong and Zhang Xing from Qing Province into Wei, then soon fled south again.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he followed his uncle Hongzhong and Zhang Xing from Qing Province into Wei, then soon fled south again.

sentences.zh: 有氣幹，拳勇過人，能手執鞍橋，倒立馳騁。

translations.literal: He had force of spirit; his fists and courage surpassed others—he could grip the saddle bow and ride head-down at full gallop.
translations.idiomatic: He had force of spirit and fists that surpassed other men—he could grip the saddle bow and ride upside down at full gallop.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，有友人與之書而不能答，請洪仲，洪仲深讓之而不為報。

translations.literal: In his twenties a friend wrote to him and he could not reply; he asked Hongzhong, who rebuked him severely and would not answer for him.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties a friend wrote to him and he could not reply; he asked Hongzhong, who rebuked him sharply and refused to answer for him.

sentences.zh: 永乃發憤讀書，涉獵經史，兼有才幹。

translations.literal: Yong then threw himself into study, ranged through the classics and histories, and gained talent in both civil and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then threw himself into study, ranged through the classics and histories, and proved gifted in both civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 為崔道固城局參軍，與道固俱降，入為平齊百姓。

translations.literal: He served Cui Daogu as garrison bureau aide; he surrendered with Daogu and entered Wei as a commoner of the Pacified Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He served Cui Daogu as garrison bureau aide; he surrendered with Daogu and entered Wei as a commoner of the Pacified Qi.

sentences.zh: 父母並老，饑寒十數年，賴其強於人事，戮力傭丐，得以存立。

translations.literal: Both parents were old; for more than ten years in hunger and cold he relied on his skill at dealing with the world, toiling together at hired labor and begging, barely to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Both parents were old; for more than ten years of hunger and cold he relied on his knack for getting by, toiling at hired labor and begging together, barely keeping them alive.

sentences.zh: 晚為奉禮郎，詣長安拜文明太后父燕宣王廟，賜爵貝丘男，除中書博士。

translations.literal: Late he became Court Gentleman of Ceremonies, went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of Empress Wumingwen's father Prince Yan Xuan, was granted the title Baron of Beiqiu, and made Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he became Court Gentleman of Ceremonies, went to Chang'an to worship at the temple of Empress Wumingwen's father Prince Yan Xuan, was granted the title Baron of Beiqiu, and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王肅之為豫州，又以永為王肅平南長史。

translations.literal: When Wang Su became governor of Yu Province, Yong was again made Wang Su's Chief of Staff for Pacifying the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su became governor of Yu Province, Yong was again made his Chief of Staff for Pacifying the South.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧慮肅難信，言于孝文。

translations.literal: Prince Xi'an of Xianyang feared Su was hard to trust and spoke to Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi'an of Xianyang feared Su was not to be trusted and spoke to Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 曰：「已選傅脩期為其長史，雖威儀不足，而文武有餘矣。」

translations.literal: He said, "I have already chosen Fu Xiuqi as his chief of staff; though his formal bearing falls short, in civil and military matters he has plenty to spare."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I have already chosen Fu Xiuqi as his chief of staff; though his formal bearing falls short, in civil and military matters he has more than enough to spare."

sentences.zh: 肅以永宿士，禮之甚厚；

translations.literal: Su treated Yong, an old companion, with the greatest courtesy;
translations.idiomatic: Su treated Yong, an old companion, with the greatest courtesy;

sentences.zh: 永亦以肅為帝眷遇，盡心事之，情義至穆。

translations.literal: Yong too, knowing Su enjoyed the emperor's favor, served him with all his heart—their bond was deepest harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Yong too, knowing Su enjoyed the emperor's favor, served him with all his heart, and their bond was one of deepest harmony.

sentences.zh: 齊將魯康祖、趙公政侵豫州之太倉口，肅令永擊之。

translations.literal: Qi generals Lu Kangzu and Zhao Gongzheng raided the Grand Granary mouth of Yu Province; Su ordered Yong to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi generals Lu Kangzu and Zhao Gongzheng raided the Grand Granary mouth of Yu Province; Su ordered Yong to strike them.

sentences.zh: 永量吳、楚兵好以斫營為事，又賊若夜來，必於渡淮之所，以火記其淺處。

translations.literal: Yong judged that Wu and Chu troops loved night raids on camps, and that if the enemy came by night they would mark shallow spots on the Huai crossing with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yong judged that Wu and Chu troops loved night raids on camps, and that if the enemy came by night they would mark the shallow fords on the Huai with fire.

sentences.zh: 永既設伏，仍密令人以瓠盛火，渡南岸，當深處置之，教云：「若有火起，即亦燃之。」

translations.literal: Having set ambushes, he secretly had men carry fire in gourds across the south bank and place them where the water was deep, instructing, "If fires appear, light these as well."
translations.idiomatic: Having set ambushes, he secretly had men carry fire in gourds across the south bank and place them where the water ran deep, instructing, "If fires appear, light these as well."

sentences.zh: 其夜，康祖、公政等果親率領來斫營。

translations.literal: That night Kangzu, Gongzheng, and the rest did indeed lead their men personally to raid the camp.
translations.idiomatic: That night Kangzu, Gongzheng, and the rest did indeed lead their men in person to raid the camp.

sentences.zh: 東西二伏夾擊之，康祖等奔趨淮水。

translations.literal: East and west ambushes closed on them; Kangzu and the others dashed for the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushes east and west closed on them; Kangzu and the others dashed for the Huai.

sentences.zh: 火既競起，不能記其本濟，遂望永所置火爭渡。

translations.literal: Fires blazed up everywhere; they could not find their original ford and rushed toward the fires Yong had placed.
translations.idiomatic: Fires blazed up everywhere; they could not find their original ford and rushed toward the fires Yong had set.

sentences.zh: 水深溺死，斬首者數千級，生禽公政。

translations.literal: The water was deep and many drowned; several thousand heads were taken, and Gongzheng was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: The water was deep and many drowned; several thousand heads were taken, and Gongzheng was captured alive.

sentences.zh: 康祖人馬墜淮，曉而獲其屍，斬首並公政送京師。

translations.literal: Kangzu's men and horses fell into the Huai; at dawn his corpse was recovered; the heads of both were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu's men and horses fell into the Huai; at dawn his corpse was recovered, and the heads of both were sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時裴叔業率王茂先、李定等東侵楚王戍，肅復令永將伏兵，擊其後軍，破之，獲叔業傘扇鼓幕甲仗萬餘。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye led Wang Maoxian, Li Ding, and others east to attack the Prince of Chu's garrison, Su again sent Yong with ambush troops to strike their rear, defeated them, and seized more than ten thousand pieces of Shuye's umbrellas, fans, drums, screens, armor, and gear.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye led Wang Maoxian, Li Ding, and others east to attack the Prince of Chu's garrison, Su again sent Yong with ambush troops to strike their rear, routed them, and seized more than ten thousand pieces of Shuye's umbrellas, fans, drums, screens, armor, and gear.

sentences.zh: 兩月之中，遂獻再捷。

translations.literal: Within two months he twice reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Within two months he reported victory twice.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，遣謁者就豫州，策拜永安遠將軍、鎮南府長史、汝南太守、貝丘縣男。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him and sent an envoy to Yu Province to appoint him by written warrant Acting General of Distant Pacification of Yong'an, Chief of Staff of the Southern Garrison, Governor of Runan, and Baron of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and sent an envoy to Yu Province to appoint him by written warrant Acting General of Distant Pacification of Yong'an, Chief of Staff of the Southern Garrison, Governor of Runan, and Baron of Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 帝每歎曰：「上馬能擊賊，下馬作露布，唯傅脩期耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor would sigh, "Able to strike the enemy from horseback and write battle bulletins on foot—only Fu Xiuqi!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would sigh, "Able to strike the enemy from horseback and write battle bulletins on foot—only Fu Xiuqi!"

sentences.zh: 裴叔業又圍渦陽，時帝在豫州，遣永為統軍，與高聰、劉藻、成道益、任莫問等救之。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye again besieged Woyang; the emperor was then in Yu Province and sent Yong as commander-in-chief with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Moqun, and others to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye again besieged Woyang; the emperor was then in Yu Province and sent Yong as commander-in-chief with Gao Cong, Liu Zao, Cheng Daoyi, Ren Moqun, and others to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「深溝固壘，然後圖之。」

translations.literal: Yong said, "Dig deep trenches and fortify the ramparts—then consider the next move."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Dig deep trenches and fortify the ramparts—then consider the next move."

sentences.zh: 聰等不從，一戰而敗。

translations.literal: Cong and the rest would not listen; one battle and they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and the rest would not listen; one battle and they were defeated.

sentences.zh: 聰等棄甲奔懸瓠，永獨收散卒徐還。

translations.literal: Cong and the others threw away their armor and fled to Xuanshi; Yong alone gathered the scattered troops and withdrew at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Cong and the others threw away their armor and fled to Xuanshi; Yong alone gathered the scattered troops and withdrew at leisure.

sentences.zh: 賊追至，又設伏擊之，挫其銳。

translations.literal: The enemy pursued; he set another ambush and blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy pursued; he set another ambush and blunted their momentum.

sentences.zh: 藻徙邊，永免官爵而已。

translations.literal: Zao was banished to the frontier; Yong was merely stripped of rank and title.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was banished to the frontier; Yong was merely stripped of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 不經旬，詔永為汝陰鎮將，帶汝陰太守。

translations.literal: Within less than ten days Yong was ordered to be garrison commander of Ruyin, concurrently Governor of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten days Yong was ordered to be garrison commander of Ruyin, concurrently Governor of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 景明初，裴叔業將以壽春歸魏，密通於永。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingming Pei Shuye was to surrender Shouchun to Wei and secretly communicated with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingming Pei Shuye was to surrender Shouchun to Wei and secretly communicated with Yong.

sentences.zh: 及將迎納，詔永為統軍，與楊大眼、奚康生等諸軍俱入壽春。

translations.literal: When the reception was mounted, Yong was ordered commander-in-chief and entered Shouchun with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrender was to be received, Yong was ordered commander-in-chief and entered Shouchun with Yang Dayan, Xi Kangsheng, and the other armies.

sentences.zh: 同日而永在後，故康生、大眼二人並賞列士，永唯清河男。

translations.literal: On the same day Yong was in the rear, so Kangsheng and Dayan were both rewarded with ranks as valiant knights, while Yong received only the title Baron of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: On the same day Yong was in the rear, so Kangsheng and Dayan were both rewarded as valiant knights, while Yong received only the title Baron of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 齊將陳伯之逼壽春，沿淮為寇。

translations.literal: Qi general Chen Bozhi pressed on Shouchun and raided along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Qi general Chen Bozhi pressed on Shouchun and raided along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 時司徒彭城王勰、廣陵侯元衍同鎮壽春，以九江初附，人情未洽，兼台援不至，深以為憂。

translations.literal: Then Minister over the Masses Prince Pengcheng of Xie and Marquis Guangling Yuan Yan jointly garrisoned Shouchun; Jiujiang had only just submitted, popular sentiment was not yet settled, and capital reinforcements had not arrived—they were deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Then Minister over the Masses Prince Pengcheng of Xie and Marquis Guangling Yuan Yan jointly garrisoned Shouchun; Jiujiang had only just submitted, hearts were not yet won, capital reinforcements had not arrived, and they were deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 詔遣永為統軍，領汝陰三千人先援之。

translations.literal: Yong was ordered commander-in-chief and led three thousand men from Ruyin as the first relief.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was ordered commander-in-chief and led three thousand men from Ruyin as the first relief.

sentences.zh: 永至，勰令永引軍入城。

translations.literal: When Yong arrived, Xie ordered him to lead his troops into the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong arrived, Xie ordered him to lead his troops into the city.

sentences.zh: 永曰：「若如教旨，便共殿下同被圍守，豈是救援之意？」

translations.literal: Yong said, "If I follow that order, I shall share entrapment with Your Highness—is that the meaning of relief?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "If I follow that order, I shall share entrapment with Your Highness—is that what relief means?"

sentences.zh: 遂孤軍城外，與勰並勢以擊伯之，頻有克捷。

translations.literal: He kept his army alone outside the walls and joined forces with Xie to strike Bozhi, winning repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his army alone outside the walls and joined forces with Xie to strike Bozhi, winning victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 中山王英之征義陽，永為甯朔將軍、統軍，當長圍遏其南門。

translations.literal: When Prince Zhongshan of Ying campaigned against Yiyang, Yong served as General of Pacifying the North and commander-in-chief, holding the long encirclement at its southern gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhongshan of Ying campaigned against Yiyang, Yong served as General of Pacifying the North and commander-in-chief, holding the long encirclement at the southern gate.

sentences.zh: 齊將馬仙琕連營稍進，規解城圍。

translations.literal: Qi general Ma Xianbi advanced camp by camp, planning to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Qi general Ma Xianbi advanced camp by camp, planning to lift the siege.

sentences.zh: 永乃分兵付長史賈思祖，令守營壘，自將馬步千人，南逆仙琕。

translations.literal: Yong then left troops with Chief Clerk Jia Sizu to hold the camps and personally led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianbi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then left troops with Chief Clerk Jia Sizu to hold the camps and personally led a thousand horse and foot south to meet Xianbi.

sentences.zh: 賊俯射永，洞其左股，永出箭復入，遂大破之。

translations.literal: The enemy shot down at Yong and pierced his left thigh; Yong pulled out the arrow and charged back in, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy shot down at Yong and pierced his left thigh; Yong pulled out the arrow and charged back in, and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 仙琕燒營卷甲而遁。

translations.literal: Xianbi burned his camps, rolled up his armor, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xianbi burned his camps, rolled up his armor, and fled.

sentences.zh: 英曰：「公傷矣！

translations.literal: Ying said, "Sir, you are wounded!
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "Sir, you are wounded!

sentences.zh: 且還營。」

translations.literal: Go back to camp."
translations.idiomatic: Go back to camp."

sentences.zh: 永曰：「昔漢祖捫足，不欲人知。

translations.literal: Yong said, "Long ago Emperor Gao of Han clutched his foot and did not want others to know.
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Long ago Emperor Gao of Han clutched his foot and did not want others to know.

sentences.zh: 下官雖微，國家一帥，奈何使虜有傷將之名！」

translations.literal: Though I am lowly, I am a commander of the state—how can I let the enemy boast that they wounded a general!"
translations.idiomatic: Though I am lowly, I am a commander of the state—how can I let the enemy boast that they wounded a general!"

sentences.zh: 遂與諸軍追之，極夜而返。

translations.literal: He pursued with the other armies and returned only at dead of night.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued with the other armies and returned only at dead of night.

sentences.zh: 時年七十餘矣，三軍莫不壯之。

translations.literal: He was then past seventy; the whole army was stirred with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He was then past seventy; the whole army was stirred with admiration.

sentences.zh: 義陽既平，英使司馬陸希道為露布，意謂不可，令永改之。

translations.literal: When Yiyang was pacified, Ying had Major Lu Xidao draft the victory bulletin but thought it inadequate and ordered Yong to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yiyang was pacified, Ying had Major Lu Xidao draft the victory bulletin but thought it inadequate and ordered Yong to revise it.

sentences.zh: 永亦不增文采，直與之改，陳列軍儀，處置形要，而英深賞之。

translations.literal: Yong added no literary flourish—he simply reworked it, setting forth military order and dispositions; Ying deeply admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Yong added no literary flourish—he simply reworked it, setting forth military order and dispositions, and Ying deeply admired it.

sentences.zh: 還京，除太中大夫。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was made Grand Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he was appointed Grand Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 後除恆農太守，非心所樂。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Hengnong—not to his liking.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Governor of Hengnong—not to his liking.

sentences.zh: 時英東征鐘離，表請永，求以為將，朝廷不聽。

translations.literal: When Ying campaigned east against Zhongli he petitioned for Yong and begged to use him as a general; the court would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When Ying campaigned east against Zhongli he petitioned for Yong and begged to use him as a general; the court would not agree.

sentences.zh: 永每言曰：「馬援、充國，竟何人哉？

translations.literal: Yong would often say, "What manner of men were Ma Yuan and Zhao Chongguo?
translations.idiomatic: Yong would often say, "What manner of men were Ma Yuan and Zhao Chongguo?

sentences.zh: 吾獨白首見拘此郡！」

translations.literal: Must I alone, white-haired, be chained to this commandery!"
translations.idiomatic: Must I alone, white-haired, be chained to this commandery!"

sentences.zh: 然於御人非其所長，故在任無多聲稱。

translations.literal: Yet governing people was not his strength, so in office he won little renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet governing people was not his strength, so in office he won little renown.

sentences.zh: 後為南袞州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 年逾八十，猶能馳射，盤馬奮槊，常諱言老，每自稱六十九。

translations.literal: Past eighty he could still ride and shoot, wheel his horse and flourish his spear; he always shunned talk of age and called himself sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Past eighty he could still ride and shoot, wheel his horse and flourish his spear; he always shunned talk of age and called himself sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 還京，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He returned to the capital and was appointed Grand Master for the Splendor of State.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital and was appointed Grand Master for the Splendor of State.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 永嘗登北芒，於平坦處奮矛躍馬，盤旋瞻望，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Yong once climbed the Northern Mang Hills; on level ground he flourished his spear and spurred his horse, wheeling about and gazing around with the wish to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Yong once climbed the Northern Mang Hills; on a level stretch he brandished his spear and spurred his horse, circling and looking about as though he meant to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 遠慕杜預，近好李沖、王肅，欲葬附墓。

translations.literal: From afar he admired Du Yu; in recent times he favored Li Chong and Wang Su, and wished to be buried beside their tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He admired Du Yu from afar and in his own day favored Li Chong and Wang Su, hoping to be buried beside their graves.

sentences.zh: 遂買左右地數頃，遺敕子叔偉：「此吾之永宅也。」

translations.literal: He therefore bought several mou of land to left and right and left instructions to his son Shuwei: "This is my everlasting home."
translations.idiomatic: He bought several mou of land on either side and left instructions to his son Shuwei: "This is where I shall rest forever."

sentences.zh: 永妻賈氏留本鄉，永至代都，娶妾馮氏，生叔偉及數女。

translations.literal: Yong's wife the Lady Jia remained in her native district; Yong reached the capital of Dai, took a concubine the Lady Feng, and by her had Shuwei and several daughters.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's wife Lady Jia stayed in her home district. When Yong reached Dai he took concubine Lady Feng, who bore Shuwei and several daughters.

sentences.zh: 賈后歸平城，無男，唯一女。

translations.literal: When the Lady Jia returned to Pingcheng she had no sons—only one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jia returned to Pingcheng with no sons, only a single daughter.

sentences.zh: 馮恃子，事賈無禮，叔偉亦奉賈不順，賈常忿之。

translations.literal: Feng relied on her son and treated Jia without courtesy; Shuwei too was disrespectful toward Jia, and Jia was often resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Feng leaned on her son and treated Jia rudely; Shuwei likewise slighted Jia, who grew bitter toward them.

sentences.zh: 馮先永卒，叔偉稱父命欲葬北芒，賈疑叔偉將以馮合葬，遂求歸葬永于所封貝丘縣。

translations.literal: Feng died before Yong; Shuwei claimed his father's command and wished to bury him on the Northern Mang, but Jia suspected Shuwei meant to bury Feng with him and therefore sought to have Yong returned for burial in his enfeoffed county of Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng died before Yong. Shuwei cited his father's orders and wanted burial on the Northern Mang, but Jia feared he would inter Feng beside Yong and demanded Yong be buried in his fief of Beiqiu county instead.

sentences.zh: 事經司徒，司徒胡國珍感其所慕，許叔偉葬焉。

translations.literal: The matter went before the Minister over the Masses; the Minister Hu Guozhen, moved by whom Yong had admired, permitted Shuwei to bury him there.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the Minister over the Masses Hu Guozhen, who, touched by Yong's chosen exemplars, allowed Shuwei to bury him on the Mang.

sentences.zh: 賈乃邀訴靈太后，太后從賈意，乃葬於東清河。

translations.literal: Jia then appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, and the Empress Dowager sided with Jia; he was buried in Eastern Qinghe instead.
translations.idiomatic: Jia appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, who took her side, and Yong was buried in Eastern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 又永昔營宅兆，葬父母于舊鄉，賈于此強徙之，與永同處，永宗親不能抑。

translations.literal: Moreover Yong had once chosen a grave site and buried his parents in his old home district; Jia forcibly had them moved to lie with Yong, and Yong's clansmen could not restrain her.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had also prepared a family grave in his native district and buried his parents there; Jia had them forcibly moved to Yong's new tomb, and his kin could not stop her.

sentences.zh: 葬已數十年矣，棺為桑棗根所繞束，去地尺餘，甚為周固。

translations.literal: Though the burial had been decades earlier, the coffins were bound round and round by mulberry and jujube roots and stood more than a foot above the ground, extraordinarily firm.
translations.idiomatic: Though decades had passed, the coffins were wound tight with mulberry and jujube roots and stood more than a foot above the ground, remarkably secure.

sentences.zh: 以斧斫，出之于坎，時人咸怪。

translations.literal: When they were hewn out with axes and lifted from the pit, everyone present was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: They were cut free with axes and raised from the pit, and all who saw it were astonished.

sentences.zh: 叔偉膂力過人，彎弓三百斤，左右馳射，能立馬上與人角騁，見者以為得永武而不得永文。

translations.literal: Shuwei's physical strength surpassed other men; he could bend a bow of three hundred jin, shoot left and right while galloping, and wrestle on horseback with others—onlookers thought he had Yong's martial prowess but not Yong's learning.
translations.idiomatic: Shuwei's strength surpassed ordinary men; he drew a three-hundred-jin bow, shot on the move from either hand, and could wrestle mounted—observers said he had Yong's fighting skill but not his refinement.

sentences.zh: 傅豎眼，本清河人也。

translations.literal: Fu Shuyan was originally a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shuyan was a native of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 七世祖伷。

translations.literal: His seventh-generation ancestor was You.
translations.idiomatic: His seventh-generation ancestor was You.

sentences.zh: 伷子遘，石季龍太常。

translations.literal: You's son Sui was Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Shi Hu of Later Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: You's son Sui served Shi Hu of Later Zhao as Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祖父融，南徙度河，家于磐陽，為鄉閭所重。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rong moved south across the Yellow River and settled at Panyang, where he was respected in village and neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rong migrated south across the Yellow River and made his home at Panyang, esteemed among neighbors.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，有三子，靈慶、靈根、靈越，並有才力。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and chivalrous; he had three sons—Lingqing, Linggen, and Lingyue—all gifted with strength and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and chivalrous by nature, he had three sons—Lingqing, Linggen, and Lingyue—each strong and capable.

sentences.zh: 融以自負，謂足為一時之雄。

translations.literal: Rong, confident in himself, considered himself hero enough for an age.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, full of self-confidence, reckoned himself a hero of the times.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂人曰：「吾昨夢夜，有一駿馬，無堪乘者，人曰'何由得人乘'，有一人曰'唯傅靈慶堪乘此馬'；

translations.literal: He once told others: "Last night I dreamed of a fine steed with no one fit to ride it. Someone said, 'How could one find a rider?' Another said, 'Only Fu Lingqing can ride this horse';
translations.idiomatic: He once said to others: "I dreamed last night of a fine horse and no rider worthy of it. They asked who could ride it, and someone answered, 'Only Fu Lingqing can ride this horse';

sentences.zh: 又有弓一張，亦無人堪引，人曰'唯有傅靈根可彎此弓'；

translations.literal: There was also a bow with no one able to draw it; they said, 'Only Fu Linggen can bend this bow';
translations.idiomatic: There was also a bow no one could draw; they said, 'Only Fu Linggen can bend it';

sentences.zh: 又有數紙文書，人皆讀不能解，人曰'唯有傅靈越能解此文。

translations.literal: There were also several sheets of writing no one could read; they said, 'Only Fu Lingyue can interpret this text.'"
translations.idiomatic: And several written sheets no one could read; they said, 'Only Fu Lingyue can make sense of them.'"

sentences.zh: '」融謂其三子文武才幹足以駕馭當世，常從容謂鄉人曰：「汝聞之不？

translations.literal: Rong said his three sons' civil and military talent was enough to master the age, and would calmly tell his neighbors: "Have you not heard?
translations.idiomatic: Rong declared that his three sons' civil and military gifts were enough to command the age, and would calmly tell neighbors: "Have you heard?

sentences.zh: 鬲蟲之子有三靈，此圖讖文也。」

translations.literal: The son of the Ge insect has three Ling—this is the text of a prophecy."
translations.idiomatic: The son of the Ge creature has three Ling—that is what the prophecy means."

sentences.zh: 好事者然之，故豪勇士多相歸附。

translations.literal: Those fond of such things believed him, so bold warriors in great numbers attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Believers took him at his word, and bold fighting men flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 宋將蕭斌、王玄謨寇磝碻。

translations.literal: Song generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo attacked Aoqi.
translations.idiomatic: Song generals Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo invaded Aoqi.

sentences.zh: 時融始死，玄謨強引靈慶為軍主。

translations.literal: At that time Rong had just died; Xuemo forcibly made Lingqing army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had just died; Xuemo pressed Lingqing into service as army commander.

sentences.zh: 將攻城，攻車為城內所燒，靈慶懼軍法，詐云傷重，令左右輿還營，遂與壯士數十騎遁還。

translations.literal: When they were about to assault the city, the siege engines were burned by those within; Lingqing feared military law, pretended grave wounds, had his attendants carry him back to camp on a litter, and fled with several dozen stalwart riders.
translations.idiomatic: As they prepared to storm the city, defenders burned the siege engines. Fearful of punishment, Lingqing feigned serious wounds, was carried back to camp, and fled with several dozen picked horsemen.

sentences.zh: 斌、玄謨命追之。

translations.literal: Bin and Xuemo ordered pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Xuemo ordered him pursued.

sentences.zh: 左右諫曰：「靈慶兄弟並有雄才，兼其部曲多是壯勇，如彭超、屍生之徒，皆一當數十人，援不虛發，不可逼也。」

translations.literal: His attendants remonstrated: "Lingqing and his brothers all have heroic talent, and most of their followers are fierce braves—men like Peng Chao and Shisheng, each a match for dozens, never missing with the bow; they must not be pressed."
translations.idiomatic: His staff warned: "The Lingqing brothers are all formidable, and their followers—men like Peng Chao and Shisheng—fight one against many and never miss a shot. Do not press them."

sentences.zh: 玄謨乃止。

translations.literal: Xuemo then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo heeded them and halted the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 靈慶至家，遂與二弟匿山澤間。

translations.literal: Lingqing reached home and hid with his two brothers in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Lingqing reached home and hid in the hills with his two brothers.

sentences.zh: 時靈慶從叔乾愛為斌法曹參軍，斌遣乾愛誘呼之，以腰刀為信，密令壯健者隨之。

translations.literal: At that time Lingqing's paternal cousin Gan'ai served Bin as Registrar of the Law; Bin sent Gan'ai to lure them out, giving a waist-knife as token and secretly ordering stout men to follow.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Fu Gan'ai was Bin's Registrar of the Law; Bin sent Gan'ai to call them in with a waist-knife as pledge, while strong men followed secretly.

sentences.zh: 而乾愛不知斌之欲圖靈慶。

translations.literal: Gan'ai did not know Bin intended to trap Lingqing.
translations.idiomatic: Gan'ai did not know Bin meant to seize Lingqing.

sentences.zh: 既至，斌所遣壯士執靈慶殺之。

translations.literal: Once they arrived, the stalwarts Bin had sent seized Lingqing and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Bin's men seized Lingqing and killed him.

sentences.zh: 靈慶將死，與母崔氏訣，言：「法曹殺人，不可忘也。」

translations.literal: As Lingqing was dying he took leave of his mother the Lady Cui, saying: "The Registrar of the Law has killed a man—do not forget it."
translations.idiomatic: Facing death, Lingqing bade farewell to his mother Lady Cui: "The Registrar of the Law has shed blood—never forget it."

sentences.zh: 靈根、靈越奔河北。

translations.literal: Linggen and Lingyue fled north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen and Lingyue fled to the north bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 靈越至京師，因說齊人慕化，青州可平。

translations.literal: Lingyue reached the capital and reported that the people of Qi yearned for transformation and that Qingzhou could be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue reached the Northern Wei capital and argued that Qi's people longed for the dynasty and Qingzhou could be taken.

sentences.zh: 文成大悅，拜靈越青州刺史、貝丘子，鎮羊蘭城；

translations.literal: Emperor Wencheng was greatly pleased, made Lingyue Governor of Qingzhou and Marquis of Beiqiu, and garrisoned Yanglan fortress;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wencheng was delighted, appointed Lingyue Governor of Qingzhou and Marquis of Beiqiu, and posted him at Yanglan fortress;

sentences.zh: 靈根為臨齊副將，鎮明潛壘。

translations.literal: Linggen became deputy commander of the Linqi garrison and held Mingqian fort.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen became deputy of the Linqi command and held Mingqian fort.

sentences.zh: 靈越北入之後，母崔氏遇赦免。

translations.literal: After Lingyue went north, his mother the Lady Cui was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lingyue had gone north, Lady Cui received an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 宋恐靈越在邊擾三齊，乃以靈越叔父琰為冀州中從事，乾愛為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: Song, fearing Lingyue would trouble the three Qi commanderies from the frontier, made his uncle Yan Regional Inspector of Ji and Gan'ai Governor of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Song, fearing trouble on the Qi frontier, made his uncle Yan Inspector of Ji and Gan'ai Governor of Leling.

sentences.zh: 樂陵與羊蘭隔河相對，命琰遣其門生與靈越婢詐為夫婦，投化以招之。

translations.literal: Leling lay across the river from Yanglan; Yan was ordered to send a student of his household and Lingyue's maid, disguised as husband and wife, to defect and lure him back.
translations.idiomatic: Leling faced Yanglan across the river; Yan sent a household student and Lingyue's maid, posing as a couple, to lure him south.

sentences.zh: 靈越與母分離思積，遂與靈根南走。

translations.literal: Lingyue, torn by longing for his mother from whom he was parted, went south with Linggen.
translations.idiomatic: Longing for his mother, Lingyue went south with Linggen.

sentences.zh: 靈越與羊蘭奮兵相擊，乾愛出，遣船迎之，得免。

translations.literal: Lingyue fought fiercely with the garrison at Yanglan; Gan'ai came out and sent boats to receive them, and they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue fought the Yanglan garrison; Gan'ai came out with boats and brought them off safely.

sentences.zh: 靈根差期，不得俱渡，臨齊人知，剉斬殺之。

translations.literal: Linggen was late and could not cross with them; the men of Linqi learned of it and hacked him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Linggen missed the crossing; the Linqi garrison learned of it and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 乾愛出郡迎靈越，問靈根愆期狀，靈越殊不應答。

translations.literal: Gan'ai left the commandery to welcome Lingyue and asked why Linggen had been late; Lingyue would not answer at all.
translations.idiomatic: Gan'ai went out to welcome Lingyue and asked about Linggen's delay; Lingyue would not reply.

sentences.zh: 乾愛不以為惡，敕左右出匣中烏皮袴褶，令靈越代所常服。

translations.literal: Gan'ai did not take this as ill will and ordered his attendants to bring from a chest black leather riding dress and trousers for Lingyue to wear instead of his usual clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Gan'ai took no offense and had attendants bring black leather riding dress from a chest for Lingyue to wear in place of his old clothes.

sentences.zh: 靈越言「不須」。

translations.literal: Lingyue said, "I have no need of them."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue said, "I do not need them."

sentences.zh: 乾愛云：「汝可著體上衣服見垣公也？」

translations.literal: Gan'ai said, "Will you go before Lord Yuan in the clothes on your back?"
translations.idiomatic: Gan'ai said, "Will you appear before Lord Yuan dressed like that?"

sentences.zh: 時垣護之為刺史。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Huzhi was Regional Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi was then Regional Inspector.

sentences.zh: 靈越奮聲言：「垣公！

translations.literal: Lingyue cried out loudly, "Lord Yuan!
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue shouted, "Lord Yuan!

sentences.zh: 垣公！

translations.literal: Lord Yuan!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yuan!

sentences.zh: 著此當見南方國主，豈垣公也！」

translations.literal: Am I to wear this to meet the lord of the southern realm—not Lord Yuan!"
translations.idiomatic: I am to wear this before the southern emperor—not before Lord Yuan!"

sentences.zh: 竟不肯著。

translations.literal: In the end he would not put them on.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to wear them.

sentences.zh: 及至丹陽，宋孝武見而禮之，拜袞州司馬，而乾愛亦遷青、冀司馬，帶魏郡。

translations.literal: When he reached Danyang, Emperor Xiaowu of Song received him with ceremony and made him Military Commander of Yanzhou, while Gan'ai was also transferred to be Military Commander of Qing and Ji, with Wei commandery attached.
translations.idiomatic: At Danyang, Emperor Xiaowu of Song honored him and made him Military Commander of Yanzhou; Gan'ai too became Military Commander of Qing and Ji with Wei commandery attached.

sentences.zh: 後二人俱還建鄴。

translations.literal: Later both men returned to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Later both returned to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 靈越意恆欲為兄復仇，而乾愛初不疑防。

translations.literal: Lingyue constantly meant to avenge his brother, while Gan'ai at first never suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue burned to avenge his brother; Gan'ai at first never guarded against him.

sentences.zh: 知乾愛嗜雞肉葵菜食，乃為作之，下以毒藥，乾愛飯還而卒。

translations.literal: Knowing Gan'ai loved chicken with purslane, he prepared it for him and poisoned it; after the meal Gan'ai returned and died.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Gan'ai loved chicken with purslane, he cooked it for him with poison; Gan'ai ate, went home, and died.

sentences.zh: 後數年，靈越為太原太守，戍升城。

translations.literal: Several years later Lingyue became Governor of Taiyuan and garrisoned Shengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Lingyue was Governor of Taiyuan, garrisoning Shengcheng.

sentences.zh: 後舉兵同孝武子子勳，子勳以靈越為前軍將軍。

translations.literal: Later he raised troops with Emperor Xiaowu's son Zixun; Zixun made Lingyue General of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Zixun's rebellion; Zixun made him General of the Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 子勳敗，靈越軍眾散亡，為明帝將王廣之軍人所擒，厲聲曰：「我傅靈越也，汝得賊何不即殺！」

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated, Lingyue's army scattered; he was seized by soldiers of Ming Emperor's general Wang Guangzhi and cried out: "I am Fu Lingyue! You have your captive—why not kill me at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Zixun fell; Lingyue's troops dispersed. Wang Guangzhi's men seized him, and he shouted: "I am Fu Lingyue! You have your enemy—why not kill me now!"

sentences.zh: 廣之生送詣宋輔國司馬劉勔，勔躬自慰勞。

translations.literal: Guangzhi sent him alive to Song's Assistant to the General Who Conquers the North, Liu Kan, who came forward in person to console and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhi sent him alive to Liu Kan, Assistant to the General Who Conquers the North, who came out in person to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 靈越曰：「人生歸於死，實無面求活。」

translations.literal: Lingyue said: "In life all men return to death; I truly have no face left with which to beg for life."
translations.idiomatic: Lingyue said: "All men must die; I have no shame left to beg for my life."

sentences.zh: 勔壯其意，送詣建康。

translations.literal: Kan admired his spirit and sent him on to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Kan admired his spirit and sent him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝欲加原宥，靈越辭對如一，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song wished to pardon him, but Lingyue answered as before and was therefore executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming wished to spare him, but Lingyue answered as steadfastly as ever and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 豎眼即靈越子也，沉毅壯烈，少有父風。

translations.literal: Shuyan was Lingyue's son—grave, resolute, and fierce, showing his father's manner from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan was Lingyue's son: stern, resolute, and bold, with his father's spirit even as a youth.

sentences.zh: 入魏，鎮南王肅見而異之，且奇其父節，傾身禮敬，表為參軍。

translations.literal: On entering Wei, Prince of Zhennan Xiao Su saw him and was struck by him; he also marveled at his father's integrity, paid him full personal respect, and memorialized to have him made a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Wei, Prince of Zhennan Xiao Su was impressed by him and by his father's integrity, treated him with full courtesy, and had him appointed to his staff.

sentences.zh: 以軍功累遷益州刺史。

translations.literal: Through military merit he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By military merit he rose to Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 高肇伐蜀，假豎眼征虜將軍、持節，領步兵三萬，先討巴北，所至克捷。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned against Shu, Shuyan was made acting General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Bearer of the Staff, leading thirty thousand foot soldiers to strike Ba north first; wherever he went he won.
translations.idiomatic: In Gao Zhao's Shu campaign, Shuyan was made acting General Who Pacifies the Barbarians with the Staff, leading thirty thousand foot to subdue northern Ba and winning wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 豎眼性既清素，不營產業，衣食之外，俸祿粟帛皆以饗賜夷首，振恤士卒。

translations.literal: Shuyan's nature was plain and austere; he did not pursue estates—beyond food and clothing he used salary, grain, and silk to feast and reward tribal chiefs and relieve his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and austere by nature, he built no estates; beyond necessities he spent salary, grain, and silk on tribal leaders and his troops.

sentences.zh: 撫蜀人以恩信為本，保境安人，不以小利侵竊。

translations.literal: He governed Shu on the basis of kindness and trust, secured the borders and settled the people, and did not steal by petty gains.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled Shu through kindness and trust, kept the borders secure and the people at peace, and scorned petty plunder.

sentences.zh: 有掠蜀人入境者，皆移送還本。

translations.literal: Any who plundered Shu people and crossed the border were sent back to their own lands.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who seized Shu subjects across the border was returned home.

sentences.zh: 檢勒部下，守宰肅然。

translations.literal: He inspected and restrained his subordinates; prefects and magistrates were in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his subordinates in strict order; local officials stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 遠近雜夷相率款謁，仰其德化，思為魏人矣。

translations.literal: Tribes near and far came in succession to pay court, looking up to his civilizing virtue and wishing to become men of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tribes far and near came to submit, drawn by his virtue and wishing to become Wei subjects.

sentences.zh: 宣武甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，屢請解州，乃以元法僧代之，益州人追隨戀泣者數百里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he repeatedly asked to be relieved of the province; Yuan Faseng was sent to replace him, and the people of Yizhou followed him in tears for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first took the throne, Shuyan repeatedly asked to leave office; Yuan Faseng replaced him, and Yizhou people followed him weeping for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 梁將趙祖悅逼壽春，鎮南將軍崔亮討之，以豎眼為持節、鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: Liang general Zhao Zuyue pressed Shouyang; the General Who Guards the South Cui Liang campaigned against him and made Shuyan Bearer of the Staff and army supervisor of the southern command.
translations.idiomatic: Liang general Zhao Zuyue threatened Shouyang; Cui Liang, General Who Guards the South, made Shuyan Bearer of the Staff and army supervisor for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 法僧既至，大失人和。

translations.literal: Once Faseng arrived he utterly lost the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Faseng arrived he lost all popular support.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其衡州刺史張齊因人心怨入寇，進圍州城。

translations.literal: Liang sent its Inspector of Hengzhou Zhang Qi to exploit popular resentment and invade, advancing to besiege the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Hengzhou Inspector Zhang Qi to exploit the discontent and invade, pressing the siege of the capital.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以西南為憂，乃驛征豎眼於淮南，以為益州刺史。

translations.literal: The court, anxious for the southwest, dispatched Shuyan by post from Huainan to be Governor of Yizhou again.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed for the southwest, the court recalled Shuyan by express from Huainan and reappointed him Governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍、西征都督，率步騎三千以討齊。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Western Expedition, leading three thousand foot and horse to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Western Expedition with three thousand foot and horse to strike Qi.

sentences.zh: 給銅印千餘，須有假職者，聽六品已下板之。

translations.literal: More than a thousand bronze seals were given him; wherever temporary office was needed, ranks of sixth grade and below might be stamped on boards.
translations.idiomatic: He received more than a thousand bronze seals and authority to grant provisional posts through sixth rank on wooden boards.

sentences.zh: 豎眼既出梁州，梁軍所在拒塞，豎眼三日中轉戰二百餘里，甲不去身，頻致九捷。

translations.literal: Once Shuyan had left Liangzhou, Liang armies blocked him everywhere; in three days he fought over two hundred li, never doffing his armor, and won nine victories in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Liangzhou, he met Liang resistance at every turn; in three days he fought over two hundred li without removing his armor and won nine battles straight.

sentences.zh: 蜀人聞豎眼復為刺史，人人喜悅，迎于路者日有百數。

translations.literal: When the people of Shu heard Shuyan was governor again, everyone rejoiced; those who met him on the road numbered a hundred or more each day.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Shuyan was governor again, the people of Shu rejoiced; hundreds greeted him on the road each day.

sentences.zh: 豎眼至州，白水已東，人皆寧業。

translations.literal: When Shuyan reached the province, east of the Baishui all lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached the province, all east of the Baishui had settled in peace.

sentences.zh: 張齊仍阻白水屯，寇葭萌。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi still held the Baishui crossing and raided Jiameng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi still blocked the Baishui ford and raided Jiameng.

sentences.zh: 豎眼分遣諸將水陸討之，大破其軍。

translations.literal: Shuyan sent his generals against him by land and water and smashed his army.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan sent generals against him by land and water and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 齊被重創，奔而退，小劍大劍賊亦捐城西走，益州平。

translations.literal: Qi was badly wounded and fled in retreat; the bandits at Lesser Sword and Greater Sword also abandoned the cities and fled west; Yizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was badly wounded and fled; rebels at Lesser Sword and Greater Sword abandoned their cities and fled west, and Yizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 靈太后璽書慰勞，賜驊騮馬一匹，寶劍一口。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent a message of imperial comfort and bestowed one piebald horse and one treasured sword.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling sent words of praise and granted a piebald horse and a treasured sword.

sentences.zh: 後轉岐州刺史，仍轉梁州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Governor of Qi and then to Governor of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Qi, then Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁州人既得豎眼為牧，人咸自賀。

translations.literal: The people of Liang, having gained Shuyan as their shepherd, all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Liang, having Shuyan as governor again, congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 而豎眼至州遇患，不堪綜理。

translations.literal: But when Shuyan reached the province he fell ill and could not manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuyan arrived he fell ill and could not govern.

sentences.zh: 其子敬紹嶮暴不仁，聚貨耽色，甚為人害，遠近怨望。

translations.literal: His son Jingshao was brutal and cruel, amassed wealth and indulged in lust, and did great harm; near and far resented him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingshao was savage and cruel, hoarded wealth and chased pleasure, and harmed the region until all despised him.

sentences.zh: 尋假鎮南將軍，都督梁、西益、巴三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting General Who Guards the South and commander of military affairs in Liang, Western Yizhou, and Ba.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting General Who Guards the South, commanding armies in Liang, Western Yizhou, and Ba.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其北梁州長史錫休儒等十軍率眾三萬人寇直城，豎眼遣敬紹總眾赴擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Liang sent Chief Clerk of North Liangzhou Xi Xiuru and ten armies totaling thirty thousand men to attack Zhicheng; Shuyan sent Jingshao to command the forces to meet them and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent North Liangzhou Chief Clerk Xi Xiuru with ten armies, thirty thousand men, against Zhicheng; Shuyan sent Jingshao to meet them and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 敬紹頗覽書傳，微有膽力，而奢淫倜儻，輕為殘害，又見天下多事，陰懷異圖，欲杜絕四方，擅據南鄭。

translations.literal: Jingshao had read somewhat and had a little courage, but was extravagant, dissolute, and lightly cruel; seeing turmoil everywhere, he secretly harbored a separate design, wished to cut off the four directions, and hold Nanzheng alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshao had some learning and nerve, but was extravagant, dissolute, and casually brutal; seeing chaos in the realm, he plotted to seal off the roads and hold Nanzheng for himself.

sentences.zh: 令其妾兄唐昆侖扇攪於外，聚眾圍城，敬紹謀為內應。

translations.literal: He had his concubine's elder brother Tang Kunlun stir up trouble outside and gather men to besiege the city while Jingshao plotted to act within as their ally.
translations.idiomatic: He set his concubine's brother Tang Kunlun to agitate abroad and raise a siege while he conspired within.

sentences.zh: 賊圍既合，事泄，在城兵執敬紹；

translations.literal: Once the rebels had closed the encirclement the plot leaked out; soldiers in the city seized Jingshao;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels closed the ring; the plot was exposed and the garrison seized Jingshao;

sentences.zh: 白豎眼而殺之。

translations.literal: He reported the matter to Shuyan, who had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Shuyan, who had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 豎眼恚，發疾卒。

translations.literal: Shuyan, enraged, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan, furious, took ill and died.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈吏部尚書、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era he was posthumously made Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan he was posthumously Minister of the Civil Service and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初，贈司空公、相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made Duke of Works and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu first took the throne, he was posthumously Duke of Works and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子敬和，次敬仲，並好酒薄行，傾側勢家。

translations.literal: The eldest son was Jinghe; the next, Jingzhong—both were heavy drinkers of loose morals who leaned toward powerful houses.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jinghe and second son Jingzhong were both heavy drinkers of poor character, currying favor with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 敬和，孝莊時以其父有遺惠於益州，復為益州刺史。

translations.literal: Jinghe, in Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, because his father had left lingering kindness in Yizhou, was again made Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang, Jinghe was again made Governor of Yizhou, his father's lingering goodwill in the province still remembered.

sentences.zh: 至州，聚斂無已，好酒嗜色，遠近失望。

translations.literal: On reaching the province he extorted without end, loved wine and women, and men near and far lost hope in him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he extorted without cease, drowned himself in wine and women, and disappointed the whole region.

sentences.zh: 仍為梁將樊文熾攻圍，城降，送於江南。

translations.literal: He was then besieged by the Liang general Fan Wenchi; the city surrendered and he was sent to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang general Fan Wenchi besieged him; the city fell and he was sent south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 後以齊神武威德日廣，令敬和還北，以申和通之意。

translations.literal: Later, as the might and virtue of the Qi divine warrior grew daily, Jinghe was ordered back north to signal a wish for harmony.
translations.idiomatic: As Northern Qi's prestige grew, Jinghe was sent back north to show a desire for peace.

sentences.zh: 除北徐州刺史，復以耽酒為土賊掩襲，棄城走。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of North Xuzhou, but again, through drunkenness, was surprised by local bandits, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Made Governor of North Xuzhou, he was again caught drunk by local bandits, abandoned the city, and fled.

sentences.zh: 遂廢棄，卒於家。

translations.literal: He was then cast aside and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed from office, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 張烈，字徽之，清河東武城人也，孝文帝賜名曰烈，仍以本名為字焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Lie, style Huizhi, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe. Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the personal name Lie and still used his original name as his style.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lie, style Huizhi, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe. Emperor Xiaowen gave him the personal name Lie while keeping his original name as his style.

sentences.zh: 高祖悕，為慕容俊尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xi was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Murong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xi served Murong Jun as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 曾祖恂，散騎常侍，隨慕容德南度，因居齊郡之臨淄縣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xun was Palace Attendant; he followed Murong De south across the river and thus settled in Linzi County, Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xun was Palace Attendant. He followed Murong De south and settled in Linzi, Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 烈少孤貧，涉獵經史，有氣概，時青州有崔徽伯、房徽叔、與烈並有令譽，時人號「三徽」。

translations.literal: Lie was orphaned young and poor, ranged widely through the classics and histories, and had spirit. In Qingzhou at the time were Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu, who with Lie all enjoyed fine reputations; men of the age called them the "Three Huizhi."
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, Lie read widely in the classics and histories and had real backbone. In Qingzhou, Cui Huibo and Fang Huishu shared his renown; contemporaries called them the "Three Huizhi."

sentences.zh: 孝文時，入官代都，曆侍御、主文中散。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowen's time he entered office at the capital in the north, serving in succession as Attendant and Master of Documents in the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaowen he entered service at the northern capital, rising through Attendant and Master of Documents in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，為太子步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang he became Commandant of Footsoldiers for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang he became Commandant of Footsoldiers for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 齊將陳顯達謀將入寇，時順陽太守王青石，世官江南，荊州刺史、廣陽王嘉慮其有異，表請代之。

translations.literal: The Qi general Chen Xianda planned to invade. At the time the Governor of Shunyang, Wang Qingshi, came from a family long in office south of the river; the Governor of Jingzhou, Prince Guangyang Jia, fearing he harbored other intentions, memorialized to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi general Chen Xianda was preparing to invade. Shunyang governor Wang Qingshi came from a southern official family; Jingzhou governor Prince Guangyang Jia, fearing disloyalty, asked to replace him.

sentences.zh: 詔侍臣各舉所知，互有申薦者。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the attendant ministers each to recommend someone they knew; several spoke up with nominations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered each attendant minister to recommend someone he knew; several names were put forward.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「太子步兵張烈，每論軍國事，時有會人意處，朕欲用之如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhang Lie—whenever he discusses military and state affairs he sometimes hits the heart of the matter. How would it be if I used him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Crown Prince's Commandant Zhang Lie—when he speaks of military and state affairs he often grasps the point. Shall I use him?"

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰稱讚之，遂除順陽太守。

translations.literal: Prince Pengcheng Xie praised him, and Lie was appointed Governor of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pengcheng Xie praised him, and Lie was made Governor of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 烈到郡二日，便為齊將崔慧景攻，圍之七十餘日，烈撫厲將士，甚得軍人之和。

translations.literal: Two days after Lie reached the commandery he was attacked by the Qi general Cui Huijing and besieged for more than seventy days; Lie encouraged and rallied the troops and won the soldiers' deep loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Lie took office, Qi general Cui Huijing attacked and besieged him for over seventy days. Lie rallied his men and won the army's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會車駕南討，慧景遁走。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Huijing fled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched south; Huijing fled.

sentences.zh: 帝親勞之曰：「卿果能不負所寄。」

translations.literal: The emperor personally comforted him, saying, "You truly did not betray what was entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person to praise him: "You truly did not betray my trust."

sentences.zh: 烈謝曰：「不遇鑾輿親駕，臣不免困於犬羊。

translations.literal: Lie replied, "Had Your Majesty's carriage not come in person, your servant would not have escaped being trapped among dogs and goats.
translations.idiomatic: Lie answered, "Had Your Majesty not come yourself, I would still be trapped among dogs and goats.

sentences.zh: 自是陛上不負臣，非臣能不負陛下。」

translations.literal: From this it is Your Majesty who did not fail your servant—not that your servant did not fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: It is Your Majesty who did not fail me—not I who did not fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝善其對。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 宣武即位，追錄先勳，封清河縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, earlier merit was reviewed and recorded; Lie was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanwu succeeded, prior service was rewarded and Lie was enfeoffed Viscount of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 尋以母老歸養，積十餘年。

translations.literal: Soon, because his mother was old, he returned home to support her, for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to care for his aged mother and stayed away more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 頻遇凶儉，烈為粥以食饑人，蒙濟者甚眾，鄉黨以此稱之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly met famine years; Lie made gruel to feed the hungry, and very many were saved—his neighborhood praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Famine came again and again; Lie cooked gruel for the starving and saved countless lives. His neighbors praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，為司空長史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Lie became Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming succeeded, Lie became Chief Clerk to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 先是元叉父江陽王繼曾為青州刺史，及叉當權，烈托故義之懷，遂相諂附。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yuan Cha's father, Prince Jiangyang Ji, had once been Governor of Qingzhou; when Cha held power, Lie, relying on old ties of righteousness, fawned upon him and attached himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha's father Prince Jiangyang Ji had once governed Qingzhou; when Cha rose, Lie leaned on old ties and flattered his way into favor.

sentences.zh: 曆給事黃門侍郎、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master for the Splendor of State.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master for the Splendor of State.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，以叉黨出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored the government, as a member of Cha's faction he was sent out as Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Ling retook power, he was exiled to Qingzhou as one of Cha's party.

sentences.zh: 時議者以烈家產畜殖，家僮甚多，慮其有異，恐不宜出為本州，改瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time opinion held that Lie's household wealth had grown through livestock and he had many retainers; they feared he might harbor other designs and that he ought not be sent to his native province, so he was changed to Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Lie's estates and servants had grown too large and feared trouble if he governed his home province, so he was made Governor of Yingzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，吏人安之。

translations.literal: His government was quiet and pure; officials and people were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He governed quietly and fairly; officials and people were content.

sentences.zh: 後因辭老還鄉，兄弟同居怡然，為親類所慕。

translations.literal: Later, citing age, he returned to his home village; he and his brothers lived together in harmony and were admired by kin.
translations.idiomatic: He retired home in old age; he and his brothers lived together in easy harmony, to the envy of their kin.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 烈先為家誡千餘言，並自敘志行及所曆之官。

translations.literal: Lie had earlier written a family admonition of more than a thousand words, together with his own account of his aims, conduct, and the offices he had held.
translations.idiomatic: Lie had already written a thousand-word family admonition and a memoir of his aims, conduct, and offices.

sentences.zh: 臨終，敕子侄不聽求贈，但勒家誡立碣而已。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he ordered his sons and nephews not to seek posthumous honors, but only to inscribe the family admonition on a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he forbade his sons and nephews to seek posthumous titles—only to carve his family admonition on stone.

sentences.zh: 其子質奉行焉。

translations.literal: His son Zhi carried this out.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi obeyed.

sentences.zh: 質博學有才藝，位諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Zhi was broadly learned and talented in the arts, and reached the post of Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was learned and gifted, rising to Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 烈弟僧皓，字山容，曆涉群書，工于談說，有名於當世。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Senghao, style Shanrong, ranged through many books and was skilled at discourse, with a name in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's brother Senghao, style Shanrong, read widely and excelled at talk; he was known in his day.

sentences.zh: 以諫議大夫、國子博士、散騎侍郎徵，並不起，世號徵君焉。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Remonstrating Censor, Erudite of the National University, and Gentleman of the Palace Cadency, but never accepted; the age called him the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as censor, university erudite, and palace gentleman, he never took office; the world called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 好營產業，孜孜不已，藏鏹巨萬，他資稱是。

translations.literal: He loved building up estates and worked at it tirelessly; he hoarded cash by the tens of thousands, with other assets to match.
translations.idiomatic: He loved amassing property and never stopped; his cash ran to tens of thousands, his other holdings likewise.

sentences.zh: 兄弟自供儉約，車馬瘦弊，身服布裳，而婢妾紈綺。

translations.literal: The brothers kept their own living spare: horses and carriages lean and worn, they themselves in cloth robes, while maidservants and concubines wore silk brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived plainly—thin horses, coarse carts, cotton robes on their own backs—while their maids and concubines wore brocade.

sentences.zh: 僧皓尤好蒲弈，戲不擇人，是以獲譏於世。

translations.literal: Senghao especially loved playing liubo and would play with anyone at all, for which he was mocked in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Senghao loved liubo above all and would play with anyone, which earned him ridicule.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝時，崔祖螭舉兵攻東陽城，僧皓與同事，事敗，死於獄中。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Jiemin, Cui Zuchi raised troops and attacked Dongyang city; Senghao joined the plot, which failed, and he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin, Cui Zuchi attacked Dongyang; Senghao joined him, the plot failed, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 李叔彪，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Li Shubiao was a man of Mao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shubiao came from Mao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 從祖金，神蒨中，與高允俱徵，位征南從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Jin, in the Shenrui era, was summoned together with Gao Yun and reached the post of Staff Officer to the Campaign South.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Jin, in Shenrui, was summoned with Gao Yun and rose to Staff Officer on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 叔彪好學博聞，有識度，為鄉閭所稱。

translations.literal: Shubiao loved learning and was widely informed, with judgment and insight, and was praised in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Shubiao loved learning, knew a great deal, and had judgment; his neighbors praised him.

sentences.zh: 太和中，拜中書博士，與清河崔亮、河間邢巒並相親友。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat and became close friends with Cui Liang of Qinghe and Xing Luan of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he became Secretariat Erudite and befriended Cui Liang of Qinghe and Xing Luan of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 三遷國子博士、本國中正，攝樂陵中正。

translations.literal: After three promotions he was Erudite of the National University and Rectifier of his native commandery, and also acted as Rectifier of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted thrice, he was university erudite and native commandery rectifier, and also acted as rectifier of Leling.

sentences.zh: 性清直，甚有公平之稱。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and upright, and he had a strong reputation for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Upright by nature, he was known for fairness.

sentences.zh: 曆中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍以其器操重之。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Prince Gaoyang Yong, held his talent and integrity in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Gaoyang Yong valued his character and ability.

sentences.zh: 尋除假節，行華州事，為吏人所稱。

translations.literal: Soon he was given provisional credentials and acted as Governor of Huazhou; officials and people praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given provisional credentials to govern Huazhou, to the praise of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南青州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of South Qingzhou, posthumous name Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of South Qingzhou, posthumous name Mu.

sentences.zh: 叔彪子述，字道興，有學識，州舉秀才，拜太常博士。

translations.literal: Shubiao's son Shu, style Daoxing, was learned and knowledgeable; the province recommended him as xiucai and he was appointed Erudite of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shu, style Daoxing, was learned; the province recommended him as xiucai and he became Grand Sacrifices Erudite.

sentences.zh: 使詣長安冊祭燕宣王廟。

translations.literal: He was sent to Chang'an to perform the investiture sacrifice at the temple of Prince Xuanyan of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Chang'an to perform the investiture rites at Prince Xuanyan of Yan's temple.

sentences.zh: 還，除儀曹郎，賜爵蓚縣男。

translations.literal: On his return he was made Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau and enfeoffed as Baron of Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he was made Gentleman of the Ceremonial Bureau and enfeoffed Baron of Mao.

sentences.zh: 稍遷興平太守。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Governor of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子象，字孟則，清簡有風概，博涉群書。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, style Mengze, was pure and restrained in bearing, with breadth in many books.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang, style Mengze, was spare in manner and widely read.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，稍遷中書侍郎、光祿大夫，兼散騎常侍，使梁。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was gradually promoted to Secretariat Gentleman, Grand Master for the Splendor of State, and concurrently Gentleman of the Palace Cadency, and was sent as envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title, rose to Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Master for the Splendor of State, served concurrently as Palace Cadency Gentleman, and went as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈驃騎大將軍、儀同三司，冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously General of Agile Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 象從容風素，有名于時，喪妻無子，終竟不娶，論者非之。

translations.literal: Xiang was easy in manner and pure in style, with a name in his time; he lost his wife and had no son, and to the end never remarried—commentators criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was graceful and known in his day; widowed and childless, he never remarried—to the disapproval of critics.

sentences.zh: 路恃慶，字伯瑞，陽平清泉人也。

translations.literal: Lu Shiqing, style Borui, was a man of Qingquan in Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shiqing, style Borui, came from Qingquan in Yangping.

sentences.zh: 祖綽，陽平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chuo was Governor of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chuo was Governor of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 恃慶有幹用，與廣平宋翻俱知名，為鄉閭所稱。

translations.literal: Shiqing had practical ability and, together with Song Fan of Guangping, was well known and praised in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqing was capable and, with Song Fan of Guangping, enjoyed local renown.

sentences.zh: 太和中，除奉朝請，恃慶以從兄文舉有才望，因推讓之，孝文遂並拜焉。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was made Court Gentleman for Attendance; Shiqing, because his cousin Wenju had talent and standing, yielded the place to him, and Emperor Xiaowen appointed them both.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he was made Court Gentleman; seeing his cousin Wenju's greater talent, he yielded the post, and Xiaowen appointed them both.

sentences.zh: 累遷定州河間王琛長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Chief Clerk to Prince Hejian of Dingzhou, Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Chief Clerk to Prince Hejian Chen of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 琛貪暴肆意，恃慶每進苦言。

translations.literal: Chen was greedy and violent at will; Shiqing often offered bitter remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was greedy and brutal; Shiqing often spoke harsh truth to him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左將軍、安州刺史，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made General of the Left, Governor of Anzhou, posthumous name Xiang.
