translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously General of the Left and Governor of Anzhou, posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子祖璧，給事中。

translations.literal: His son Zubi was a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zubi served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 恃慶弟仲信、思令，並有令名官位。

translations.literal: Shiqing's younger brothers Zhongxin and Siling both had fine reputations and official standing.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Zhongxin and Siling also won good names and offices.

sentences.zh: 房亮，字景高，清河人也。

translations.literal: Fang Liang, style Jinggao, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Liang, style Jinggao, came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父法延，譙郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Fayán was Governor of Qiao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fayán was Governor of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 亮好學有節操。

translations.literal: Liang loved learning and had moral discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Liang loved learning and held to principle.

sentences.zh: 太和中，舉秀才，為奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was recommended as xiucai and made Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he was recommended as xiucai and made Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後兼員外常侍，使高麗。

translations.literal: Later he served concurrently as Extraordinary Attendant and was sent as envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Extraordinary Attendant and went as envoy to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 高麗王托疾不拜。

translations.literal: The king of Goguryeo pleaded illness and did not perform the bow of ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo king claimed illness and refused the ceremonial bow.

sentences.zh: 以亮辱命，坐白衣守郎中。

translations.literal: Because Liang had disgraced his commission, he was demoted to commoner status and kept on as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was judged to have failed his mission and was reduced to commoner rank while retained as a writing-office gentleman.

sentences.zh: 曆濟北、平原二郡太守，以清嚴稱。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Governor of Jibei and Pingyuan, renowned for purity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Jibei and Pingyuan in turn, known for stern integrity.

sentences.zh: 後為東荊州刺史，亮留心撫納，夷夏安之。

translations.literal: Later he became Governor of East Jingzhou; Liang gave his heart to comforting and winning people, and Yi and Han were at peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Governor of East Jingzhou; he governed with care, and both barbarians and Chinese were at ease.

sentences.zh: 時邊州刺史例得一子出身，亮不言其子而啟弟子起為奉朝請，議者稱之。

translations.literal: At the time frontier governors by precedent could obtain a son's entry into office; Liang did not name his own son but memorialized that his nephew Qi should be made Court Gentleman for Attendance—commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier governors could usually secure office for a son; Liang did not ask for his own son but recommended his nephew Qi as Court Gentleman, which critics praised.

sentences.zh: 卒于光祿大夫，贈撫軍將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while Grand Master for the Splendor of State and was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Grand Master for the Splendor of State and was posthumously General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟詮、悅等，並歷位清顯。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Quan, Yue, and others all reached clear and eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Quan, Yue, and others all rose to distinguished office.

sentences.zh: 曹世表，字景升，魏大司馬休九世孫也。

translations.literal: Cao Shibiao, style Jingsheng, was the ninth-generation descendant of the Wei Grand Marshal Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Shibiao, style Jingsheng, was ninth in descent from Wei Grand Marshal Xiu.

sentences.zh: 祖謨，父慶，並有學問。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mo and father Qing both had learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mo and father Qing were both scholars.

sentences.zh: 世表性雅正，工尺牘，涉獵群書。

translations.literal: Shibiao's nature was refined and upright; he was skilled at letters and ranged through many books.
translations.idiomatic: Shibiao was refined and upright, skilled at correspondence, and widely read.

sentences.zh: 為司徒記室，與武威賈思伯、范陽盧同、隴西辛雄並相友善。

translations.literal: He was Recorder in the office of the Minister of Education and was on friendly terms with Jia Sibo of Wuwei, Lu Tong of Fanyang, and Xin Xiong of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: As Recorder to the Minister of Education he befriended Jia Sibo of Wuwei, Lu Tong of Fanyang, and Xin Xiong of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光，鄉里貴達，每稱美之。

translations.literal: Cui Guang, Attendant-in-Chief, was a man of standing in their home district and often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant-in-Chief Cui Guang, a local dignitary, often praised him.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，除清河太守，臨官省約，百姓安之。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era he was made Governor of Qinghe; in office he was sparing and restrained, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang he became Governor of Qinghe, governing frugally so the people were content.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，為尚書左丞，出行東豫州刺史，遷東南道行台。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, went out as acting Governor of East Yuzhou, and was transferred to Commissioner on the Southeastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaochang he was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then acting Governor of East Yuzhou, then Southeastern Circuit Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 潘永基，字紹業，長樂廣宗人也。

translations.literal: Pan Yongji, style Shaoye, was a man of Guangzong in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yongji, style Shaoye, came from Guangzong in Changle.

sentences.zh: 父靈乾，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Lingqian was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingqian was Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永基性通率，輕財好施。

translations.literal: Yongji's nature was open and direct; he was light with wealth and generous in giving.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji was frank by nature, careless of money, and generous.

sentences.zh: 為長樂太守。

translations.literal: He was made Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Changle.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮攻信都，永基與刺史元孚同心防捍。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong attacked Xindu; Yongji and the Inspector Yuan Fu were of one heart in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Ge Rong attacked Xindu, Yongji and Inspector Yuan Fu stood shoulder to shoulder in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 力窮城陷，榮欲害孚，永基請以身代孚死。

translations.literal: Strength exhausted, the city fell; Rong wished to kill Fu, and Yongji asked to die in Fu's place with his own body.
translations.idiomatic: When strength failed and the city fell, Rong meant to kill Fu; Yongji pleaded to die in his stead.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，除潁川太守，遷東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an he was made Governor of Yingchuan and transferred to Governor of East Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an he was appointed Governor of Yingchuan, then transferred to Governor of East Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，為車騎將軍、左光祿大夫，尋加衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was made Cavalry General and Left Grand Master for the Splendor of State, and soon after was additionally made Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi he became Cavalry General and Left Grand Master for the Splendor of State, and soon after Guard General as well.

sentences.zh: 復除東徐州刺史，前後在州，為吏人所愛。

translations.literal: He was again made Governor of East Xuzhou; in his terms before and after at the province, officials and commoners loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Governor of East Xuzhou, and in both stints there officials and people alike held him dear.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射、司徒公、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Masses, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Duke of the Masses, and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 子子義、子智。

translations.literal: His sons were Ziyi and Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ziyi and Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 子義學涉有父風，仕隨，至尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Ziyi in learning ranged widely and had his father's manner; he served Sui and reached Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was widely learned in his father's vein, entered Sui service, and rose to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 硃元旭，字君升，本樂陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Yuanxu, style Junsheng, was originally a man of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yuanxu, style Junsheng, was originally from Leling.

sentences.zh: 頗涉子史，開解几案。

translations.literal: He ranged considerably through the masters and histories and was quick to grasp desk affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had read widely in the classics and histories and was sharp at administrative work.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書度支郎中。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Bureau Director of Revenue in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Bureau Director of Revenue in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 神龜末，以郎選不精，大加沙汰。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengui era, because selection of gentlemen was not exacting, a great winnowing was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengui, because court gentleman selection had grown lax, a sweeping purge was ordered.

sentences.zh: 元旭與隴西辛雄、范陽祖瑩、太山羊深、西平源子恭並以才用見留。

translations.literal: Yuanxu, together with Xin Xiong of Longxi, Zu Ying of Fanyang, Yang Shen of Taishan, and Yuan Zigong of Xiping, were all retained for talent and usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxu was kept, along with Xin Xiong of Longxi, Zu Ying of Fanyang, Yang Shen of Taishan, and Yuan Zigong of Xiping, for proven talent.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書右丞，仍郎中、本州中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, while still holding the bureau director post and serving as Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, while retaining his bureau post and serving as Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 時關西都督蕭寶夤啟雲所統十萬，食唯一月。

translations.literal: At that time the Guanxi Commissioner Xiao Baoyao reported that the hundred thousand men under his command had provisions for only one month.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guanxi Commissioner Xiao Baoyao reported that his hundred thousand troops had barely a month's rations.

sentences.zh: 明帝大怒，詔問所由，錄、令已下皆推罪元旭。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was greatly angered and ordered an inquiry into the cause; from the Secretariat and Chancellery heads downward all shifted blame onto Yuanxu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming flew into a rage and demanded an accounting; from the Secretariat and Chancellery heads on down, all laid the blame on Yuanxu.

sentences.zh: 入見御坐前，屈指校計，寶夤兵糧乃逾一年，事乃得釋。

translations.literal: He entered and appeared before the imperial seat, counted on his fingers and checked the reckoning, and Baoyao's army grain turned out to exceed a year—the matter was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the throne, he reckoned on his fingers and showed Baoyao's stores would last more than a year, and the affair was dropped.

sentences.zh: 後遷衛將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Guard General and Left Grand Master for the Splendor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Guard General and Left Grand Master for the Splendor of State.

sentences.zh: 天平中，復拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he was again appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 既無風操，俛仰隨俗，性多機數，自容而已。

translations.literal: He had no moral bearing, bowed and looked up with the times, and his nature held many schemes—he merely accommodated himself.
translations.idiomatic: He lacked moral backbone, bent with every fashion, and lived by stratagem—nothing more than self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷分汲郡河內二界挾河之地立義州，置關西歸款戶，除元旭義州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: At that time the court divided the river-flanked lands on the border of Ji and Henei commanderies to establish Yizhou, settled households from Guanxi who had submitted, made Yuanxu Governor of Yizhou, and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The court then carved out riverine borderlands between Ji and Henei commanderies as Yizhou, settled surrendered households from Guanxi there, appointed Yuanxu its governor, and he died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：壽春形勝，南鄭要險，乃建鄴之肩髀，成都之喉嗌。

translations.literal: Commentary: Shouchun's terrain was strategically strong; Nanzheng was a vital pass—they were the shoulder and thigh of Jiankang, the throat of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Shouchun held commanding ground and Nanzheng guarded a critical pass—the shoulder and thigh of Jiankang, the throat of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 裴叔業、夏侯道遷體運知機，翻然鵲起，舉地而來，功誠兩茂，其以大啟茅賦，兼列旄ＣＭ，固其宜矣。

translations.literal: Pei Shuye and Xiahou Daoqian sensed the turn of fortune and knew the moment; like the magpie they rose in a sudden flight, bringing their territories when they came—merit and loyalty both flourished. That they should greatly open feudal estates and also be arrayed with ceremonial axes and regalia was indeed fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuye and Xiahou Daoqian read the times and seized their moment; they rose like startled magpies, surrendering whole territories with both merit and loyalty in full flower. Great enfeoffments and the full trappings of command were only their due.

sentences.zh: 植不恆其德，器小志大，斯所以顛覆也。

translations.literal: Zhi did not keep his virtue constant; his vessel was small but his aims were large—this is why he was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi could not hold his virtue steady—small in capacity, vast in ambition—and that is why he fell.

sentences.zh: 衍才行將略，不遂其終，惜哉！

translations.literal: Yan's conduct and talent, his generalship and strategy, did not reach their end—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yan had talent, bearing, and military gifts, yet never saw their fulfillment—a pity!

sentences.zh: 李、席、王、江雖復因人成事，亦為果決之士。

translations.literal: Li, Xi, Wang, and Jiang, though they again accomplished things by following others, were also men of resolute decision.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xi, Wang, and Jiang rode others' momentum to success, yet they too were men of bold resolve.

sentences.zh: 淳于誕好立功名，有志竟不遂也。

translations.literal: Chunyu Dan loved to establish fame and merit, yet his will in the end was not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyu Dan hungered for fame and achievement, but his ambitions never came to pass.

sentences.zh: 文秀不回，有死節之氣，非直身蒙嘉禮，遂乃子免刑戮，在我欲其罵人，忠義可不勉也？

translations.literal: Wenxiu did not bend back; he had the spirit to die for principle. It was not only that he personally received honored rites—even his son was spared punishment and execution. As for me, I would wish him to revile the enemy; can loyalty and righteousness not be encouraged?
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu would not yield and bore the air of a man ready to die for principle. He won not only posthumous honors but even exemption for his son from punishment. In his place I would have wished him to curse the foe outright—how can loyalty and righteousness fail to inspire?

sentences.zh: 張讜觀機委質，篤恤流離，亦仁智矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Dang observed the moment and entrusted himself; he was earnest in pity for the displaced—this too was benevolence and wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dang read the moment and offered his allegiance, showing deep compassion for the displaced—true benevolence and wisdom.

sentences.zh: 李苗以文武幹局，沉毅過人，臨難慨然，奮斯大節，蹈忠履義，沒而後已，仁必有勇，其斯人之謂乎！

translations.literal: Li Miao, with civil and military capacity and administrative grasp, was more deep and resolute than others; facing hardship he was stirred and roused to this great constancy, treading loyalty and walking righteousness until after death he ceased—benevolence must have courage: is this not what such a man means!
translations.idiomatic: Li Miao united civil and military talent with a steadiness beyond ordinary men; in peril he roused himself to the highest constancy, walking loyalty and righteousness to the grave. The benevolent must also be brave—was he not exactly that?

sentences.zh: 劉藻、傅永，豎眼文武器幹，知名于時。

translations.literal: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, and Shuyan—for civil and military arms and administrative grasp—were famed in their time.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao, Fu Yong, and Shuyan were famed in their day for literary and martial gifts and administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 豎眼加以撫邊導俗，風化尤美，方之二子，固已優乎，抑又魏世良牧。

translations.literal: Shuyan, with the addition of pacifying the frontier and guiding custom, had especially fine transformation by instruction; compared with the two sons he was surely superior, and moreover was a fine governor of the Wei age.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyan went further, pacifying the frontier and guiding the people to an exemplary civility; set beside the other two he was plainly their better, and among the Wei age's finest governors.

sentences.zh: 張烈早有氣尚，名輩見知，趣舍沉浮，俱至顯達，雅道正路，其殆病諸。

translations.literal: Zhang Lie early had spirited integrity and was known to men of reputation; in choice and rejection they drifted with the tide, yet all reached eminence—the refined way and the upright path: are these perhaps what ailed them?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lie early showed force of character and won notice among his peers; yet in the rise and fall of fortune they all bobbed with the current to high rank—the refined way and the straight path seem to have been just what troubled them.

sentences.zh: 李、路器尚所及，俱可觀者。

translations.literal: Li and Lu in capacity and integrity reached what they could; both were worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Lu achieved what their talents allowed; both are worth regard.

sentences.zh: 象風彩詞涉，亦當年之俊乂。

translations.literal: Xiang in bearing, elegance, and literary range was also an outstanding man of that age.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's grace, eloquence, and learning made him another leading light of the day.

sentences.zh: 房亮、曹世表、潘永基、硃元旭拔萃從官，咸享名器，各有由也。

translations.literal: Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, and Zhu Yuanxu stood out among attendant officials; all enjoyed famous offices and vessels of rank—each had his reason.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Liang, Cao Shibiao, Pan Yongji, and Zhu Yuanxu rose above the ranks of court servitors, each winning honored office for reasons of his own.
